// DXT1 (BC1) blocks rewritten as ASTC 4x4 blocks, for a GPU without texture-compression-bc that has ASTC (Apple's:
// iPhones, iPads).  Unpacked to BGRA8 (dxt.ts) a DXT1 texture takes 8x its size; as ASTC 4x4 it takes 2x, and a
// phone's memory is what runs out (free roam: 159 MB of opaque DXT1 unpacked, ~40 MB as ASTC).
//
// A DXT1 block is two RGB565 colours and a 2-bit index per texel.  ASTC can say the same in one partition: colour
// endpoint mode 8 (LDR RGB direct) at 8 bits a value keeps both colours exactly (expanded to 8 bits as BC1 does), and
// the weights pick the points between them:
//   four colours (c0 > c1): weights of 2 bits, 0 21 43 64 of 64, against BC1's thirds: at most 1.3 of 255 off;
//   three colours (c0 <= c1): trit weights, 0 32 64 of 64: the midpoint exactly.
// The fourth index of a three-colour block is transparent black, which one plane cannot give: such a block goes into
// a texture unpacked instead (dxt1HasPunch, the encoder's choice at a texture's first upload), or, met in a later
// level of a texture already ASTC, into a dual-plane block (endpoint mode 12, RGBA at 7 bits, alpha its own plane):
// the alpha is right, the colour under a transparent texel the darker endpoint, not black.
//
// Layout (Khronos Data Format spec, ASTC): bits 0-10 the block mode, 11-12 partitions - 1, 13-16 the endpoint mode,
// then the endpoint values from bit 17 up; the weights from bit 127 down (bit i of their sequence at bit 127 - i), a
// dual-plane block's colour component selector just below them.
//   0x042: a 4x4 grid of 2-bit weights, one plane          0x051: a 4x4 grid of trit weights, one plane
//   0x451: 0x051 with two planes (32 weights, interleaved: plane 0 then plane 1 for each texel)
// The endpoint range is not stored: the decoder takes the largest whose values fit in the bits the weights leave
// (8 bits for 6 values in both one-plane modes; 7 bits for the 8 of the dual-plane one: 128 - 17 - 2 - 52 = 57).
import { C5, C6 } from './dxt';

/** trit quintuples (t0 + 3 t1 + 9 t2 + 27 t3 + 81 t4) to their 8-bit packing, from the spec's decoding */
const TRITS = new Uint8Array(243);
{
  const seen = new Uint8Array(243);
  for (let T = 255; T >= 0; T--) {         // downwards: the smallest packing wins (a short last group needs it)
    const b = (i: number, n = 1) => (T >> i) & ((1 << n) - 1);
    let C: number, t3: number, t4: number;
    if (b(2, 3) === 7) { C = b(5, 3) << 2 | b(0, 2); t4 = 2; t3 = 2; }
    else { C = b(0, 5); if (b(5, 2) === 3) { t4 = 2; t3 = b(7); } else { t4 = b(7); t3 = b(5, 2); } }
    let t0: number, t1: number, t2: number;
    const c = (i: number, n = 1) => (C >> i) & ((1 << n) - 1);
    if (c(0, 2) === 3) { t2 = 2; t1 = c(4); t0 = c(3) << 1 | (c(2) & ~c(3) & 1); }
    else if (c(2, 2) === 3) { t2 = 2; t1 = 2; t0 = c(0, 2); }
    else { t2 = c(4); t1 = c(2, 2); t0 = c(1) << 1 | (c(0) & ~c(1) & 1); }
    const k = t0 + 3 * t1 + 9 * t2 + 27 * t3 + 81 * t4;
    TRITS[k] = T; seen[k] = 1;
  }
  if (seen.indexOf(0) >= 0) throw new Error('astc: trit table incomplete');
}

// a block being built: four 32-bit words, low bits first
const blk = new Uint32Array(4), wts = new Uint8Array(32);
function put(pos: number, n: number, v: number) {
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++, pos++) if ((v >>> i) & 1) blk[pos >> 5] |= 1 << (pos & 31);
}
/** the weights' bits from the top down: 2 bits each, or trits packed 5 to 8 bits (a short last group, its bits only) */
function putWeights(n: number, trits: boolean) {
  let pos = 127;
  const top = (v: number, bits: number) => { for (let i = 0; i < bits; i++, pos--) if ((v >> i) & 1) blk[pos >> 5] |= 1 << (pos & 31); };
  if (!trits) { for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) top(wts[i], 2); return pos; }
  for (let g = 0; g < n; g += 5) {
    const t = (i: number) => g + i < n ? wts[g + i] : 0;
    const k = t(0) + 3 * t(1) + 9 * t(2) + 27 * t(3) + 81 * t(4);
    top(TRITS[k], [0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8][Math.min(5, n - g)]);
  }
  return pos;
}

function rev32(x: number): number {
  x = (x >>> 1 & 0x55555555) | (x & 0x55555555) << 1;
  x = (x >>> 2 & 0x33333333) | (x & 0x33333333) << 2;
  x = (x >>> 4 & 0x0F0F0F0F) | (x & 0x0F0F0F0F) << 4;
  x = (x >>> 8 & 0x00FF00FF) | (x & 0x00FF00FF) << 8;
  return x >>> 16 | x << 16;
}

/** whether any block of a DXT1 level (bw x bh blocks, pitch bytes a row of blocks) has a transparent texel */
export function dxt1HasPunch(src: Uint8Array, off: number, pitch: number, bw: number, bh: number): boolean {
  for (let by = 0; by < bh; by++) {
    for (let bx = 0; bx < bw; bx++) {
      const b = off + by * pitch + bx * 8;
      if ((src[b] | src[b + 1] << 8) > (src[b + 2] | src[b + 3] << 8)) continue;
      const idx = (src[b + 4] | src[b + 5] << 8 | src[b + 6] << 16 | src[b + 7] << 24) >>> 0;
      // a 2-bit index 3: both bits set
      if ((idx & (idx >>> 1) & 0x55555555) !== 0) return true;
    }
  }
  return false;
}

const W3 = [0, 2, 1, 0];   // a three-colour block's codes to trit weights: c0 = 0, c1 = 2, the midpoint 1
/** an 8-bit value at 7 bits, as the decoder unquantizes it (v << 1 | v >> 6) */
const q7 = (c: number) => (c & ~1) | (c >> 7);

/** One DXT1 level (bw x bh blocks, pitch bytes a row of blocks) as ASTC 4x4 blocks, 16 bytes each, bw * 16 bytes a
 *  row; into the start of `into` when that has room, else into a new array.  punch counts the blocks that needed two
 *  planes (a transparent texel). */
export function dxt1ToAstc(src: Uint8Array, off: number, pitch: number, bw: number, bh: number, into?: Uint8Array,
  punch?: { blocks: number }): Uint8Array {
  const n = bw * bh * 16, out = into && into.length >= n ? into.subarray(0, n) : new Uint8Array(n);
  const o32 = new Uint32Array(out.buffer, out.byteOffset, n >> 2);
  for (let by = 0; by < bh; by++) {
    for (let bx = 0; bx < bw; bx++) {
      const b = off + by * pitch + bx * 8;
      const c0 = src[b] | src[b + 1] << 8, c1 = src[b + 2] | src[b + 3] << 8;
      const idx = (src[b + 4] | src[b + 5] << 8 | src[b + 6] << 16 | src[b + 7] << 24) >>> 0;
      let r0 = C5[c0 >> 11], g0 = C6[(c0 >> 5) & 63], b0 = C5[c0 & 31];
      let r1 = C5[c1 >> 11], g1 = C6[(c1 >> 5) & 63], b1 = C5[c1 & 31];
      const four = c0 > c1, holes = !four && (idx & (idx >>> 1) & 0x55555555) !== 0;
      // a dual-plane block's endpoints at 7 bits: the decoder compares (and gives) what they unquantize to
      if (holes) { r0 = q7(r0); g0 = q7(g0); b0 = q7(b0); r1 = q7(r1); g1 = q7(g1); b1 = q7(b1); }
      // the decoder wants the second endpoint's sum the larger (else it swaps them and blends blue in): swap here,
      // and turn the weights round
      const swap = r1 + g1 + b1 < r0 + g0 + b0;
      if (swap) { let x = r0; r0 = r1; r1 = x; x = g0; g0 = g1; g1 = x; x = b0; b0 = b1; b1 = x; }
      const o = (by * bw + bx) * 4;
      if (!holes) {
        // the weights' sequence, lowest bit first (at most 32 bits: the top word of the block, its bits reversed)
        let ws: number;
        if (four) {
          // codes 0 1 2 3 to weights 0 3 1 2, all 16 at once: high bit the code's low bit, low bit the two bits' xor
          const lo = idx & 0x55555555, hi = (idx >>> 1) & 0x55555555;
          ws = swap ? ~(lo << 1 | (lo ^ hi)) : lo << 1 | (lo ^ hi);
        } else {
          for (let i = 0; i < 16; i++) { const w = W3[(idx >>> 2 * i) & 3]; wts[i] = swap ? 2 - w : w; }
          const g = (i: number) => TRITS[wts[i] + 3 * wts[i + 1] + 9 * wts[i + 2] + 27 * wts[i + 3] + 81 * wts[i + 4]];
          ws = g(0) | g(5) << 8 | g(10) << 16 | TRITS[wts[15]] << 24;
        }
        // block mode, one partition, endpoint mode 8, then r0 r1 g0 g1 b0 b1 at 8 bits from bit 17
        o32[o] = (four ? 0x042 : 0x051) | 8 << 13 | r0 << 17 | r1 << 25;
        o32[o + 1] = r1 >> 7 | g0 << 1 | g1 << 9 | b0 << 17 | b1 << 25;
        o32[o + 2] = b1 >> 7;
        o32[o + 3] = rev32(ws);
        continue;
      }
      // alpha 255 at the first endpoint, 0 at the second; a transparent texel takes the first's colour (the darker)
      blk.fill(0);
      for (let i = 0; i < 16; i++) {
        const k = (idx >>> 2 * i) & 3, w = W3[k];
        wts[2 * i] = k === 3 ? 0 : swap ? 2 - w : w;
        wts[2 * i + 1] = k === 3 ? 2 : 0;
      }
      put(0, 11, 0x451); put(13, 4, 12);
      const v = [r0, r1, g0, g1, b0, b1, 255, 0];
      for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) put(17 + 7 * i, 7, v[i] >> 1);   // q7 values: >> 1 is their 7 bits
      const below = putWeights(32, true);
      put(below - 1, 2, 3);                  // the second plane is alpha
      if (punch) punch.blocks++;
      o32[o] = blk[0]; o32[o + 1] = blk[1]; o32[o + 2] = blk[2]; o32[o + 3] = blk[3];
    }
  }
  return out;
}

// DXT1/3/5 (BC1/2/3) unpacked to BGRA8 on the CPU, for a GPU without
// texture-compression-bc (PowerVR and Mali phones).  The blocks decode as
// WebGPU's bc1/bc2/bc3 formats define them (the D3D10 rules): DXT3 and DXT5
// colour blocks always have four colours; a DXT1 block with c0 <= c1 has three
// and a transparent black.  Unpacked, a texture takes 8x (DXT1) or 4x (DXT3/5)
// the GPU memory: the textures of a Quick Race, 30 MB packed, become 210 MB.
import * as P from './proto';

/** 5- and 6-bit colour values expanded to 8 bits (bit replication, as WebGPU's bc formats do; astc.ts too) */
export const C5 = new Uint8Array(32), C6 = new Uint8Array(64);
for (let i = 0; i < 32; i++) C5[i] = (i << 3) | (i >> 2);
for (let i = 0; i < 64; i++) C6[i] = (i << 2) | (i >> 4);
const pal = new Uint32Array(4), alpha = new Uint8Array(16), at = new Uint8Array(8);

/** One mip level of w x h texels (pitch = bytes per row of 4x4 blocks) as BGRA8, w * 4 bytes per row; into the start
 *  of `into` when that has room (every texel is written), else into a new array. */
export function unpackDxt(fmt: number, src: Uint8Array, off: number, pitch: number, w: number, h: number, into?: Uint8Array): Uint8Array {
  const n = w * h * 4, out = into && into.length >= n ? into.subarray(0, n) : new Uint8Array(n), o32 = new Uint32Array(out.buffer, out.byteOffset, w * h);
  const dxt1 = fmt === P.Fmt.DXT1, dxt5 = fmt === P.Fmt.DXT5, bsz = dxt1 ? 8 : 16, co = dxt1 ? 0 : 8;
  const bw = (w + 3) >> 2, bh = (h + 3) >> 2;
  for (let by = 0; by < bh; by++) {
    for (let bx = 0; bx < bw; bx++) {
      const b = off + by * pitch + bx * bsz;
      if (dxt5) {
        // two alpha endpoints, then 16 3-bit codes: 8 levels, or 6 levels plus 0 and 255
        const a0 = src[b], a1 = src[b + 1];
        at[0] = a0; at[1] = a1;
        if (a0 > a1) for (let i = 1; i < 7; i++) at[i + 1] = ((7 - i) * a0 + i * a1) / 7 | 0;
        else { for (let i = 1; i < 5; i++) at[i + 1] = ((5 - i) * a0 + i * a1) / 5 | 0; at[6] = 0; at[7] = 255; }
        const lo = src[b + 2] | src[b + 3] << 8 | src[b + 4] << 16, hi = src[b + 5] | src[b + 6] << 8 | src[b + 7] << 16;
        for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) { alpha[i] = at[(lo >> 3 * i) & 7]; alpha[i + 8] = at[(hi >> 3 * i) & 7]; }
      } else if (!dxt1) {
        // 16 explicit 4-bit alphas
        for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) { const v = src[b + i]; alpha[2 * i] = (v & 15) * 17; alpha[2 * i + 1] = (v >> 4) * 17; }
      }
      const c0 = src[b + co] | src[b + co + 1] << 8, c1 = src[b + co + 2] | src[b + co + 3] << 8;
      const r0 = C5[c0 >> 11], g0 = C6[(c0 >> 5) & 63], b0 = C5[c0 & 31];
      const r1 = C5[c1 >> 11], g1 = C6[(c1 >> 5) & 63], b1 = C5[c1 & 31];
      pal[0] = (b0 | g0 << 8 | r0 << 16 | 0xFF000000) >>> 0;
      pal[1] = (b1 | g1 << 8 | r1 << 16 | 0xFF000000) >>> 0;
      if (!dxt1 || c0 > c1) {
        pal[2] = ((2 * b0 + b1) / 3 | (2 * g0 + g1) / 3 << 8 | (2 * r0 + r1) / 3 << 16 | 0xFF000000) >>> 0;
        pal[3] = ((b0 + 2 * b1) / 3 | (g0 + 2 * g1) / 3 << 8 | (r0 + 2 * r1) / 3 << 16 | 0xFF000000) >>> 0;
      } else {
        pal[2] = ((b0 + b1) >> 1 | (g0 + g1) >> 1 << 8 | (r0 + r1) >> 1 << 16 | 0xFF000000) >>> 0;
        pal[3] = 0;
      }
      const idx = (src[b + co + 4] | src[b + co + 5] << 8 | src[b + co + 6] << 16 | src[b + co + 7] << 24) >>> 0;
      // an edge block, or a level smaller than a block (2x2, 1x1): only the texels inside
      const ph = Math.min(4, h - by * 4), pw = Math.min(4, w - bx * 4);
      for (let py = 0; py < ph; py++) {
        const row = (by * 4 + py) * w + bx * 4;
        for (let px = 0; px < pw; px++) {
          const i = py * 4 + px, c = pal[(idx >>> 2 * i) & 3];
          o32[row + px] = dxt1 ? c : ((c & 0xFFFFFF) | alpha[i] << 24) >>> 0;
        }
      }
    }
  }
  return out;
}

// The WebGPU encoder: applies the resource queue and turns a handed-off frame
// (runtime/web/gpu_web.c records) into render passes.  A port of the encode
// half of runtime/metal.m,
// reading the records zero-copy from the wasm memory.
//
// Semantics kept from the Mac port, on purpose (the reference screenshots come
// from it):
//   - the first pass of a target in a frame starts with a clear to the clear
//     colour (alpha 1), later passes load; a colour Clear only matters there;
//   - Z clears are deferred to the next pass that binds the Z surface;
//   - every Z surface is depth32float, created at the size of the first target
//     it is used with (the implicit one follows the screen); a size mismatch
//     binds a scratch depth and turns the Z test off;
//   - draw viewports follow Direct3D; a scissor also keeps the 2D UI in its
//     4:3 band on a screen narrower than 4:3 (GwDraw.clip);
//   - StretchRect: a copy when size and format match, else a scaled quad; from a
//     source rectangle (the cover shoot's picture) always a scaled quad, opaque from
//     the screen (the D3D back buffer has no alpha).
// Deliberate differences: the clear colour is the frame's own (Clear records
// in stream order) rather than a global read at encode time; scaled blits do
// not blend; draws into a texture that no longer exists are dropped (the Mac
// drew them on the screen).
import * as P from './proto';
import { D, F, Kind, Op } from './proto';
import { COPY, FF_FS, MS_RESOLVE, TONE, TVERT_VS } from './wgsl';
import { createShaderAbi, alphaFunc, PSCUBE, VSPAR_SIZE, KWIN_SIZE, PSPAR_SIZE, HLPAR_SIZE } from './shader-abi';
import { unpackDxt } from './dxt';
import { drawViewport, drawScissor } from './viewport';
import { dxt1HasPunch, dxt1ToAstc } from './astc';
import type { GameMemory } from '../host/memory';
import { HqSkins, type DataReader } from './hqskin';

export interface EncodeStats {
  draws: number; passes: number; skipped: number; encodeMs: number;
  /** the frame was drawn straight into the texture given to encodeFrame (no back buffer, no composite) */
  direct: boolean;
}

interface Tex {
  serial: number; tex: GPUTexture; fmt: number; w: number; h: number; levels: number; cube: boolean; rt: boolean;
  view: GPUTextureView;            // sampling view (2d, or cube)
  rtViews: GPUTextureView[];       // render target views: [0] = level 0 (2d) or faces 0..5 (cube)
  expandA8: boolean; bc: boolean;
  unpack: boolean;                 // DXT on a GPU without texture-compression-bc: BGRA8, unpacked on upload
  astc: boolean;                   // DXT1 on a GPU with ASTC but not BC: ASTC 4x4, rewritten on upload (astc.ts)
  filled: boolean;                 // a level has gone up (an ASTC texture's choice is made at its first upload)
  bytes: number;                   // its size on the GPU, every level and face
  face0?: GPUTextureView;          // a cube's face 0, level 0 as a 2D view (StretchRect from it), made at its first use
  ms?: MsTwin;                     // a render target made with TF_MS: its 4-sample twin (runtime/com.c MULTISAMPLING)
}

/** a 4-sample colour texture that a target's passes draw into and resolve from (runtime/com.c MULTISAMPLING); stale:
 *  the target was written another way (a blit, a copy, a clear pass of its own) since the twin last resolved into it */
interface MsTwin { tex: GPUTexture; view: GPUTextureView; stale: boolean }
/** HQ vinyls (hqskin.ts): skins painted again at 1024 shown at once, at most; the one drawn longest ago goes */
const OVER_MAX = 16;
/** a sampler key (encoder.sampler) with a mip filter: linear where it had none */
const overSmp = (k: number) => ((k >> 4) & 3) ? k : (k & ~(3 << 4)) | (2 << 4);

const enum Src { TVert = 0, Raw = 1, Pool = 2 }
const PSLOT = 768;                 // PSPar (560 bytes) at 256-aligned slots
const PSPAR_BYTES = PSPAR_SIZE;

/** FNV-1a of a shader's text: identifies a module across sessions */
function fnv(t: string): number {
  let h = 0x811c9dc5;
  for (let i = 0; i < t.length; i++) { h ^= t.charCodeAt(i); h = Math.imul(h, 0x01000193); }
  return h >>> 0;
}

const BLEND: GPUBlendFactor[] = ['one', 'zero', 'one', 'src', 'one-minus-src', 'src-alpha', 'one-minus-src-alpha', 'dst-alpha',
  'one-minus-dst-alpha', 'dst', 'one-minus-dst', 'src-alpha-saturated', 'src-alpha', 'one-minus-src-alpha', 'constant', 'one-minus-constant'];
const BLENDOP: GPUBlendOperation[] = ['add', 'add', 'subtract', 'reverse-subtract', 'min', 'max'];
const CMP: GPUCompareFunction[] = ['always', 'never', 'less', 'equal', 'less-equal', 'greater', 'not-equal', 'greater-equal', 'always'];
const ADDR: GPUAddressMode[] = ['repeat', 'repeat', 'mirror-repeat', 'clamp-to-edge', 'clamp-to-edge', 'mirror-repeat'];

export class Encoder {
  private regionClearPipes = new Map<string, GPURenderPipeline>();
  /** Attachment clears ignore viewports. A triangle clears only this player's
   * pixels and preserves the colour/depth belonging to the other players. */
  private regionClearPipe(flags: number, argb: number, z: number, ms = false): GPURenderPipeline {
    const key = `${flags & 3}:${argb}:${z}${ms ? ':x4' : ''}`;
    let pipe = this.regionClearPipes.get(key);
    if (pipe) return pipe;
    const rgba = [(argb >>> 16 & 255) / 255, (argb >>> 8 & 255) / 255, (argb & 255) / 255, (argb >>> 24) / 255];
    const module = this.device.createShaderModule({ label: 'split region clear', code: `
      @vertex fn vs(@builtin(vertex_index) i: u32) -> @builtin(position) vec4f {
        let xy = array<vec2f, 3>(vec2f(-1., -1.), vec2f(3., -1.), vec2f(-1., 3.));
        return vec4f(xy[i], ${z.toFixed(9)}, 1.);
      }
      @fragment fn fs() -> @location(0) vec4f { return vec4f(${rgba.map(v => v.toFixed(9)).join(',')}); }
    ` });
    pipe = this.device.createRenderPipeline({ label: 'split region clear', layout: 'auto',
      vertex: { module, entryPoint: 'vs' }, fragment: { module, entryPoint: 'fs', targets: [{ format: 'bgra8unorm', writeMask: flags & 1 ? 15 : 0 }] },
      primitive: { topology: 'triangle-list' },
      depthStencil: { format: 'depth32float', depthWriteEnabled: !!(flags & 2), depthCompare: 'always' },
      ...(ms ? { multisample: { count: 4 } } : {}),
    });
    this.regionClearPipes.set(key, pipe);
    return pipe;
  }
  readonly device: GPUDevice;
  private queue: GPUQueue;
  private memory: GameMemory;
  private sab!: SharedArrayBuffer;
  private u8!: Uint8Array; private u32!: Uint32Array; private i32!: Int32Array; private f32!: Float32Array;
  private ctlW: number;              // word index of GwCtl
  private log: (s: string) => void;
  private feat: { bc: boolean; astc: boolean; swizzle: boolean; unaligned: boolean };

  // resources
  private tex: (Tex | undefined)[] = [];
  // HQ vinyls: the 1024 skins shown in the game's skins' places (texFor), by the game's texture id; the latest paint
  // asked for each id (a newer one, the game painting it again or freeing it: an older paint is dropped)
  private hq: HqSkins | null = null;
  private over = new Map<number, Tex & { drawn: number }>();
  private hqWant = new Map<number, number>();
  private hqSeq = 0;
  private drawClock = 0;
  private serial = 1;
  private white!: Tex; private whiteCube!: Tex;
  private zTex: (GPUTexture | undefined)[] = [];
  private zView: (GPUTextureView | undefined)[] = [];
  private zpend = new Uint8Array(64); private zpendV = new Float32Array(64);
  private scratchZ = new Map<string, GPUTextureView>();
  private pool: GPUBuffer | null = null;

  private samplers = new Map<number, GPUSampler>();
  private pipes = new Map<number, GPURenderPipeline | null>();
  private bg1 = new Map<string, GPUBindGroup>();
  private destroyLater: { destroy(): void }[] = [];

  private tvBuf: GPUBuffer; private rawBuf: GPUBuffer; private kBuf: GPUBuffer; private pBuf: GPUBuffer;
  private bufGen = 0; private bg0: (GPUBindGroup | null)[] = [null, null, null]; private bg0Gen = -1;
  private pStage = new Float32Array(192 * 1024);
  // per-draw scratch, reused so that a draw allocates nothing: group 0's dynamic
  // offsets, and the group 1 tuple of the previous draw (cube, 4 texture serials,
  // 4 sampler keys; [0] = -1 when the pass has none bound yet)
  private dyn = new Uint32Array(3);
  private b1 = new Int32Array(9);

  private bgl0: GPUBindGroupLayout; private bgl1: GPUBindGroupLayout; private bgl1c: GPUBindGroupLayout;
  private pl2d: GPUPipelineLayout; private plCube: GPUPipelineLayout;
  private tvertMod: GPUShaderModule; private ffMod: GPUShaderModule; private ffCubeMod: GPUShaderModule;

    bgs: WeakMap<GPUTextureView, Map<GPUSampler, GPUBindGroup>> } | null = null;
  private toneArgs = new Float32Array(4);

  // back buffer (the game's device-size "screen"), and the texture the current frame
  // draws its screen into: the back buffer, or the canvas texture when sizes match
  bb: GPUTexture | null = null; private bbView: GPUTextureView | null = null;
  screen: GPUTexture | null = null; screenView: GPUTextureView | null = null;
  /** frames that copied from the screen before drawing to it (they keep the back buffer) */
  screenReadFirst = 0;
  // multisampling (runtime/com.c MULTISAMPLING: the game's Full Scene Anti-Aliasing): the back buffer with 4 samples
  // (Op.BbSamples) and a render target made with TF_MS each have a 4-sample twin; their passes draw into the twin, with
  // a 4-sample twin of their Z surface (by surface and size), and resolve into the screen or the texture at the pass's
  // end; a blit or copy into them leaves the twin behind (stale) until the next pass that loads draws the picture into it.
  // The resolve is a pass of ours (msResolve: the samples' average), not the GPU's own (a resolveTarget): the twin is
  // kept for the next pass that loads, and the GPU's resolve of a picture it also keeps failed on two computers'
  // graphics on 2026-11-08 (an AMD Ryzen 5600GT's Vega in Chrome and Edge: the GPU hung at the third frame, every game;
  // a Qualcomm Snapdragon laptop: the picture in scrambled tiles once frames had several passes on the screen)
  private bbSamples = 1;
  // msResolve's shader, layout, pipelines by format and bind groups by twin, made at its first use
  private msRes: { mod: GPUShaderModule; bgl: GPUBindGroupLayout; layout: GPUPipelineLayout; pipes: Map<string, GPURenderPipeline>;
    bgs: WeakMap<GPUTexture, GPUBindGroup> } | null = null;

  /** passes drawn at 4 samples (resolved at their end), pictures drawn into a twin again after a blit or copy */
  msPasses = 0; msRefreshes = 0;

  traceSeq = new Set<number>(); traceDumps = false; logShaders = false;
