// Photo mode's picture (runtime/photo.c, GwPhoto in runtime/web/gpu_proto.h).  While photo mode is on, every frame's
// back buffer goes into an average (rgba16float, the back buffer's size): a frame of a moving camera replaces it, and
// once the camera stands still the game draws each frame from a slightly different spot (within a pixel: smooth edges;
// the eye over a lens: the blur away from the focus), which add up, frame n weighing 1/n.  The canvas shows that
// average with the picture's look (photo mode's panel: exposure, filter, vignette) and the crop's preview (the rest
// dimmed, lines of thirds), and F12 keeps it: the same look at the picture's own size, the crop's rectangle of it, read
// back (index.ts).  The look is wgsl.ts PHOTO.  A picture bigger than the screen comes as tiles, each a still picture
// of its part of the view, read out as it is whole (shot() with the tile's place: the vignette is the whole picture's)
// while the canvas keeps showing the whole view as it was (hold()); a fisheye bends the picture round as it is shown
// and kept (the game draws it wider: GwPhoto's fov).
import { PHOTO } from './wgsl';

export const PH_OFF = 0, PH_LIVE = 1, PH_ADD = 2, PH_DONE = 3, PH_NOW = 4;
const LOOK_BYTES = 112;

/** a tile's place in the whole picture: its column and row of n a side */
export interface PhotoTile { x: number; y: number; n: number }
/** the fisheye: the field of view the frame was drawn with (degrees across), its width over its height */
export interface PhotoFisheye { fov: number; aspect: number }

/** the picture's look (app/photo.ts) */
export interface PhotoLook {
  exposure: number;                     // times
  contrast: number;                     // 1 as drawn
  saturation: number;                   // 1 as drawn, 0 grey
  tint: [number, number, number];       // times, per channel
  fade: number;                         // blacks lifted to this
  vignette: number;                     // the corners darker by this part
  crop: [number, number, number, number]; // the part kept: left, top, right, bottom (0 .. 1 of the picture)
  grid: boolean;                        // the preview's lines of thirds
}
export const PLAIN_LOOK: PhotoLook = {
  exposure: 1, contrast: 1, saturation: 1, tint: [1, 1, 1], fade: 0, vignette: 0, crop: [0, 0, 1, 1], grid: false,
};

export class PhotoPicture {
  private mod: GPUShaderModule;
  private bgl: GPUBindGroupLayout;
  private addPipe: GPURenderPipeline;
  private lookPipes = new Map<GPUTextureFormat, GPURenderPipeline>();
  private bufShow: GPUBuffer; private bufShot: GPUBuffer;
  private args = new Float32Array(LOOK_BYTES / 4);
  private acc: GPUTexture | null = null; private accView: GPUTextureView | null = null;
  private shotTex: GPUTexture | null = null; private shotView: GPUTextureView | null = null;
  private holdTex: GPUTexture | null = null; private holdView: GPUTextureView | null = null;
  /** the fisheye the picture is shown and kept with (null: as drawn) */
  fisheye: PhotoFisheye | null = null;
  private bgs = new WeakMap<GPUTextureView, Map<string, GPUBindGroup>>();
  /** the frames in the average */
  count = 0;
  /** the frames the still picture will have (0: the camera moves), from the game */
  target = 0;
  /** the average holds a whole still picture */
  done = false;

  constructor(private device: GPUDevice) {
    const d = device;
    this.mod = d.createShaderModule({ label: 'photo', code: PHOTO });
    this.bgl = d.createBindGroupLayout({ entries: [
      { binding: 0, visibility: GPUShaderStage.FRAGMENT, texture: { sampleType: 'float' } },
      { binding: 1, visibility: GPUShaderStage.FRAGMENT, sampler: { type: 'filtering' } },
      { binding: 2, visibility: GPUShaderStage.FRAGMENT, buffer: { type: 'uniform' } }] });
    const layout = d.createPipelineLayout({ bindGroupLayouts: [this.bgl] });
    // the new frame times the constant plus the average times one minus it: 1 replaces, 1/n adds the n-th
    const blend: GPUBlendComponent = { srcFactor: 'constant', dstFactor: 'one-minus-constant', operation: 'add' };
    this.addPipe = d.createRenderPipeline({ label: 'photo add', layout,
      vertex: { module: this.mod, entryPoint: 'vs_full' },
      fragment: { module: this.mod, entryPoint: 'fs_add', targets: [{ format: 'rgba16float', blend: { color: blend, alpha: blend } }] },
      primitive: { topology: 'triangle-list' } });
    this.bufShow = d.createBuffer({ label: 'photo look', size: LOOK_BYTES, usage: GPUBufferUsage.UNIFORM | GPUBufferUsage.COPY_DST });
    this.bufShot = d.createBuffer({ label: 'photo look (picture)', size: LOOK_BYTES, usage: GPUBufferUsage.UNIFORM | GPUBufferUsage.COPY_DST });
  }

  private bg(src: GPUTextureView, smp: GPUSampler, buf: GPUBuffer, key: string): GPUBindGroup {
    let m = this.bgs.get(src);
    if (!m) this.bgs.set(src, m = new Map());
    let g = m.get(key);
    if (!g) m.set(key, g = this.device.createBindGroup({ layout: this.bgl, entries: [
      { binding: 0, resource: src }, { binding: 1, resource: smp }, { binding: 2, resource: { buffer: buf } }] }));
    return g;
  }

  private lookPipe(format: GPUTextureFormat): GPURenderPipeline {
    let p = this.lookPipes.get(format);
    if (!p) this.lookPipes.set(format, p = this.device.createRenderPipeline({ label: `photo look ${format}`,
      layout: this.device.createPipelineLayout({ bindGroupLayouts: [this.bgl] }),
      vertex: { module: this.mod, entryPoint: 'vs_full' },
      fragment: { module: this.mod, entryPoint: 'fs_look', targets: [{ format }] },
      primitive: { topology: 'triangle-list' } }));
    return p;
  }

  /** still picture gen's frames in the average (for the game: GwPhoto ack) */
  gen = 0;

  /** a frame of photo mode: its back buffer (w x h) into the average, as the game's state says: a moving camera's
   *  replaces it; frame n of still picture gen adds to it when it is the next one (the game draws a frame again until
   *  it is in: frames the page skips never leave a gap, and a frame drawn twice counts once) */
  add(enc: GPUCommandEncoder, src: GPUTextureView, w: number, h: number, smp: GPUSampler, state: number, n: number, target: number, gen: number) {
    if (!this.acc || this.acc.width !== w || this.acc.height !== h) {
      this.acc?.destroy(); this.shotTex?.destroy(); this.shotTex = this.shotView = null; this.release();
      this.acc = this.device.createTexture({ label: 'photo average', size: [w, h], format: 'rgba16float',
        usage: GPUTextureUsage.RENDER_ATTACHMENT | GPUTextureUsage.TEXTURE_BINDING | GPUTextureUsage.COPY_SRC });
      this.accView = this.acc.createView();
      this.count = 0; this.gen = 0;
    }
    if (state === PH_ADD || state === PH_DONE) {
      if (gen !== this.gen) { this.gen = gen; this.count = 0; }
      this.target = target; this.done = this.count > 0 && this.count >= target;
      if (state === PH_DONE || n !== this.count + 1) return;
      this.count = n; this.done = n >= target;
    } else { this.count = 0; this.target = 0; this.gen = 0; this.done = state === PH_NOW; }   // (now: this frame is it)
    const k = this.count > 0 ? 1 / this.count : 1;
    const pass = enc.beginRenderPass({ colorAttachments: [{ view: this.accView!, loadOp: k === 1 ? 'clear' : 'load', clearValue: [0, 0, 0, 1], storeOp: 'store' }] });
    pass.setPipeline(this.addPipe);
    pass.setBindGroup(0, this.bg(src, smp, this.bufShow, 'add'));
    pass.setBlendConstant([k, k, k, k]);
    pass.draw(3);
    pass.end();
  }

  private fill(look: PhotoLook, tone: ArrayLike<number> | null, preview: [number, number] | null, tile?: PhotoTile) {
    const a = this.args, c = look.crop, n = tile?.n ?? 1, f = this.fisheye;
    // the fisheye's: the tangent of the picture's half diagonal as drawn (its half width's times the diagonal's share)
    const tc = f ? Math.tan(Math.min(170, Math.max(1, f.fov)) * Math.PI / 360) * Math.hypot(1, 1 / f.aspect) : 0;
    a.set([look.exposure, look.contrast, look.saturation, look.vignette,
      look.tint[0], look.tint[1], look.tint[2], look.fade,
      tone ? tone[0] : 1, tone ? tone[1] : 1, tone ? tone[2] : 1, tone ? 1 : 0,
      c[0], c[1], c[2], c[3],
      look.grid ? 1 : 0, preview ? 1 : 0, preview ? preview[0] * (c[2] - c[0]) : 0, preview ? preview[1] * (c[3] - c[1]) : 0,
      (tile?.x ?? 0) / n, (tile?.y ?? 0) / n, 1 / n, 1 / n,
      f ? 1 : 0, tc, f?.aspect ?? 1, 0]);
  }

  /** the canvas keeps showing the picture as it is now (a picture in tiles is being taken: the average holds tiles) */
  hold(enc: GPUCommandEncoder) {
    if (!this.acc || this.holdTex) return;
    this.holdTex = this.device.createTexture({ label: 'photo picture held', size: [this.acc.width, this.acc.height], format: 'rgba16float',
      usage: GPUTextureUsage.COPY_DST | GPUTextureUsage.TEXTURE_BINDING });
    this.holdView = this.holdTex.createView();
    enc.copyTextureToTexture({ texture: this.acc }, { texture: this.holdTex }, [this.acc.width, this.acc.height]);
  }
  /** ...and the average again */
  release() { this.holdTex?.destroy(); this.holdTex = this.holdView = null; }
  get holding() { return !!this.holdTex; }

  /** the average with its look into dst (the canvas), in the viewport vp, with Exposure and White Level (tone) and the
   *  crop's preview */
  show(enc: GPUCommandEncoder, dst: GPUTextureView, format: GPUTextureFormat, smp: GPUSampler, vp: [number, number, number, number],
       look: PhotoLook, tone: ArrayLike<number> | null, ts?: GPURenderPassTimestampWrites) {
    if (!this.accView) return;
    this.fill(look, tone, [vp[2], vp[3]]);
    this.device.queue.writeBuffer(this.bufShow, 0, this.args);
    const pass = enc.beginRenderPass({ colorAttachments: [{ view: dst, loadOp: 'clear', clearValue: [0, 0, 0, 1], storeOp: 'store' }], timestampWrites: ts });
    pass.setPipeline(this.lookPipe(format));
    pass.setBindGroup(0, this.bg(this.holdView ?? this.accView, smp, this.bufShow, 'show'));
    pass.setViewport(vp[0], vp[1], vp[2], vp[3], 0, 1);
    pass.draw(3);
    pass.end();
  }

  /** the picture as kept: the look over the average at its own size (no Exposure and White Level, no preview), and the
   *  crop's rectangle of it in pixels (a tile's: the whole tile, its look as the whole picture's part) */
  shot(enc: GPUCommandEncoder, smp: GPUSampler, look: PhotoLook, tile?: PhotoTile): { tex: GPUTexture; x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number } | null {
    if (!this.acc || !this.accView) return null;
    const W = this.acc.width, H = this.acc.height;
    if (!this.shotTex) {
      this.shotTex = this.device.createTexture({ label: 'photo picture', size: [W, H], format: 'bgra8unorm',
        usage: GPUTextureUsage.RENDER_ATTACHMENT | GPUTextureUsage.COPY_SRC });
      this.shotView = this.shotTex.createView();
    }
    this.fill(look, null, null, tile);
    this.device.queue.writeBuffer(this.bufShot, 0, this.args);
    const pass = enc.beginRenderPass({ colorAttachments: [{ view: this.shotView!, loadOp: 'clear', clearValue: [0, 0, 0, 1], storeOp: 'store' }] });
    pass.setPipeline(this.lookPipe('bgra8unorm'));
    pass.setBindGroup(0, this.bg(this.accView, smp, this.bufShot, 'shot'));
    pass.draw(3);
    pass.end();
    if (tile) return { tex: this.shotTex, x: 0, y: 0, w: W, h: H };
    const c = look.crop;
    const x = Math.max(0, Math.min(W - 1, Math.round(c[0] * W))), y = Math.max(0, Math.min(H - 1, Math.round(c[1] * H)));
    const w = Math.max(1, Math.min(W - x, Math.round((c[2] - c[0]) * W))), h = Math.max(1, Math.min(H - y, Math.round((c[3] - c[1]) * H)));
    return { tex: this.shotTex, x, y, w, h };
  }

  destroy() { this.acc?.destroy(); this.shotTex?.destroy(); this.release(); this.acc = this.shotTex = null; this.accView = this.shotView = null; }
}

{"id": "AT001825", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/web/src/gpu/png-worker.ts", "originalBytes": 3649, "originalSha256": "ee6f646d868cf753ff634e32ce0ae6bb309d6e3d2cb01cf66c03b342980ca4b4", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 3649, "utf8TotalBytes": 3649}

// The renderer's frame dumps (index.ts readback: F12 screenshots, the tests'
// dumps) made into PNGs here instead of on the page thread, which draws the
// game: converting and encoding a 4K frame held it for over 100 ms.
// In: a readback's bytes (BGRA rows bpr apart); out: the frame as a PNG,
// scaled down by `scale` when it is below 1, with the site's address in its
// corner when `mark` is set (F12 pictures, unless photo mode's panel turned it off).
// A picture bigger than the screen comes as tiles (photo mode's Size): each put in its place of one big picture as
// it comes, then the crop's rectangle of it made into the PNG.

import { drawMark, markBox } from './mark';

export interface ToPng { id: number; px: ArrayBuffer; w: number; h: number; bpr: number; scale: number; mark?: boolean }
/** a tile of picture `pic` (W x H in all) at x, y; its last message (end) gives the crop's rectangle and the mark */
export interface ToPngTile { tile: true; pic: number; px: ArrayBuffer; w: number; h: number; bpr: number; x: number; y: number; W: number; H: number }
export interface ToPngEnd { end: true; id: number; pic: number; crop: [number, number, number, number]; mark?: boolean }
export type FromPng = { id: number; png: Blob } | { id: number; error: string };

const post = (m: FromPng) => (self as unknown as Worker).postMessage(m);

/** the address bottom right (mark.ts), 2.6 % of the picture's height */
function mark(g: OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D, w: number, h: number) {
  const px = Math.max(12, Math.round(h * 0.026)), m = Math.round(h * 0.024);
  drawMark(g, px, w - m - markBox(g, px).w, h - m);
}

/** a readback's BGRA rows as an image */
function image(px: ArrayBuffer, w: number, h: number, bpr: number): ImageData {
  const src = new Uint8Array(px), img = new ImageData(w, h), d = img.data;
  for (let y = 0; y < h; y++) {
    let s = y * bpr, o = y * w * 4;
    for (let x = 0; x < w; x++, s += 4, o += 4) { d[o] = src[s + 2]; d[o + 1] = src[s + 1]; d[o + 2] = src[s]; d[o + 3] = 255; }
  }
  return img;
}

// the big pictures being put together, by number
const big = new Map<number, OffscreenCanvas>();

onmessage = async (e: MessageEvent<ToPng | ToPngTile | ToPngEnd>) => {
  const m = e.data;
  if ('tile' in m) {
    let c = big.get(m.pic);
    if (!c) big.set(m.pic, c = new OffscreenCanvas(m.W, m.H));
    c.getContext('2d')!.putImageData(image(m.px, m.w, m.h, m.bpr), m.x, m.y);
    return;
  }
  if ('end' in m) {
    const c = big.get(m.pic);
    big.delete(m.pic);
    try {
      if (!c) throw new Error('no tiles');
      const [x, y, w, h] = m.crop;
      let oc = c;
      if (x || y || w !== c.width || h !== c.height) { oc = new OffscreenCanvas(w, h); oc.getContext('2d')!.drawImage(c, -x, -y); }
      if (m.mark) mark(oc.getContext('2d')!, oc.width, oc.height);
      post({ id: m.id, png: await oc.convertToBlob({ type: 'image/png' }) });
    } catch (x) { post({ id: m.id, error: String(x) }); }
    return;
  }
  const { id, px, w, h, bpr, scale, mark: marked } = m;
  try {
    const img = image(px, w, h, bpr);
    let oc = new OffscreenCanvas(w, h);
    oc.getContext('2d')!.putImageData(img, 0, 0);
    if (scale > 0 && scale < 1) {
      const o2 = new OffscreenCanvas(Math.max(1, Math.round(w * scale)), Math.max(1, Math.round(h * scale)));
      const g = o2.getContext('2d')!;
      g.imageSmoothingQuality = 'high';
      g.drawImage(oc, 0, 0, o2.width, o2.height);
      oc = o2;
    }
    if (marked) mark(oc.getContext('2d')!, oc.width, oc.height);
    post({ id, png: await oc.convertToBlob({ type: 'image/png' }) });
  } catch (x) { post({ id, error: String(x) }); }
};

export const K_MARKS = 1024, MARKS_BYTES = 528, MARKS_MAX = 32, MARKS_MAGIC = 0x4B52414D;

export const K_LAT = 1568, LAT_BYTES = 24, LAT_MAGIC = 0x4E54414C;

export const K_PHOTO = 1600, PHOTO_BYTES = 48, PHOTO_MAGIC = 0x544F4850, PHOTO_ACK = 20, PHOTO_TILE = 24, PHOTO_WANT = 28,

// the VS constant arena is bound in windows of this many 16-byte rows (GW_KWIN_ROWS)
export const KWIN_ROWS = 4096;

// rectangle, left | top << 16 and right | bottom << 16 (count 0 = the whole source)
export const DRAW_BYTES = 180, DRAW_WORDS = 45;
export const enum D {

  tex1 = 8, tex2 = 9, tex3 = 10, ps = 11, psci = 12, vsid = 13, rawoff = 14, koff = 15,
  proj = 16, smp = 20, blitSrc = 24, bcol = 25, cull = 26, fogv = 27, clrArgb = 31, clrFlags = 32,

export const enum Kind { Draw = 0, Clear = 1, Blit = 2 }

// GwFrame: 156 bytes.  rbId nonzero: after the frame, texture rbTex's level 0 goes to the game, rbRows rows of
// rbPitch bytes at wasm address rbDst (see C.rbWant)

{"id": "AT001827", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/web/src/gpu/shader-abi.ts", "originalBytes": 3906, "originalSha256": "fdd14bb445f97f8c50b13a025860490e7c8d70e70d68fdbab5cfae09c4a45747", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 3906, "utf8TotalBytes": 3906}

// The WGSL shader ABI as WebGPU objects: the bind group
// layouts and pipeline layouts every game pipeline uses, the uniform sizes and
// the override constants.  The renderer and the shader check both build their
// pipelines from here, so the check validates exactly what the game will run.

/** A draw's VS constant block: {stride, tsel, base, target w | h << 16} + 256 vec4f (the rows it may read). */
export const VSPAR_SIZE = 4112;
/** The K binding: a 64 KB window of the frame's VS constant arena (gpu_proto.h GW_KWIN_ROWS rows); a draw's
 *  block starts at row firstInstance of it, at most KWIN_SIZE - VSPAR_SIZE bytes in. */
export const KWIN_SIZE = 65536;
/** PSPar: {aref, usec, pad0, pad1}, proj, 32 vec4f, fog. */
export const PSPAR_SIZE = 560;
/** HLPar (gpu_proto.h GwHL): the other cars' headlights, {n, s, o, pad} + 8 x {mat4x4f, vec4f}. */
export const HLPAR_SIZE = 656;
/** One CPU-transformed vertex (gfx.h TVert): pos, col0, col1, t[4], all f32. */
export const TVERT_SIZE = 112;
/** Pixel shader id offset of the stage-0 cube twin (com.c / metal.m PSCUBE). */
export const PSCUBE = 256;
/** Interstage locations used by VOut (col0, col1, uv0..uv3, fog). */
export const VOUT_LOCATIONS = 7;

/** D3DCMP values for the ALPHA_FUNC override: 7 = the Mac's "a >= aref" test, 8 = no test, no discard. */
export const ALPHA_GREATEREQUAL = 7;
export const ALPHA_ALWAYS = 8;

/** ALPHA_FUNC for a draw, as the Mac picks its no-discard twin (MDraw.alpha_ref <= 0). */
export function alphaFunc(alphaRef: number): number {
  return alphaRef > 0 ? ALPHA_GREATEREQUAL : ALPHA_ALWAYS;
}

/** Override constants every pixel shader module declares (unknown keys are a pipeline error). */
export interface PsConstants { ALPHA_FUNC: number; PS20_TEXCOORD?: number }

/** True when pixel shader module `ps_<id>` is a cube twin and needs the cube layout. */
export function isCubePs(id: number): boolean { return id >= PSCUBE; }

export interface ShaderAbi {
  /** group 0: VB (storage), K and P (uniform, dynamic offsets in that order), H (uniform, the frame's). */
  group0: GPUBindGroupLayout;
  /** group 1: tex0..tex3 (2d) at bindings 0..3, smp0..smp3 at 4..7. */
  group1: GPUBindGroupLayout;
  /** group 1 with tex0 as a cube texture. */
  group1Cube: GPUBindGroupLayout;
  layout2d: GPUPipelineLayout;
  layoutCube: GPUPipelineLayout;
}

export function createShaderAbi(device: GPUDevice): ShaderAbi {
  const V = GPUShaderStage.VERTEX, F = GPUShaderStage.FRAGMENT;
  const group0 = device.createBindGroupLayout({
    label: 'abi.group0',
    entries: [
      { binding: 0, visibility: V, buffer: { type: 'read-only-storage', hasDynamicOffset: false } },
      { binding: 1, visibility: V, buffer: { type: 'uniform', hasDynamicOffset: true, minBindingSize: KWIN_SIZE } },
      { binding: 2, visibility: F, buffer: { type: 'uniform', hasDynamicOffset: true, minBindingSize: PSPAR_SIZE } },
      { binding: 3, visibility: F, buffer: { type: 'uniform', hasDynamicOffset: true, minBindingSize: HLPAR_SIZE } },
    ],
  });
  const textures = (cube: boolean): GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry[] => {
    const e: GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry[] = [];
    for (let k = 0; k < 4; k++)
      e.push({ binding: k, visibility: F, texture: { sampleType: 'float', viewDimension: cube && k === 0 ? 'cube' : '2d' } });
    for (let k = 0; k < 4; k++) e.push({ binding: 4 + k, visibility: F, sampler: { type: 'filtering' } });
    return e;
  };
  const group1 = device.createBindGroupLayout({ label: 'abi.group1', entries: textures(false) });
  const group1Cube = device.createBindGroupLayout({ label: 'abi.group1.cube', entries: textures(true) });
  return {
    group0, group1, group1Cube,
    layout2d: device.createPipelineLayout({ label: 'abi.layout2d', bindGroupLayouts: [group0, group1] }),
    layoutCube: device.createPipelineLayout({ label: 'abi.layoutCube', bindGroupLayouts: [group0, group1Cube] }),
  };
}

export type Viewport = [number, number, number, number, number, number];
/** Intersect the camera cell, letterboxed UI and normalized post-effect cell.
 * Normalized clips work on both full-size and downsampled bloom targets.
 * Fills and returns `out` (the encoder passes its own: a draw allocates nothing). */
export function drawScissor(v: ArrayLike<number>, width: number, height: number, clip = 0, fx0 = 0, fx1 = 0,
                            out: number[] = [0, 0, 0, 0]): number[] {
  const x0 = Math.max(Math.ceil(v[0]), fx1 ? Math.round((fx0 & 65535) * width / 65535) : 0);
  const x1 = Math.min(Math.floor(v[0] + v[2]), fx1 ? Math.round((fx1 & 65535) * width / 65535) : width);
  const y0 = Math.max(Math.ceil(v[1]), fx1 ? Math.round((fx0 >>> 16) * height / 65535) : 0, clip ? Math.min(clip & 65535, height) : 0);
  const y1 = Math.min(Math.floor(v[1] + v[3]), fx1 ? Math.round((fx1 >>> 16) * height / 65535) : height, clip ? Math.min(clip >>> 16, height) : height);
  out[0] = x0; out[1] = y0; out[2] = Math.max(0, x1 - x0); out[3] = Math.max(0, y1 - y0);
  return out;
}
/** Validate before setViewport: invalid guest state must not invalidate a
 * whole WebGPU frame. An unset viewport means the full render target.
 * Fills and returns `out`, or null for a viewport that is not valid. */
export function drawViewport(values: ArrayLike<number>, offset: number, width: number, height: number,
                             out: number[] = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]): number[] | null {
  if (!values[offset + 2]) { out[0] = 0; out[1] = 0; out[2] = width; out[3] = height; out[4] = 0; out[5] = 1; return out; }
  for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) out[i] = values[offset + i];
  // written so that a NaN or an infinity fails it
  if (!(out[0] >= 0 && out[1] >= 0 && out[2] > 0 && out[3] > 0 && out[0] + out[2] <= width && out[1] + out[3] <= height
        && out[4] >= 0 && out[5] <= 1 && out[4] <= out[5])) return null;
  return out;
}

{"id": "AT001829", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/web/src/gpu/wgsl.ts", "originalBytes": 8029, "originalSha256": "7496eefbd8ba1e2b379258d856a251d109d1cb4145312aef1dcc689c74dc16db", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 8029, "utf8TotalBytes": 8029}

// Built-in WGSL: the copy/composite passes, and fallbacks for the
// pretransformed-vertex (TVert) path and the fixed-function fragment stage
// (the translator's vs_0 / ps_0 / ps_256 replace them as soon as the game
// registers those).  The game's own shaders come
// from the translator (track gpu-shaders) over the same bindings:
//   group 0: VB (storage, vertex pulling), K (VS constants, dynamic offset),
//            P (PS parameters, dynamic offset)
//   group 1: t0..t3 at bindings 0..3, s0..s3 at bindings 4..7
// and the same inter-stage block (VOut), so a translated pixel shader can sit
// behind the TVert vertex stage and the other way round.

export const VOUT = /* wgsl */`
struct VOut {
  @builtin(position) pos: vec4f,
  @location(0) col0: vec4f,
  @location(1) col1: vec4f,
  @location(2) uv0: vec4f,
  @location(3) uv1: vec4f,
  @location(4) uv2: vec4f,
  @location(5) uv3: vec4f,
  @location(6) fog: f32,
}`;

const PSPAR = /* wgsl */`
struct PSPar { aref: f32, usec: f32, pad0: f32, pad1: f32, proj: vec4f, c: array<vec4f, 32>, fog: vec4f }
@group(0) @binding(2) var<uniform> P: PSPar;`;

// The CPU vertex path (com.c draw_up -> metal_draw_tv): clip-space vertices,
// both colours and four 4-component texture coordinates, pulled from the
// frame's TVert arena (28 floats per vertex).  As metal.m vmain: no fog.
export const TVERT_VS = /* wgsl */`
${VOUT}
@group(0) @binding(0) var<storage, read> VB: array<f32>;
@vertex fn vs_tvert(@builtin(vertex_index) vi: u32) -> VOut {
  let b = vi * 28u;
  var o: VOut;
  o.pos  = vec4f(VB[b],       VB[b + 1u],  VB[b + 2u],  VB[b + 3u]);
  o.col0 = vec4f(VB[b + 4u],  VB[b + 5u],  VB[b + 6u],  VB[b + 7u]);
  o.col1 = vec4f(VB[b + 8u],  VB[b + 9u],  VB[b + 10u], VB[b + 11u]);
  o.uv0  = vec4f(VB[b + 12u], VB[b + 13u], VB[b + 14u], VB[b + 15u]);
  o.uv1  = vec4f(VB[b + 16u], VB[b + 17u], VB[b + 18u], VB[b + 19u]);
  o.uv2  = vec4f(VB[b + 20u], VB[b + 21u], VB[b + 22u], VB[b + 23u]);
  o.uv3  = vec4f(VB[b + 24u], VB[b + 25u], VB[b + 26u], VB[b + 27u]);
  o.fog  = 1.0;
  return o;
}`;

// metal.m fmain/fmain_nd: col0 x tex0, alpha test (a < ref discards), vertex
// fog.  ALPHA_FUNC: 7 = the Mac's test, 8 = the
// no-discard twin (alpha_ref <= 0) that keeps hidden-surface removal on tile
// GPUs.  Used only until the translator's ps_0 / ps_256 arrive.
export const FF_FS = (cube: boolean) => /* wgsl */`
${VOUT}
${PSPAR}
@group(1) @binding(0) var t0: ${cube ? 'texture_cube<f32>' : 'texture_2d<f32>'};
@group(1) @binding(4) var s0: sampler;
override ALPHA_FUNC: u32 = 7u;
@fragment fn fs_ff(i: VOut) -> @location(0) vec4f {
  var c = i.col0 * textureSample(t0, s0, ${cube ? 'i.uv0.xyz' : 'i.uv0.xy'});
  if (ALPHA_FUNC == 7u && c.a < P.aref) { discard; }
  return vec4f(mix(P.fog.rgb, c.rgb, mix(1.0, saturate(i.fog), P.fog.a)), c.a);
}`;

// Full-target triangle sampling one texture: StretchRect between differently
// sized targets and the final composite to the canvas.  uv (0,0) = top left,
// as metal.m's blit quad.
export const COPY = /* wgsl */`
@group(0) @binding(0) var src: texture_2d<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(1) var smp: sampler;
struct BOut { @builtin(position) pos: vec4f, @location(0) uv: vec2f }
@vertex fn vs_full(@builtin(vertex_index) i: u32) -> BOut {
  let p = vec2f(f32((i << 1u) & 2u), f32(i & 2u));
  var o: BOut;
  o.pos = vec4f(p.x * 2.0 - 1.0, 1.0 - p.y * 2.0, 0.0, 1.0);
  o.uv = p;
  return o;
}
@fragment fn fs_copy(i: BOut) -> @location(0) vec4f { return textureSample(src, smp, i.uv); }
@fragment fn fs_opaque(i: BOut) -> @location(0) vec4f { return vec4f(textureSample(src, smp, i.uv).rgb, 1.0); }`;

// A 4-sample twin (runtime/com.c MULTISAMPLING) into its target: the average of each pixel's 4 samples, what the GPU's
// own resolve does, drawn instead of it (encoder.ts msResolve).  The twin is the same size as the target, so a pixel's
// position is its texel.
export const MS_RESOLVE = /* wgsl */`
@group(0) @binding(0) var src: texture_multisampled_2d<f32>;
@vertex fn vs_full(@builtin(vertex_index) i: u32) -> @builtin(position) vec4f {
  let p = vec2f(f32((i << 1u) & 2u), f32(i & 2u));
  return vec4f(p.x * 2.0 - 1.0, 1.0 - p.y * 2.0, 0.0, 1.0);
}
@fragment fn fs_resolve(@builtin(position) pos: vec4f) -> @location(0) vec4f {
  let c = vec2i(pos.xy);
  return (textureLoad(src, c, 0) + textureLoad(src, c, 1) + textureLoad(src, c, 2) + textureLoad(src, c, 3)) * 0.25;
}`;

// The composite with Exposure and White Level (runtime/tonemenu.c, GwTone): each channel times mult (at most 1),
// then a value above knee * white bends down so that 1 lands on white (a rational shoulder: slope 1 where it starts,
// so no edge shows).  tone: mult, white, knee.
export const TONE = COPY + /* wgsl */`
@group(0) @binding(2) var<uniform> tone: vec4f;
@fragment fn fs_tone(i: BOut) -> @location(0) vec4f {
  let y = min(textureSample(src, smp, i.uv).rgb * tone.x, vec3f(1.0));
  let s = tone.z * tone.y;
  let m = (1.0 - s) / (tone.y - s);
  let t = max(y - s, vec3f(0.0)) / (1.0 - s);
  let b = s + (tone.y - s) * (m * t) / (1.0 + (m - 1.0) * t);
  return vec4f(select(y, b, y > vec3f(s)), 1.0);
}`;

// Photo mode's picture (photo-picture.ts): fs_add takes the back buffer pixel for pixel into the average (the blend
// weighs it); fs_look draws the average with the picture's look: exposure (a.x, times), the tint (b.rgb, times),
// saturation (a.z, 0 grey), contrast (a.y, about the middle), fade (b.w: blacks lifted that far), vignette (a.w: the
// corners of the kept part darker by that much), then Exposure and White Level as TONE does (t: mult, white, knee;
// t.w 1: on).  crop: the kept part (left, top, right, bottom, 0 .. 1).  The preview only (g.y 1): outside the kept
// part dimmed, and with g.x 1 the lines of thirds over it, g.zw its size in pixels.
export const PHOTO = COPY + /* wgsl */`
// tl: a tile's place in the whole picture (where its corner is, its part of the width and height: the vignette and the
// crop are the whole picture's); fx: the fisheye (on, the tangent of the picture's half diagonal as drawn, width over
// height)
struct Look { a: vec4f, b: vec4f, t: vec4f, crop: vec4f, g: vec4f, tl: vec4f, fx: vec4f }
@group(0) @binding(2) var<uniform> L: Look;
@fragment fn fs_add(i: BOut) -> @location(0) vec4f { return vec4f(textureLoad(src, vec2i(i.pos.xy), 0).rgb, 1.0); }
// the fisheye: the picture's corners stay where they are (a full-frame fisheye), each point as far out as a
// stereographic lens puts it: the middle larger, straight lines bowed round it
fn fisheye(uv: vec2f) -> vec2f {
  let a = L.fx.z;
  let v = (uv - vec2f(0.5)) * vec2f(a, 1.0);
  let R = 0.5 * sqrt(a * a + 1.0);
  let rho = length(v) / R;
  let tc = L.fx.y;
  let k = 2.0 * tan(0.5 * atan(tc)) / tc;            // where rho -> 0
  let th = 2.0 * atan(rho * tan(0.5 * atan(tc)));
  let s = select(k, tan(th) / tc / max(rho, 1e-6), rho > 1e-4);
  return vec2f(0.5) + v * s / vec2f(a, 1.0);
}
@fragment fn fs_look(i: BOut) -> @location(0) vec4f {
  let uv = select(i.uv, fisheye(i.uv), L.fx.x > 0.5);
  var c = textureSample(src, smp, uv).rgb * L.a.x * L.b.rgb;
  c = mix(vec3f(dot(c, vec3f(0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722))), c, L.a.z);
  c = (c - vec3f(0.5)) * L.a.y + vec3f(0.5);
  c = vec3f(L.b.w) + c * (1.0 - L.b.w);
  let sz = max(L.crop.zw - L.crop.xy, vec2f(1e-6));
  let p = (L.tl.xy + i.uv * L.tl.zw - L.crop.xy) / sz;
  c *= 1.0 - L.a.w * smoothstep(0.25, 1.0, length(p - vec2f(0.5)) * 1.41421356);
  c = clamp(c, vec3f(0.0), vec3f(1.0));
  if (L.t.w > 0.5) {
    let y = min(c * L.t.x, vec3f(1.0));
    let s = L.t.z * L.t.y;
    let m = (1.0 - s) / (L.t.y - s);
    let t = max(y - s, vec3f(0.0)) / (1.0 - s);
    c = select(y, s + (L.t.y - s) * (m * t) / (1.0 + (m - 1.0) * t), y > vec3f(s));
  }
  if (L.g.y > 0.5) {
    if (any(p < vec2f(0.0)) || any(p > vec2f(1.0))) { c *= 0.3; }
    else if (L.g.x > 0.5) {
      let d = min(abs(p - vec2f(1.0 / 3.0)), abs(p - vec2f(2.0 / 3.0))) * L.g.zw;
      if (min(d.x, d.y) < 0.75) { c = mix(c, vec3f(1.0), 0.55); }
    }
  }
  return vec4f(c, 1.0);
}`;

// The game data cache in OPFS "cache/", shared by the I/O worker (which fills
// it with the blocks the game reads) and the predownload worker (which fills
// all of it ahead, predownload-worker.ts).  One sparse file per file of the
// install folder, named by its path, size and mtime (a file changed on the
// server is a new name), next to a ".have" map of one byte per 1 MiB block.
// A block's data is written before its byte in the map.

export const BLOCK = 1 << 20;
export const CACHE_DIR = 'cache';
/** the game data's cache files the I/O worker keeps open in this browser (io-worker.ts CACHE_OPEN, which says why):
 *  512 in Chrome (Edge, Opera...) and Firefox on Windows, 64 elsewhere (Safari takes 251 handles at most) */
export function cacheOpen(ua: string): number {
  return /Windows/.test(ua) && /\b(Chrome|Firefox)\//.test(ua) ? 512 : 64;
}
/** where the server has the manifest and the install folder (web/server-rs/src/app/manifest.rs) */
export const MANIFEST_URL = '/data-manifest', DATA_BASE = '/data/';

/** the server's /data-manifest: every file and folder of the install folder it serves, and where it serves runs
 *  of their blocks compressed */
export interface Manifest {
  files: { p: string; d?: number; s?: number; m?: number }[];
  blocks: { url: string; size: number; max: number };
}
/** The manifest's compressed runs in this cache's block size: [url, most blocks a request]; throws when it names
 *  none. */
export function blockRuns(m: Manifest): { url: string; max: number } {
  const b = m.blocks;
  if (b && typeof b.url === 'string' && b.url.startsWith('/') && b.size === BLOCK && b.max >= 1) return { url: b.url, max: b.max };
  throw new Error(`the list of game files names no blocks of ${BLOCK} bytes (${JSON.stringify(b ?? null)})`);
}
/** blocks first .. first+n-1 of a file, compressed: a 200 whose body (decoded by the browser) is exactly their bytes.  The
 *  file's mtime and size (m, s) make a changed file a new address, so the server lets Cloudflare keep the answer for
 *  good. */
export const runUrl = (base: string, path: string, first: number, n: number, f: { mtime: number; size: number }) =>
  `${dataUrl(base, path)}?b=${first}&n=${n}&m=${f.mtime}&s=${f.size}`;
/** bytes off .. off+len-1 of a file as they are: a 200 of exactly those bytes, which Cloudflare keeps for good like a

export const exactUrl = (base: string, path: string, off: number, len: number, f: { mtime: number; size: number }) =>

const parts = (f: DataFile) => f.path.toLowerCase().split('/');
/** The data the settings pick: a texture pack (TEXPACKS/<name>.pak, runtime/web/texrep_web.c; '' for none), the
 *  songs (settings.ini songs: 'original' reads pfdata/original's files in place of pfdata's, songsPath), the crash
 *  damage's scratches (MODPACKS/DAMAGE/, runtime/damage.c, which opens them only with crash_damage on) and the
 *  gearbox whine's sounds (MODPACKS/WHINE, runtime/whine.c: read only with gearbox_whine on). */
export interface Packs { texpack: string; songs: string; damage?: boolean; whine?: boolean }
export const NO_PACKS: Packs = { texpack: '', songs: '' };
/** EA's own songs (tools/musicpack.py --original) for a file of pfdata: pfdata/<name> -> pfdata/original/<name>; null
 *  for any other path.  The folder's own are a soundtrack mod's uncensored versions. */
export function songsPath(path: string): string | null {
  const p = path.split('/');
  return p.length === 2 && p[0].toLowerCase() === 'pfdata' ? [p[0], 'original', p[1]].join('/') : null;
}
/** The files a game in this language reads: the folder's, but where its language pack (LANGPACKS/<language>,
 *  runtime/language.c) has a file of the same path, that one; no other language's pack; of the texture packs
 *  (TEXPACKS/<name>.pak and its <name>.tracks, runtime/web/texrep_web.c) only those picked (packs.texpack: their
 *  names, comma-separated; '' for none); pfdata/original's files only with the original songs, and then in place
 *  of pfdata's; the crash damage's (MODPACKS/DAMAGE/) only with it on, and MODPACKS/WHINE only with the gearbox whine on.
 *  HQVINYLS/ never: the HQ vinyls' pictures (gpu/hqskin.ts) are read as cars are seen, 330 MB in all. */
function gameFiles(files: DataFile[], language: string, packs: Packs): DataFile[] {
  const own = new Set(files.filter(f => { const p = parts(f); return p[0] === 'langpacks' && p[1] === language; })
    .map(f => parts(f).slice(2).join('/')));
  const isOriginal = (p: string[]) => p.length === 3 && p[0] === 'pfdata' && p[1] === 'original';
  const original = packs.songs === 'original';
  const replaced = new Set(original ? files.map(parts).filter(isOriginal).map(p => `pfdata/${p[2]}`) : []);
  return files.filter(f => {
    const p = parts(f);
    if (p[0] === 'texpacks') return p.length === 2 && packs.texpack.split(',').some(n => n && (p[1] === `${n}.pak` || p[1] === `${n}.tracks`));
    if (p[0] === 'modpacks' && p[1] === 'damage') return !!packs.damage;
    if (p[0] === 'modpacks' && p[1] === 'whine') return !!packs.whine;
    if (p[0] === 'hqvinyls') return false;
    if (isOriginal(p)) return original;
    if (replaced.has(p.join('/'))) return false;
    return p[0] === 'langpacks' ? p[1] === language : !own.has(p.join('/'));
  });
}
const isMovie = (f: DataFile) => { const p = parts(f); return (p[0] === 'langpacks' ? p[2] : p[0]) === 'movies'; };
/** The AV1 copy of a movie (tools/movies_av1.py, played where the browser decodes AV1: movie.ts): MOVIES/<name>.vp6 ->
 *  MOVIES/AV1/<name>.vp6, the same in a language pack's MOVIES; null for any other path. */
export function av1Path(path: string): string | null {
  const p = path.split('/'), i = p[0].toLowerCase() === 'langpacks' ? 2 : 0;
  if (p.length !== i + 2 || p[i].toLowerCase() !== 'movies' || !p[i + 1].toLowerCase().endsWith('.vp6')) return null;
  return [...p.slice(0, i + 1), 'AV1', p[i + 1]].join('/');
}
/** What "Preload the game data" fetches: all but the movies (MOVIES/, a third of the folder in VP6 video that
 *  does not compress, and their AV1 copies).  They stream as they play, and with Movies off the game never opens
 *  them. */
export const aheadFiles = (files: DataFile[], language: string, packs: Packs = NO_PACKS) =>
  gameFiles(files, language, packs).filter(f => !isMovie(f));
/** The movies a game in this language can open: its VP6 files, or where it plays AV1 (av1) their AV1 copies, the
 *  VP6 file where a movie has none (as the I/O worker opens them, io-worker.ts dataFile). */
export function languageMovies(files: DataFile[], language: string, av1 = false): DataFile[] {
  const all = gameFiles(files, language, NO_PACKS).filter(isMovie), byPath = new Map(all.map(f => [f.path.toLowerCase(), f]));
  return all.filter(f => av1Path(f.path) !== null).map(f => (av1 && byPath.get(av1Path(f.path)!.toLowerCase())) || f);
}
export const dataUrl = (base: string, path: string) => base + path.split('/').map(encodeURIComponent).join('/');
export function cacheKey(f: DataFile) { return `${f.path.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/g, '_')}.${f.size}.${f.mtime}`; }
export const blockCount = (size: number) => Math.ceil(size / BLOCK);
export const blockLen = (size: number, bi: number) => Math.min(BLOCK, size - bi * BLOCK);

/** A file's sync handles and its map, made empty if it does not fit the file (workers only). */
export async function openCacheFile(dir: FileSystemDirectoryHandle, f: DataFile): Promise<CacheFile> {
  const k = cacheKey(f);
  const fh = await dir.getFileHandle(k, { create: true });
  const mh = await dir.getFileHandle(k + '.have', { create: true });
  const h = await fh.createSyncAccessHandle({ mode: 'readwrite-unsafe' });
  let haveH: FileSystemSyncAccessHandle;
  try { haveH = await mh.createSyncAccessHandle({ mode: 'readwrite-unsafe' }); }
  catch (e) { h.close(); throw e; }
  const nb = blockCount(f.size);
  const have = new Uint8Array(nb);
  if (haveH.getSize() === nb) haveH.read(have, { at: 0 }); else { haveH.truncate(0); haveH.write(have, { at: 0 }); }
  return { h, have, haveH };
}

/** block bi of the file is in its cache file now (throws if it is not: no room for it, say) */
export function putBlock(cf: CacheFile, bi: number, b: Uint8Array) {
  const k = cf.h.write(b, { at: bi * BLOCK });
  if (k !== b.length) throw new Error(`${k} of ${b.length} bytes written`);   // marked as there, a short block would stay
  cf.have[bi] = 1; cf.haveH.write(cf.have.subarray(bi, bi + 1), { at: bi });
}

export interface Scan {
  /** bytes of the manifest's files, and of those that are in the cache */
  total: number; have: number;
  /** what the cache files take already (their sizes: the browser counts a sparse file's whole length) */
  allocated: number;
  /** each file's map (null: nothing of it yet) */
  files: { f: DataFile; have: Uint8Array | null }[];
}

/** What of the manifest's files the cache holds.  Async reads only (any thread), no handle is opened. */
export async function scanCache(files: DataFile[]): Promise<Scan> {
  const s: Scan = { total: 0, have: 0, allocated: 0, files: [] };
  let dir: FileSystemDirectoryHandle | null = null;
  try { dir = await (await navigator.storage.getDirectory()).getDirectoryHandle(CACHE_DIR); } catch { /* no cache yet */ }
  for (const f of files) {
    s.total += f.size;
    let have: Uint8Array | null = null;
    if (dir) try {
      const k = cacheKey(f);
      const m = new Uint8Array(await (await (await dir.getFileHandle(k + '.have')).getFile()).arrayBuffer());
      s.allocated += Math.min(f.size, (await (await dir.getFileHandle(k)).getFile()).size);
      if (m.length === blockCount(f.size)) have = m;
    } catch { /* not cached */ }
    if (have) for (let bi = 0; bi < have.length; bi++) if (have[bi]) s.have += blockLen(f.size, bi);
    s.files.push({ f, have });
  }
  return s;
}

// in ms: the runtime subtracts it from the time it held the guest lock to get
// the guest thread's busy time (runtime/win32_ext.c, [status] gcpu)

// page ({ t: 'memory' }): where the I/O worker could not post it on the port, or where nothing usable came on it in

const memoryFrom = (p: MessagePort, slot: number) => new Promise<WebAssembly.Memory>(res => {
  let done = false, asked = false;

  const viaPage = (why: string) => { if (done || asked) return; asked = true; post({ t: 'memory-please', slot, why }); };

  p.onmessage = (e) => { if (e.data instanceof WebAssembly.Memory) take(e.data); else viaPage('something else came on its port'); };

// One view of each kind, made again only when the memory grew, not one per call: a game thread's sleeps and file calls
// come hundreds of times a second, and its garbage is never collected in WebKit (a game thread holds the Memory:

const dv = () => (dvv && dvv.buffer === memory.buffer ? dvv : (dvv = new DataView(memory.buffer)));

// ---- logging: stdout/stderr lines go to the page ----
const pending: Record<number, string> = { 1: '', 2: '' };
function writeOut(fd: number, bytes: Uint8Array) {
  pending[fd] += td.decode(bytes, { stream: true });
  let k: number;
  while ((k = pending[fd].indexOf('\n')) >= 0) { post({ t: 'log', s: pending[fd].slice(0, k), fd, tid }); pending[fd] = pending[fd].slice(k + 1); }

// ---- synchronous call into the I/O worker ----
function io(op: Op, ...args: (number | bigint)[]): number {
  const b = slot * (RPC_SLOT / 4), b64 = slot * (RPC_SLOT / 8);
  rpcI32[b + 1] = op; rpcI32[b + 3] = args.length;
  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i++) rpcI64[b64 + 2 + i] = BigInt(args[i]);
  Atomics.store(rpcI32, b, RPC_POSTED);
  Atomics.add(ctl, CTL_IO_DOORBELL, 1); Atomics.notify(ctl, CTL_IO_DOORBELL);
  const t0 = performance.now();
  // wait on the value just checked: re-loading it for Atomics.wait could read
  // RPC_DONE (the I/O worker finished in between) and then sleep on DONE
  // forever, the notify already gone (seen: a CreateFileA that never returned).
  // In slices of a second: a request still unanswered after IO_SLOW_MS goes into
  // the log, with whether the I/O worker's loop still runs (CTL_IO_BEAT moved)
  let next = IO_SLOW_MS, beat = Atomics.load(ctl, CTL_IO_BEAT);
  for (let v; (v = Atomics.load(rpcI32, b)) !== RPC_DONE;) {
    Atomics.wait(rpcI32, b, v, 1000);
    const w = performance.now() - t0;
    if (w < next) continue;
    next *= 2;
    const now = Atomics.load(ctl, CTL_IO_BEAT), runs = now !== beat;
    beat = now;
    post({ t: 'log', fd: 2, tid, s: `[io] thread ${tid}: ${opName(op)} (fd ${args[0] ?? '-'}) unanswered for ${(w / 1000).toFixed(0)} s; ` +
      (runs ? 'the I/O worker runs (this request is stuck in it)' : 'the I/O worker has stopped (its loop has not run since)') });
  }
  blockedMs += performance.now() - t0;
  const r = rpcI32[b + 2];
  Atomics.store(rpcI32, b, RPC_IDLE);
  return r;
}

// clock_time_get is the guest's most frequent host import (QueryPerformanceCounter, timeGetTime: ~100 calls
// in a race frame).  It writes the same values as BigInt µs × 1000 would, but from integer microseconds held in doubles
// (exact below 2^53) as two u32 halves: no BigInt and no DataView per call.
// The time origin is fixed for the worker's life: read once, not on each of the guest's ~1,000 timer reads a frame;
// set to the I/O worker's clock before the worker takes a thread (alignClock)
let T0MS = performance.timeOrigin;
let T0US = Math.round(T0MS * 1e3);
/** Every worker's clock is its time origin + now(), and a worker's time origin is the wall clock as it started (as the
 *  browser had it then): one started after the system's clock was set reads that much off its elders.  WSL sets its
 *  clock about a second every 35 s on a loaded box: a pool worker started a minute into a game read 3.9 s ahead of the
 *  game's main thread, and EA's network clock (NetTick, runtime/winsock.c: never back across threads) jumped 4 s
 *  under the game's main thread; a LAN race broke at its start.  So each worker reads the I/O worker's clock (the
 *  first worker, started with the page) a few times before it takes a thread, and keeps the offset of the shortest
 *  round trip when the offset is more than that round trip (else its own clock stays, as before) */
function alignClock() {
  const f64 = new Float64Array(rpcI32.buffer), at = (slot * RPC_SLOT + 128) / 8;
  let best = Infinity, off = 0;
  for (let k = 0; k < 5; k++) {
    const t0 = T0MS + performance.now();
    if (io(Op.Clock, slot) !== 0) return;
    const t1 = T0MS + performance.now();
    if (t1 - t0 < best) { best = t1 - t0; off = f64[at] - (t0 + t1) / 2; }
  }
  if (!(Math.abs(off) > Math.max(1, best))) return;
  T0MS += off; T0US = Math.round(T0MS * 1e3);
  post({ t: 'log', s: `[clock] game worker ${slot}: its clock read ${(-off).toFixed(1)} ms off the I/O worker's (asked in ${best.toFixed(2)} ms): it reads that one`, fd: 2, tid });
}
let u32v: Uint32Array | null = null;
function writeUsAsNs(p: number, us: number) {
  if (p & 7) { dv().setBigUint64(p, BigInt(us) * 1000n, true); return; }
  if (!u32v || u32v.buffer !== memory.buffer) u32v = new Uint32Array(memory.buffer);
  const hi = Math.floor(us / 4294967296), lo = (us - hi * 4294967296) * 1000, carry = Math.floor(lo / 4294967296);
  u32v[p >>> 2] = lo - carry * 4294967296; u32v[(p >>> 2) + 1] = hi * 1000 + carry;
}

// NFSU2_TEST_TIMER_MS=15.625 (tests): every sleep ends on that grid of the clock, as a wait does in Chrome on
// Windows while the OS timer ticks every 15.6 ms (runtime/win32_ext.c, the frame pacer's sleep)
let timerGrid = -1;
function sleepMs(ms: number) {

  if (ms > 0 && timerGrid > 0) { const now = T0MS + performance.now(); ms = Math.ceil((now + ms) / timerGrid) * timerGrid - now; }

function strings(list: string[]) { return list.map(s => te.encode(s + '\0')); }

// A wasm i32 comes into JS signed: a pointer at 2 GB or more (the runtime's heap past the guest heap's window above
// it, runtime/guest_span.h) would be a negative offset.  Every WASI argument that is a number is an unsigned 32-bit
// one (pointers, lengths, descriptors, flags), so each import takes them as such (the 64-bit ones are BigInts and
// keep their sign: a seek's offset).  Only where the memory is 2 GB or more from its start (the window's try,
// host/memory.ts): the runtime steps past 2 GB only with the window on (runtime/web/sbrk.c).  Elsewhere the imports
// are taken as they are: the wrapper's two arrays a call filled WebKit's heap (an iPhone's Quick Race in WebKit:
// 1.3 GB without them, 6 GB with them, and growing).
type Fn = (...a: any[]) => any;

function unsignedAll(o: Record<string, Fn>, keep: string[] = []): Record<string, Fn> {

    fd_pread: (fd: number, iov: number, n: number, off: bigint, pr: number) => io(Op.FdPread, fd, iov, n, off, pr),

      return io(Op.FdFdstatGet, fd, p);
    },

// The page keeps a few workers idle beyond the threads running (process.ts) and starts more as threads take them.  A
// thread that finds none idle all the same asks for one and waits for it, as a slow CreateThread would (a worker takes
// ~50 ms to start; at most 10 s here).
const SPAWN_WAIT_MS = 10_000;
function threadSpawn(arg: number): number {
  const t = Atomics.add(ctl, CTL_NEXT_TID, 1), t0 = performance.now();
  for (let asked = false; ;) {
    const ready = Atomics.load(ctl, CTL_POOL_READY);
    for (let s = 0; s < POOL; s++) {
      const i = CTL_POOL + 4 * s;
      if (Atomics.compareExchange(ctl, i, POOL_IDLE, 1) === POOL_IDLE) {   // claim the slot
        ctl[i + 1] = t; ctl[i + 2] = arg;
        Atomics.store(ctl, i, 2); Atomics.notify(ctl, i);
        post({ t: 'pool' });
        if (asked) post({ t: 'log', s: `thread-spawn: thread ${t} waited ${(performance.now() - t0).toFixed(0)} ms for a pool worker`, fd: 2, tid });
        return t;
      }
    }
    const left = SPAWN_WAIT_MS - (performance.now() - t0);
    if (left <= 0) break;
    if (!asked) { asked = true; post({ t: 'pool' }); }
    Atomics.wait(ctl, CTL_POOL_READY, ready, left);
  }
  post({ t: 'log', s: `thread-spawn: no pool worker for thread ${t} within ${SPAWN_WAIT_MS / 1000} s (at most ${POOL})`, fd: 2, tid });
  return -6; // EAGAIN
}

// Engine call depth (runtime/web/stackprobe.c, NFSU2_STACKPROBE): the number
// of frames on this thread's stack (wasm and JS: every lifted guest call is a
// wasm frame), from a stack trace.  Bytes would be the better measure, but a
// recursion probe is not stable in Chrome (the same context fit 4536 to 7352
// frames of an interpreted probe function), and frame sizes are not exposed.
const V8Error = Error as ErrorConstructor & { stackTraceLimit: number };   // V8's knob
// A trap's stack (the 'trap' message below, "TRAP in thread" in the log) keeps this many frames: V8's default of
// 10 cut the lifted guest calls off before the caller that mattered.
V8Error.stackTraceLimit = 100;
function stackFrames(): number {
  const lim = V8Error.stackTraceLimit;
  V8Error.stackTraceLimit = 1e6;
  const n = (new Error().stack ?? '').split('\n').length - 2;   // minus the message line and this function
  V8Error.stackTraceLimit = lim;
  return n;
}

// Host imports the runtime may call by name ("nfsu2" module).  The page adds
// subsystems (gpu, audio, input, net) by registering shared-memory addresses.
function hostImports(): Record<string, (...a: any[]) => any> {
  return {
    // nfsu2_host_register(kind, ptr, size): tells the page where a shared structure lives
    // (with the memory's size now: a page that holds a buffer of a smaller one waits for the grown one, host/process.ts)
    register: (kind: number, ptr: number, size: number) => { me.postMessage({ t: 'register', kind, ptr, size, bytes: memory.buffer.byteLength }); return 0; },
    // milliseconds since the page's time origin (same clock in every worker)
    now_ms: () => T0MS + performance.now(),
    // ms this thread has spent blocked in host waits (I/O, sleeps) so far
    blocked_ms: () => blockedMs,
    stack_frames: () => stackFrames(),
    // the movies' AV1 pictures, decoded by the I/O worker (movie.ts, runtime/movie.c)
    movie_open: (w: number, h: number) => io(Op.MovieOpen, w, h),
    movie_decode: (m: number, p: number, n: number, y: number, u: number, v: number, ys: number, uvs: number) =>
      io(Op.MovieDecode, m, p, n, y, u, v, ys, uvs),
    movie_close: (m: number) => io(Op.MovieClose, m),
  };
}

onmessage = async (e: MessageEvent<Init | { t: 'memory' }>) => {
  if ('t' in e.data) return;                 // the Memory through the page (memoryFrom)
  const m = e.data;
  ctl = new Int32Array(m.ctl); slot = m.slot; POOL = m.pool; cfg = m.cfg;
  memory = m.memory ?? await memoryFrom(m.memPort!, slot);
  rpcI32 = new Int32Array(m.rpc); rpcI64 = new BigInt64Array(m.rpc);
  const imports: WebAssembly.Imports = {
    env: { memory },
    wasi_snapshot_preview1: unsignedAll(wasi(), ['proc_exit']),
    wasi: { 'thread-spawn': threadSpawn },
    nfsu2: unsignedAll(hostImports()),
  };
  // stub any import the module wants that we do not provide, loudly
  for (const im of WebAssembly.Module.imports(m.mod)) {
    const ns = (imports[im.module] ??= {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
    if (im.kind === 'function' && !(im.name in ns))
      ns[im.name] = (...a: unknown[]) => { post({ t: 'log', s: `unimplemented import ${im.module}.${im.name}(${a.join(',')})`, fd: 2, tid }); return E.NOSYS; };
  }
  const inst = await WebAssembly.instantiate(m.mod, imports);
  const ex = inst.exports as Record<string, any>;
  alignClock(); blockedMs = 0;
  const i = CTL_POOL + 4 * slot;
  // ready: a thread may take this slot now (one waiting in threadSpawn is woken)
  Atomics.compareExchange(ctl, i, POOL_NONE, POOL_IDLE);
  Atomics.add(ctl, CTL_POOL_READY, 1); Atomics.notify(ctl, CTL_POOL_READY);
  post({ t: 'ready', slot });
  for (;;) {
    let st: number;
    while ((st = Atomics.load(ctl, i)) === POOL_IDLE || st === 1) Atomics.wait(ctl, i, st);
    try {
      if (st === POOL_RUN_MAIN) {
        tid = 0;
        try { ex._start(); Atomics.store(ctl, CTL_EXIT_CODE, 0); }
        catch (x) { if (x instanceof ProcExit) Atomics.store(ctl, CTL_EXIT_CODE, x.code); else throw x; }
        Atomics.store(ctl, CTL_EXIT, 1); Atomics.notify(ctl, CTL_EXIT);
        post({ t: 'exit', code: ctl[CTL_EXIT_CODE] });
        return;
      }
      tid = ctl[i + 1];
      try { ex.wasi_thread_start(tid, ctl[i + 2]); }
      catch (x) {
        if (x instanceof ProcExit) { Atomics.store(ctl, CTL_EXIT_CODE, x.code); Atomics.store(ctl, CTL_EXIT, 1); post({ t: 'exit', code: x.code }); return; }
        throw x;
      }
    } catch (x: any) {
      post({ t: 'trap', tid, msg: String(x), stack: x?.stack });
      // a trap in any thread takes the process down, as an unhandled fault would on Windows
      Atomics.store(ctl, CTL_EXIT_CODE, 134); Atomics.store(ctl, CTL_EXIT, 1); post({ t: 'exit', code: 134 });
      return;
    }
    Atomics.store(ctl, i, POOL_IDLE);
  }
};
void MAX_THREADS;

// The I/O worker: the process's file system.  Game threads post WASI file
// calls into their RPC slot and block; this worker serves them asynchronously
// (so a slow read for one thread never holds up another) and writes results
// straight into the shared wasm memory.
//
// Mounts (preopened directories, in this order: fd 3, fd 4):
//   /data  the NFSU2 install folder on the local server, read-only.  Read in
//          1 MiB blocks (compressed from a server that offers it, else
//          HTTP range requests), kept in memory, and
//          persisted in OPFS ("cache/", datacache.ts) so the next launch reads
//          locally ("Preload the game data" fills all of it ahead).
//   /save  the save overlay: OPFS directory, read/write (saves, registry,
//          settings.ini, logs).  Closing a file the game wrote there tells
//          the page ({ t: 'saved', path }: "Progress saved", F9's last save).

} from './proto';

// The memory, or the sizes to try for it where the page holds its buffer only (WebKit, memory.ts): then this worker

// each new buffer as the memory grows (memGrew)
