// The movies' pictures in AV1 (tools/movies_av1.py): the game's own movie player reads an AV1 movie as it reads a
// VP6 one, and runtime/movie.c hands each AV1 frame to the I/O worker (Op.MovieDecode), which decodes it here with
// a WebCodecs VideoDecoder and writes the picture into the game's memory, in the planes its VP6 decoder would have
// filled.  The game thread waits for that (one frame: under 1 ms at the median, ~10 at worst, in Chrome and
// Firefox with the software decoder); the I/O worker goes on serving the other threads' reads meanwhile.
//
// Where a browser decodes AV1, the page plays MOVIES/AV1/<name>.vp6 in place of MOVIES/<name>.vp6 (io-worker.ts
// dataFile, datacache.ts av1Path); elsewhere the VP6 movies play as they always have.  NFSU2_MOVIE_CODEC = vp6 (a
// settings.ini line, or &env= on the test pages) keeps the VP6 ones in any browser.
import type { GameMemory } from './memory';

/** profile 0, level 3.0 (768x512 at 30 fps, the game's movies), 8 bits */
export const AV1_CODEC = 'av01.0.04M.08';
/** the picture of one frame, at most this long (then the frame before stays on screen) */
const WAIT_MS = 250;

export type MovieCodec = 'av1' | 'vp6';

/** Which movies this browser plays: AV1 where its VideoDecoder takes AV1 (Chrome and Firefox with their software
 *  decoder, the same in a worker as here; Safari where the Mac or iPhone decodes AV1 in hardware: it says yes to the
 *  software preference too), else VP6 (Safari on the others). */
export async function movieCodec(env: Record<string, string> = {}): Promise<MovieCodec> {
  const forced = env.NFSU2_MOVIE_CODEC?.trim().toLowerCase();
  if (forced === 'vp6' || forced === 'av1') return forced;
  try {
    if (typeof VideoDecoder === 'undefined') return 'vp6';
    return (await VideoDecoder.isConfigSupported(config(768, 512))).supported ? 'av1' : 'vp6';
  } catch { return 'vp6'; }
}

function config(w: number, h: number): VideoDecoderConfig {
  // the software decoder: every frame's picture comes out as its chunk goes in (optimizeForLatency; without it
  // Chrome and Firefox hold 2-3 frames back), in I420 in Chrome and BGRX in Firefox; Firefox's hardware decoder
  // left some frames out. Safari's hardware decoder gives each picture at once too, in NV12 (Safari 27, M4 Mac).
  return { codec: AV1_CODEC, codedWidth: w, codedHeight: h, hardwareAcceleration: 'prefer-software', optimizeForLatency: true };
}

interface Movie {
  w: number; h: number;
  dec: VideoDecoder | null;
  seq: number;                      // the timestamp of the last chunk sent
  key: boolean;                     // the decoder needs a key frame next (new, or after an error)
  frame: VideoFrame | null;         // the picture of chunk seq, once out
  wake: (() => void) | null;
  error: string;
  tmp: Uint8Array | null;           // for the pictures that need converting (NV12, RGB)
}
const movies = new Map<number, Movie>();
let nextId = 1;
/** runtime/movie.c HANDLE: 'MV' in the top half, so that a page without these imports (its stub's errno) is no handle */
const TAG = 0x4d560000;

function start(m: Movie) {
  m.dec = new VideoDecoder({
    output: f => {
      if (f.timestamp !== m.seq || m.frame) { f.close(); return; }    // a late one, for a chunk given up on
      m.frame = f; m.wake?.();
    },
    error: e => { m.error = String(e); m.dec = null; m.key = true; m.wake?.(); },
  });
  m.dec.configure(config(m.w, m.h));
  m.key = true;
}

export function movieOpen(w: number, h: number): number {
  const id = TAG | (nextId++ & 0xffff);
  const m: Movie = { w, h, dec: null, seq: 0, key: true, frame: null, wake: null, error: '', tmp: null };
  try { start(m); } catch { return -1; }
  movies.set(id, m);
  return id;
}

export function movieClose(id: number) {
  const m = movies.get(id);
  if (!m) return;
  movies.delete(id);
  m.frame?.close();
  try { m.dec?.close(); } catch { /* closed by an error */ }
}

/** One AV1 frame (the chunk's payload: 'AV01', flags, 3 bytes, the temporal unit) into the planes y, u, v of the
 *  game's memory (strides ys, uvs).  0: the picture is there; 1: none came (the last one stays). */
export async function movieDecode(memory: GameMemory, id: number, payload: number, len: number,
    y: number, u: number, v: number, ys: number, uvs: number, log: (s: string) => void): Promise<number> {
  const m = movies.get(id);
  if (!m || len < 8) return 1;
  const head = new Uint8Array(memory.buffer, payload, 8), key = (head[4] & 1) !== 0;
  if (!m.dec) {
    if (!key) return 1;                                            // after an error: from the next key frame on
    try { start(m); } catch { return 1; }
  }
  if (m.key && !key) return 1;
  m.frame?.close(); m.frame = null; m.error = '';
  m.seq++;
  // the chunk takes its own copy (the guest's memory is shared)
  const data = new Uint8Array(memory.buffer, payload + 8, len - 8).slice();
  try { m.dec!.decode(new EncodedVideoChunk({ type: key ? 'key' : 'delta', timestamp: m.seq, data })); }
  catch (e) {
    log(`[movie] decode refused: ${e}`);
    try { m.dec?.close(); } catch { /* closed already */ }
    m.dec = null; return 1;
  }
  m.key = false;
  if (!m.frame) {
    let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
    await new Promise<void>(r => { m.wake = r; timer = setTimeout(r, WAIT_MS); });
    clearTimeout(timer); m.wake = null;
  }
  if (m.error) log(`[movie] decoder error: ${m.error}`);
  const f = m.frame as VideoFrame | null;     // set by the output callback meanwhile
  if (!f) return 1;
  m.frame = null;
  try { await put(memory, m, f, y, u, v, ys, uvs); return 0; }
  catch (e) { log(`[movie] picture not copied (${f.format}): ${e}`); return 1; }
  finally { f.close(); }
}

async function put(memory: GameMemory, m: Movie, f: VideoFrame, y: number, u: number, v: number, ys: number, uvs: number) {
  const w = Math.min(m.w, f.visibleRect?.width ?? m.w) & ~1, h = Math.min(m.h, f.visibleRect?.height ?? m.h) & ~1;
  const rect = { x: f.visibleRect?.x ?? 0, y: f.visibleRect?.y ?? 0, width: w, height: h };
  const span = v - y + uvs * (h / 2);
  if (f.format === 'I420') {
    const layout = [{ offset: 0, stride: ys }, { offset: u - y, stride: uvs }, { offset: v - y, stride: uvs }];
    try { await f.copyTo(new Uint8Array(memory.buffer, y, span), { rect, layout }); return; }
    catch { /* a browser that copies into no shared memory: through a copy of its own */ }
    const t = tmp(m, span);
    await f.copyTo(t, { rect, layout });
    new Uint8Array(memory.buffer, y, span).set(t.subarray(0, span));
    return;
  }
  const mem = new Uint8Array(memory.buffer);
  if (f.format === 'NV12') {
    const t = tmp(m, w * h * 3 / 2);
    await f.copyTo(t, { rect, layout: [{ offset: 0, stride: w }, { offset: w * h, stride: w }] });
    for (let r = 0; r < h; r++) mem.set(t.subarray(r * w, r * w + w), y + r * ys);
    for (let r = 0, o = w * h; r < h / 2; r++) {
      const du = u + r * uvs, dvv = v + r * uvs;
      for (let c = 0; c < w / 2; c++, o += 2) { mem[du + c] = t[o]; mem[dvv + c] = t[o + 1]; }
    }
    return;
  }
  // RGB (Firefox gives its pictures as BGRX), or anything else as RGBX: back to the YUV the frame was made from,
  // by its own matrix (limited range)
  const rgb = f.format === 'RGBX' || f.format === 'RGBA' || f.format === 'BGRX' || f.format === 'BGRA';
  const t = tmp(m, w * h * 4);
  await f.copyTo(t, rgb ? { rect, layout: [{ offset: 0, stride: w * 4 }] } : { rect, layout: [{ offset: 0, stride: w * 4 }], format: 'RGBX' } as VideoFrameCopyToOptions);
  const bgr = f.format === 'BGRX' || f.format === 'BGRA';
  const mat = f.colorSpace?.matrix;
  const kr = mat === 'bt470bg' || mat === 'smpte170m' ? 0.299 : 0.2126, kb = mat === 'bt470bg' || mat === 'smpte170m' ? 0.114 : 0.0722;
  toI420(t, w, h, bgr, kr, kb, mem, y, u, v, ys, uvs);
}

function tmp(m: Movie, n: number) {
  if (!m.tmp || m.tmp.length < n) m.tmp = new Uint8Array(n);
  return m.tmp;
}

/** RGB(X) pixels (BGRX if bgr) -> limited-range Y'CbCr 4:2:0 by the matrix of Kr and Kb, chroma from each 2x2's mean */
export function toI420(t: Uint8Array, w: number, h: number, bgr: boolean, kr: number, kb: number,
    mem: Uint8Array, y: number, u: number, v: number, ys: number, uvs: number) {
  const kg = 1 - kr - kb, sy = 219 / 255, sb = 224 / 255 / (2 * (1 - kb)) / 4, sr = 224 / 255 / (2 * (1 - kr)) / 4;
  const yr = sy * kr, yg = sy * kg, yb = sy * kb, ri = bgr ? 2 : 0, bi = bgr ? 0 : 2, row = w * 4;
  for (let r = 0; r < h; r += 2) {
    let o = r * row, d = y + r * ys, cu = u + (r >> 1) * uvs, cv = v + (r >> 1) * uvs;
    for (let c = 0; c < w; c += 2, o += 8, d += 2) {
      // a 2x2 block: its four lumas, and the chroma of its sums (Uint8Array stores clamp nothing: Y stays in
      // 16..235 by the matrix, the chroma is clamped below)
      const r0 = t[o + ri], g0 = t[o + 1], b0 = t[o + bi], r1 = t[o + 4 + ri], g1 = t[o + 5], b1 = t[o + 4 + bi];
      const r2 = t[o + row + ri], g2 = t[o + row + 1], b2 = t[o + row + bi];
      const r3 = t[o + row + 4 + ri], g3 = t[o + row + 5], b3 = t[o + row + 4 + bi];
      mem[d] = 16.5 + yr * r0 + yg * g0 + yb * b0; mem[d + 1] = 16.5 + yr * r1 + yg * g1 + yb * b1;
      mem[d + ys] = 16.5 + yr * r2 + yg * g2 + yb * b2; mem[d + ys + 1] = 16.5 + yr * r3 + yg * g3 + yb * b3;
      const R = r0 + r1 + r2 + r3, G = g0 + g1 + g2 + g3, B = b0 + b1 + b2 + b3, Y = kr * R + kg * G + kb * B;
      const cb = 128.5 + sb * (B - Y), cr = 128.5 + sr * (R - Y);
      mem[cu++] = cb < 0 ? 0 : cb > 255 ? 255 : cb;
      mem[cv++] = cr < 0 ? 0 : cr > 255 ? 255 : cr;
    }
  }
}

// The predownload worker: the install folder but the movies (datacache.ts
// aheadFiles) into the game data cache ahead of play, so a game never waits
// on the network for its data.  Blocks come compressed, one a request, at the
// game's own addresses, which Cloudflare can keep.  The page starts it ("Download all game data")
// and stops it before a game starts, since the I/O worker writes the same files.
//
// Page -> worker: { t: 'start', manifestUrl, language, packs }, { t: 'stop' }
// Worker -> page: { t: 'progress', have, total }   (bytes in the cache; at most every 250 ms)
//                 { t: 'done', have, total }       (all of it is in the cache)
//                 { t: 'stopped' }                 (after 'stop')
//                 { t: 'error', msg }
// Every file is closed before 'done', 'stopped' or 'error'.  What was written
// stays: a stopped or failed download goes on from there the next time.
import {
  BLOCK, CACHE_DIR, aheadFiles, blockCount, blockLen, blockRuns, manifestFiles, openCacheFile, putBlock, runUrl, scanCache,
  type CacheFile, type DataFile, type Manifest, type Packs,
} from './datacache';
import { fmtBytes } from '../app/checks';

export type ToPredownload = { t: 'start'; manifestUrl: string; language: string; packs: Packs } | { t: 'stop' };
export type FromPredownload =
  | { t: 'progress' | 'done'; have: number; total: number }
  | { t: 'stopped' } | { t: 'error'; msg: string };

// Requests at once (over HTTP/1.1 Chrome holds 6 connections to a server: the page keeps the rest), one block a
// request, at the address the game's own reads use (datacache.ts runUrl), so one copy in Cloudflare's cache serves
// both.
const LANES = 4;
const ATTEMPTS = 8;

const post = (m: FromPredownload) => (self as unknown as Worker).postMessage(m);
const abort = new AbortController();
let stopping = false;

/** a request's blocks, [first, end) of a file: all missing when it was queued */
interface Run { f: DataFile; first: number; end: number; file: Shared }
/** a file's cache file, open while runs of it are left */
interface Shared { cf: Promise<CacheFile> | null; runs: number }

class Retry extends Error {}

function closeFile(cf: CacheFile | null) { if (cf) { cf.h.flush(); cf.h.close(); cf.haveH.flush(); cf.haveH.close(); } }

async function download(cfg: { manifestUrl: string; language: string; packs: Packs }): Promise<{ have: number; total: number } | null> {
  const r = await fetch(cfg.manifestUrl, { cache: 'no-cache', signal: abort.signal });
  if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`the list of game files did not load (HTTP ${r.status})`);
  const m = await r.json() as Manifest;
  const served = blockRuns(m);
  const scan = await scanCache(aheadFiles(manifestFiles(m), cfg.language, cfg.packs));
  const total = scan.total;
  let have = scan.have, shown = 0;
  const progress = (now = false) => {
    const t = performance.now();
    if (now || t - shown >= 250) { shown = t; post({ t: 'progress', have, total }); }
  };
  progress(true);
  if (have >= total) return { have, total };
  // room for the rest: what the cache files do not take yet
  const need = total - scan.allocated;
  const room = await navigator.storage.estimate()
    .then(e => e.quota !== undefined && e.usage !== undefined ? e.quota - e.usage : Infinity, () => Infinity);
  if (room < need) throw new Error(`there is not enough room: the rest needs ${fmtBytes(need)}, and the browser lets this page store ${fmtBytes(Math.max(0, room))} more. Free some disk space and try again`);

  const dir = await (await navigator.storage.getDirectory()).getDirectoryHandle(CACHE_DIR, { create: true });
  const runs: Run[] = [];
  for (const { f, have: m } of scan.files) {
    const file: Shared = { cf: null, runs: 0 };
    for (let bi = 0; bi < blockCount(f.size); bi++) {
      if (m?.[bi]) continue;
      runs.push({ f, first: bi, end: bi + 1, file }); file.runs++;
    }
  }
  const open = new Set<Promise<CacheFile>>();
  async function release(s: Shared) {
    if (--s.runs || !s.cf) return;
    const p = s.cf; s.cf = null; open.delete(p);
    closeFile(await p.catch(() => null));
  }

  // a run's blocks as they arrive, each written and marked once it is whole
  async function fetchRun(run: Run, cf: CacheFile) {
    let first = run.first;
    while (first < run.end && cf.have[first]) first++;
    if (first === run.end) return;
    const start = first * BLOCK, end = Math.min(run.f.size, run.end * BLOCK);
    // compressed (the browser undoes the Content-Encoding)
    const res = await fetch(runUrl(served.url, run.f.path, first, run.end - first, run.f), { cache: 'no-store', signal: abort.signal });
    if (res.status === 429 || res.status >= 500) { await res.body?.cancel(); throw new Retry(`HTTP ${res.status}`); }
    if (res.status !== 200) throw new Error(`the server answered HTTP ${res.status} for ${run.f.path}`);
    let at = start;
    const buf = new Uint8Array(BLOCK);
    let fill = 0;
    const rd = res.body!.getReader();
    for (;;) {
      const { done, value } = await rd.read();
      if (done) break;
      for (let o = 0; o < value.length; ) {
        const bi = at / BLOCK, len = blockLen(run.f.size, bi), k = Math.min(len - fill, value.length - o);
        buf.set(value.subarray(o, o + k), fill); fill += k; o += k;
        if (fill < len) continue;
        if (!cf.have[bi]) { putBlock(cf, bi, buf.subarray(0, len)); have += len; progress(); }
        at += len; fill = 0;
        if (at >= end) { await rd.cancel(); return; }
      }
    }
    throw new Retry(`${run.f.path} ended early`);
  }

  let next = 0, failed: unknown = null;
  async function lane() {
    while (!abort.signal.aborted && next < runs.length) {
      const run = runs[next++];
      try {
        if (!run.file.cf) { run.file.cf = openCacheFile(dir, run.f); open.add(run.file.cf); }
        const cf = await run.file.cf;
        for (let attempt = 1, wait = 500; ; attempt++, wait = Math.min(wait * 2, 8000)) {
          try { await fetchRun(run, cf); break; }
          catch (e) {
            // a busy server, a dropped connection, a body cut short: again, from its first block still missing
            if (abort.signal.aborted || attempt >= ATTEMPTS || !(e instanceof Retry || e instanceof TypeError)) throw e;
            await new Promise(res => setTimeout(res, wait));
          }
        }
      } catch (e) { if (!abort.signal.aborted) { failed = e; abort.abort(); } }
      finally { await release(run.file); }
    }
  }
  await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: LANES }, lane));
  // files whose later runs were never taken (a stop, a failure)
  for (const p of open) closeFile(await p.catch(() => null));
  if (failed) throw failed;
  progress(true);
  return stopping ? null : { have, total };
}

function why(e: unknown): string {
  if (e instanceof DOMException && e.name === 'QuotaExceededError') return 'the browser has no more room for it. Free some disk space and try again';
  if (e instanceof TypeError) return 'the server stopped answering. Try again';
  if (e instanceof Retry) return `the server stopped answering (${e.message}). Try again`;
  return e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e);
}

let started = false;
onmessage = (e: MessageEvent<ToPredownload>) => {
  if (e.data.t === 'stop') { stopping = true; abort.abort(); return; }
  if (started) return;
  started = true;
  download(e.data).then(
    r => post(r ? { t: 'done', ...r } : { t: 'stopped' }),
    err => post(stopping ? { t: 'stopped' } : { t: 'error', msg: why(err) }),
  );
};

// Starting the game process from the page: the shared memory, the control
// and RPC blocks, the I/O worker and a pool of game-thread workers.
import { CTL_EXIT, CTL_INTS, CTL_NEXT_TID, CTL_POOL, MAX_THREADS, POOL_IDLE, POOL_NONE, POOL_RUN_MAIN, RPC_BYTES, type BootConfig, type ReadAnswer, type ReadAsk, type ToPage } from './proto';
import { tzEnv } from './tz';
import { movieCodec } from './movie';
import { allocMemory, memoryOffPage, memoryTries, MemoryBuffer, type GameMemory } from './memory';

export interface ProcessOptions {
  module: WebAssembly.Module;
  cfg: BootConfig;
  pool?: number;                         // game-thread workers at most (started as threads need them; default 24)
  poolStart?: number;                    // ... and at first (default POOL_START)
  initialPages?: number;                 // wasm pages (64 KiB) of the shared memory at start
  /** the page holds the memory's buffer only, not the WebAssembly.Memory (memory.ts; default: in WebKit) */
  memoryOffPage?: boolean;
  onLog?: (s: string, fd: number, tid: number) => void;
  onExit?: (code: number) => void;
  onRegister?: (kind: number, ptr: number, size: number) => void;
  /** the game closed a file of the save overlay it had written (a profile, registry.txt ...), path relative to /save */
  onSaved?: (path: string) => void;
  /** a line of the host's own for the log, from no game thread (the I/O worker's "[data] ...") */
  onNote?: (s: string) => void;
  /** the browser deleted the save folder during the game, and the I/O worker made an empty one: the saves back into
   *  it, before the game's next save there (the I/O worker holds every save call until this resolves, 12 s at most) */
  onSaveGone?: () => Promise<void>;
  /** the game deleted a file of the save overlay: a profile's (its own Delete), path relative to /save */
  onRemoved?: (path: string) => void;
  /** a file the game wrote as the browser deleted the save folder could not be kept (path relative to /save) */
  onLost?: (path: string) => void;
  /** a file of the save overlay the browser would not open or make, the folder still there (the first of a game: its
   *  error, as "Name: message"); its saves may not be kept */
  onSaveTrouble?: (error: string) => void;
}

export interface GameProcess {
  /** the WebAssembly.Memory, or in WebKit its buffer only (memory.ts MemoryBuffer: the newest as it grows) */
  memory: GameMemory;
  /** f gets each new buffer of the memory as it grows, where the page holds the buffer only (the network's worker) */
  onGrow(f: (buf: SharedArrayBuffer) => void): void;
  ctl: Int32Array;
  exited: Promise<number>;
  terminate(): void;
  /** resolves with the structure a subsystem published (runtime/web/host_abi.h) */
  registered(kind: number): Promise<{ ptr: number; size: number }>;
  /** bytes [off, off + len) of a game-folder file, through the game data's cache (the I/O worker); exact: those bytes
   *  alone from the server, not kept */
  readData(path: string, off: number, len: number, exact?: boolean): Promise<Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>>;
}

function memoryPagesOf(mod: WebAssembly.Module): number | null {
  // the module imports env.memory; its declared minimum is not exposed by the
  // JS API, so the build writes it into a custom section "nfsu2.mem"
  const s = WebAssembly.Module.customSections(mod, 'nfsu2.mem');
  return s.length ? new DataView(s[0]).getUint32(0, true) : null;
}

/** Game-thread workers: POOL_START at first, then as threads take them so that POOL_SPARE stay idle, up to the pool's
 *  size (a thread start that finds none idle waits for the next: game-worker.ts threadSpawn).  Each takes memory, a
 *  phone's: a race or free roam starts 15 (at most 13 threads at once), hosting a LAN game 18, and all 24 at once held
 *  ~55 MB more of WebKit's page process.  12 at first, fewer than any game ends with: its first second starts 10
 *  threads, and with 8 or 10 workers at first the 10th waited up to 15 ms for one. */
const POOL_START = 12, POOL_SPARE = 2;
/** how long the I/O worker may take to say it is ready (startProcess) */
const IO_START_MS = 45_000;
/** ... and the first pool of game workers after it */
const POOL_START_MS = 45_000;

export async function startProcess(o: ProcessOptions): Promise<GameProcess> {
  const pool = Math.min(o.pool ?? 24, MAX_THREADS);
  // the page's time zone (WASI has none); an explicit NFSU2_TZ in the config wins
  const cfg: BootConfig = { ...o.cfg, env: { ...tzEnv(), ...o.cfg.env } };
  // which movies the I/O worker opens (the page decides before the game starts: shell.ts; a test page here)
  cfg.env.NFSU2_MOVIE_CODEC = await movieCodec(cfg.env);
  const initial = o.initialPages ?? memoryPagesOf(o.module) ?? 16384;
  // the build's size, able to grow to 4 GB, or not growing where the browser refuses that (memory.ts); on a computer
  // 2 GB first, for the guest heap's window (NFSU2_HEAP_WINDOW=1: app/shell.ts, or a test page's env); the log says which
  const tries = memoryTries(initial, cfg.env.NFSU2_HEAP_WINDOW === '1');
  // In WebKit the page holds the memory's buffer only (memory.ts): the I/O worker makes the Memory and sends the page
  // its buffer, and each game thread gets the Memory from there on a port (withMemoryPort).  `kept`: the page's own
  // Memory elsewhere, made here as before
  const offPage = o.memoryOffPage ?? memoryOffPage();
  let kept: WebAssembly.Memory | null = null;
  if (!offPage) {
    let got: ReturnType<typeof allocMemory>;
    try { got = allocMemory(tries); }
    catch (e) { const n = (e as { note?: string } | null)?.note; if (n) o.onNote?.(n); throw e; }
    o.onNote?.(got.note);
    kept = got.memory;
  }
  let memory: GameMemory | null = kept;
  const growers: ((buf: SharedArrayBuffer) => void)[] = [];
  const ctlBuf = new SharedArrayBuffer(CTL_INTS * 4), rpc = new SharedArrayBuffer(RPC_BYTES);
  const ctl = new Int32Array(ctlBuf);
  ctl[CTL_NEXT_TID] = 1;

  const regs = new Map<number, { ptr: number; size: number }>();
  const regWaiters = new Map<number, ((r: { ptr: number; size: number }) => void)[]>();
  let resolveExit!: (c: number) => void;
  const exited = new Promise<number>(r => (resolveExit = r));
  const workers: Worker[] = [];
  const onMsg = (e: MessageEvent<ToPage | { t: 'register'; kind: number; ptr: number; size: number; bytes?: number }>) => {
    const m = e.data;
    if (m.t === 'log') o.onLog?.(m.s, m.fd, m.tid);
    else if (m.t === 'trap') o.onLog?.(`TRAP in thread ${m.tid}: ${m.msg}\n${m.stack ?? ''}`, 2, m.tid);
    else if (m.t === 'pool') topUp();
    else if (m.t === 'memory-please') {
      if (!viaPage) { viaPage = true; o.onNote?.(`[memory] game worker ${m.slot}: ${m.why}; the game threads get it through the page`); }
      io.postMessage({ t: 'give-page', slot: m.slot });
    }
    else if (m.t === 'exit') {
      o.onNote?.(`[pool] ${started} game workers started, at most ${mostBusy} threads at once`);
      o.onExit?.(m.code); resolveExit(m.code);
    }
    else if (m.t === 'register') {
      const done = () => {
        regs.set(m.kind, { ptr: m.ptr, size: m.size });
        for (const w of regWaiters.get(m.kind) ?? []) w({ ptr: m.ptr, size: m.size });
        regWaiters.delete(m.kind);
        o.onRegister?.(m.kind, m.ptr, m.size);
      };
      // a structure (and what its subsystem made before it) in memory grown since the page's buffer: once the I/O worker
      // sent the new buffer (memory.ts), not before, or the page reads past its buffer
      const need = m.bytes ?? 0;
      const buf = memory;
      if (buf instanceof MemoryBuffer && need > buf.buffer.byteLength) void buf.until(need).then(ok => {
        if (!ok) o.onNote?.(`[memory] a grown memory's buffer did not come in time (${Math.round(need / 1048576)} MB)`);
        done();
      });
      else done();
    }
  };

  const io = new Worker(new URL('/host/io-worker.js', import.meta.url), { type: 'module', name: 'io' });
  workers.push(io);
  // Ready in IO_START_MS at most (the game data's list from the server, the save folder from the browser's storage): one
  // that never answers is a game that does not start, said so, never a black stage for good.
  await new Promise<void>((res, rej) => {
    const late = setTimeout(() => {
      io.terminate();
      rej(new Error(`the game's files did not open in ${IO_START_MS / 1000} s (the browser's storage or the network did not answer)`));
    }, IO_START_MS);
    // (its lines as it starts too: playing without saving, what it copied into memory)
    io.onmessage = (e) => {
      if (e.data.t === 'io-ready') { clearTimeout(late); res(); }

      else if (e.data.t === 'memory') { memory = new MemoryBuffer(e.data.buf); o.onNote?.(e.data.note); }
      else if (e.data.t === 'io-error') {

        io.terminate();                      // (and with it a memory it made)

        rej(e.data.range ? new RangeError(e.data.msg) : new Error(e.data.msg));
      }
      else if (e.data.t === 'log') o.onNote?.(e.data.s);
    };
    io.postMessage(offPage ? { tries, ctl: ctlBuf, rpc, cfg } : { memory: kept, ctl: ctlBuf, rpc, cfg });
  });

  const mem: GameMemory = memory;
  const reads = new Map<number, { res: (b: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>) => void; rej: (e: Error) => void }>();
  let readId = 0;
  io.onmessage = (e) => {
    if (e.data.t === 'read') {
      const a = e.data as ReadAnswer, r = reads.get(a.id);
      reads.delete(a.id);
      if (r) { if (a.bytes) r.res(a.bytes); else r.rej(new Error(a.error ?? 'no bytes')); }
    }
    else if (e.data.t === 'saved') o.onSaved?.(e.data.path);
    else if (e.data.t === 'removed') o.onRemoved?.(e.data.path);
    else if (e.data.t === 'lost') o.onLost?.(e.data.path);
    else if (e.data.t === 'save-trouble') o.onSaveTrouble?.(e.data.error);
    else if (e.data.t === 'log') o.onNote?.(e.data.s);
    // the Memory for a game thread where the I/O worker could not post it on a port (withMemoryPort)
    else if (e.data.t === 'give-here') bySlot.get(e.data.slot)?.postMessage({ t: 'memory', memory: e.data.memory });
    // the memory grew: its new buffer (where the page holds the buffer only)
    else if (e.data.t === 'mem') {
      if (memory instanceof MemoryBuffer && memory.grew(e.data.buf)) {
        for (const f of growers) f(e.data.buf);
        o.onNote?.(`[memory] ${Math.round(e.data.buf.byteLength / 1048576)} MB now (it grew)`);
      }
    }
    else if (e.data.t === 'save-gone')
      void Promise.resolve().then(() => o.onSaveGone?.()).catch(err => o.onNote?.(`[app] the saves could not be put back: ${err}`))
        .finally(() => io.postMessage({ t: 'save-ready' }));
  };

  // the port first to the worker, then its other end to the I/O worker, which posts the Memory on it
  const withMemoryPort = (slot: number, send: (port: MessagePort) => void) => {
    const ch = new MessageChannel();
    send(ch.port2);
    io.postMessage({ t: 'give', port: ch.port1, slot }, [ch.port1]);
  };
  const bySlot = new Map<number, Worker>();
  let viaPage = false;
  for (let s = 0; s < pool; s++) ctl[CTL_POOL + 4 * s] = POOL_NONE;   // each worker makes its slot idle when ready
  let started = 0, starting = 0, mostBusy = 0;
  const startWorker = () => {
    const s = started++, w = new Worker(new URL('/host/game-worker.js', import.meta.url), { type: 'module', name: `game-${s}` });
    starting++;
    const ready = new Promise<void>(res => {
      w.onmessage = (e) => { if (e.data.t === 'ready') { starting--; w.onmessage = onMsg; res(); } else onMsg(e); };
    });
    w.onerror = (e) => o.onNote?.(`[pool] game worker ${s}: ${e.message}`);
    bySlot.set(s, w);
    if (offPage) withMemoryPort(s, port => w.postMessage({ mod: o.module, memPort: port, ctl: ctlBuf, rpc, slot: s, pool, cfg }, [port]));
    else w.postMessage({ mod: o.module, memory: kept, ctl: ctlBuf, rpc, slot: s, pool, cfg });
    workers.push(w);
    return ready;
  };
  // a thread took a worker (or found none): POOL_SPARE idle or starting again
  const topUp = () => {
    let idle = 0;
    for (let s = 0; s < started; s++) if (Atomics.load(ctl, CTL_POOL + 4 * s) === POOL_IDLE) idle++;
    mostBusy = Math.max(mostBusy, started - starting - idle);
    for (let n = idle + starting; n < POOL_SPARE && started < pool; n++) void startWorker();
  };
  // the first pool ready in POOL_START_MS at most: one that never is (a thread whose memory never came) is a game that
  // does not start, said so, never a black stage for good
  let poolLate: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
  try {
    await Promise.race([Promise.all(Array.from({ length: Math.max(1, Math.min(o.poolStart ?? POOL_START, pool)) }, startWorker)),
      new Promise((_, no) => { poolLate = setTimeout(() => no(new Error(`the game's threads did not start in ${POOL_START_MS / 1000} s`)), POOL_START_MS); })]);
  } catch (e) {
    for (const w of workers) w.terminate();
    throw e;
  } finally { clearTimeout(poolLate); }
  // slot 0 runs the process entry
  Atomics.store(ctl, CTL_POOL, POOL_RUN_MAIN); Atomics.notify(ctl, CTL_POOL);

  return {
    memory: mem, ctl, exited,
    onGrow(f) { growers.push(f); },
    registered(kind: number) {
      const r = regs.get(kind);
      if (r) return Promise.resolve(r);
      return new Promise(res => { const l = regWaiters.get(kind) ?? []; l.push(res); regWaiters.set(kind, l); });
    },
    readData(path: string, off: number, len: number, exact?: boolean) {
      return new Promise<Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>>((res, rej) => {
        const id = ++readId;
        reads.set(id, { res, rej });
        io.postMessage({ t: 'read', id, path, off, len, exact } satisfies ReadAsk);
      });
    },
    terminate() { for (const w of workers) w.terminate(); if (!Atomics.load(ctl, CTL_EXIT)) resolveExit(-1); },
  };
}

// Shared layout of the host's control memory (a SharedArrayBuffer separate
// from the wasm memory) and the message types between the page and workers.

export const MAX_THREADS = 64;

// ctl: Int32Array over the control SAB
export const CTL_NEXT_TID = 0;       // next thread id handed out by thread-spawn
export const CTL_IO_DOORBELL = 1;    // bumped by a thread that posted an I/O request
export const CTL_EXIT = 2;           // 1 once the process exited (proc_exit / _start returned)
export const CTL_EXIT_CODE = 3;
export const CTL_SLEEP = 4;          // a word nobody notifies: Atomics.wait on it = sleep
export const CTL_POOL_READY = 5;     // bumped and notified as each pool worker becomes ready (thread-spawn waits on it)
export const CTL_IO_BEAT = 6;        // bumped by the I/O worker's loop (every 50 ms at most): a thread whose request
                                     // goes unanswered tells a stuck request from a stopped worker (game-worker.ts io)
export const CTL_POOL = 64;          // pool slot i: [CTL_POOL + 4*i + 0] state, +1 tid, +2 start arg
// a slot's state: idle (its worker waits for a thread), 1 claimed, 2 running a thread, the process entry, or no worker
// there (yet: the page starts workers as threads need them, process.ts)
export const POOL_IDLE = 0, POOL_RUN_MAIN = -1, POOL_NONE = -2;
export const CTL_INTS = CTL_POOL + 4 * MAX_THREADS + 64;

// rpc: one slot per pool slot (a thread only ever uses its own slot)
//   i32[0] state  (0 idle, 1 posted, 2 taken by the I/O worker, 3 done)
//   i32[1] op     i32[2] result (WASI errno)   i32[3] nargs
//   i64[2..9] args (BigInt64Array index 2 = byte 16)
//   bytes 128..RPC_SLOT: scratch (unused for now; every pointer goes into wasm memory)
export const RPC_SLOT = 256;
export const RPC_BYTES = RPC_SLOT * MAX_THREADS;
export const RPC_IDLE = 0, RPC_POSTED = 1, RPC_TAKEN = 2, RPC_DONE = 3;

  FdClose = 1, FdRead, FdPread, FdWrite, FdPwrite, FdSeek, FdTell, FdSync, FdFdstatGet, FdFdstatSetFlags,

// The page's time zone for the game.  WASI has no zone database, so the C
// runtime's local time would be UTC; instead the page reads the zone from the
// browser and passes it in the environment (runtime/web/tz.c parses it):
//
//   NFSU2_TZ      "<standard name>;<daylight name>;<offset>[;<t>:<offset>]..."
//                 offsets in seconds east of UTC, t = Unix seconds of each
//                 transition (from t on, the offset after it), for the
//                 previous, this and the next year
//   NFSU2_TZ_NAME the IANA name, for the log
//
// The game reads it through GetTimeZoneInformation (the CRT's tzset) and
// FileTimeToLocalFileTime (save-file times).  Plain erasable TypeScript, so
// node can run it too (web/tools/tztest.sh).

/** seconds east of UTC at Unix time t (seconds) */
function offsetAt(t: number): number {
  return -new Date(t * 1000).getTimezoneOffset() * 60;
}

function zoneName(t: number, zone: string | undefined): string {
  try {
    const parts = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { timeZone: zone, timeZoneName: 'long' }).formatToParts(new Date(t * 1000));
    return (parts.find(p => p.type === 'timeZoneName')?.value ?? '').replace(/;/g, ',').slice(0, 31);
  } catch { return ''; }
}

export function tzEnv(now: Date = new Date()): Record<string, string> {
  const y = now.getUTCFullYear();
  const start = Date.UTC(y - 1, 0, 1) / 1000, end = Date.UTC(y + 2, 0, 1) / 1000;
  const trans: [number, number][] = [];
  let prev = offsetAt(start);
  const off0 = prev;
  for (let t = start + 3600; t <= end; t += 3600) {
    const o = offsetAt(t);
    if (o === prev) continue;
    let lo = t - 3600, hi = t;                    // to the second: offsetAt(lo) = prev, offsetAt(hi) = o
    while (hi - lo > 1) { const m = Math.floor((lo + hi) / 2); if (offsetAt(m) === prev) lo = m; else hi = m; }
    trans.push([hi, o]);
    prev = o;
  }
  const offs = [off0, ...trans.map(x => x[1])];
  const std = Math.min(...offs), dst = Math.max(...offs);
  const zone = (() => { try { return Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone; } catch { return undefined; } })();
  // names: from an instant in standard and one in daylight time
  const nowS = Math.floor(now.getTime() / 1000);
  const stdAt = [start, ...trans.map(x => x[0])].find((_t, i) => offs[i] === std) ?? nowS;
  const dstAt = [start, ...trans.map(x => x[0])].find((_t, i) => offs[i] === dst) ?? nowS;
  const stdName = zoneName(stdAt, zone) || 'Standard Time', dstName = dst !== std ? (zoneName(dstAt, zone) || 'Daylight Time') : stdName;
  const spec = [stdName, dstName, String(off0), ...trans.map(([t, o]) => `${t}:${o}`)].join(';');
  return { NFSU2_TZ: spec, ...(zone ? { NFSU2_TZ_NAME: zone } : {}) };
}

{"id": "AT001840", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/web/src/input/altgr.ts", "originalBytes": 4045, "originalSha256": "d79a38346b643ad134bb3571366e5fa113f2493e88e7fbdbec14dc189c7dbae0", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 4045, "utf8TotalBytes": 4045}

// Windows' AltGr (issue 58).  With a keyboard layout that has AltGr (German, French, Turkish, Polish, the Nordic ones
// ...) Windows sends the right Alt key as a Left Ctrl press and then Right Alt, and Chrome passes both on.  The game has
// Shift Down on Left Ctrl and Nitrous on Right Alt, so every nitrous on that key also shifted down; the PC game only
// ever got the nitrous.  Once this browser has shown that it sends that Left Ctrl (a Right Alt as AltGraph right after
// a Left Ctrl press), a Left Ctrl press waits up to WAIT_MS for the next key: Right Alt as AltGraph drops it, any other
// key (or the end of the wait) sends it first.  So on such a layout a Left Ctrl alone reaches the game up to WAIT_MS
// later, and on other layouts nothing changes.  The first AltGr in a browser still shifts down once; localStorage keeps
// what it showed.  Releases always go on: the game ignores the release of a key it does not hold.
import { ALTGR_CTRL, localStore } from '../app/prefs';

/** how long a Left Ctrl press waits for AltGr's Right Alt (Windows sends the two together; this is the margin) */
export const WAIT_MS = 25;
/** a Right Alt as AltGraph this soon after a Left Ctrl press (still down) shows that the browser sends AltGr's Left Ctrl */
const LEARN_MS = 50;

export interface AltGrKey { code: string; key: string; repeat: boolean }
/** where what it learnt is kept (a test gives its own) */
type Store = Pick<Storage, 'getItem' | 'setItem'>;
const kept: Store = { getItem: localStore.get, setItem: localStore.set };

export class AltGrCtrl {
  private held: (() => void) | null = null;
  private timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
  private heldAt = 0;
  private ctrlAt = -Infinity;          // the last Left Ctrl press, while it is down
  private dropped = false;             // AltGr's Left Ctrl was dropped: so are its repeats, until its release
  private seen = false;
  private said = false;

  /** on: Windows (no other system sends AltGr as two keys) */
  constructor(private readonly on: boolean, private readonly log: (s: string) => void,
              private readonly now: () => number = () => performance.now(), private readonly store: Store | null = kept) {
    if (on) try { this.seen = store?.getItem(ALTGR_CTRL) === '1'; } catch { /* no storage: learnt again in this tab */ }
  }

  /** a key's event on its way to the game: send goes now, a little later, or (AltGr's Left Ctrl) never */
  key(e: AltGrKey, down: boolean, send: () => void): void {
    if (!this.on) { send(); return; }
    const altGr = down && e.code === 'AltRight' && e.key === 'AltGraph';
    if (altGr && this.held) {
      const gap = this.now() - this.heldAt;
      this.cancel();
      this.dropped = true;
      if (!this.said) { this.said = true; this.log(`[keys] AltGr: its Left Ctrl (${gap.toFixed(1)} ms before Right Alt) does not reach the game`); }
      send();
      return;
    }
    this.flush();
    if (altGr && !this.seen && this.now() - this.ctrlAt < LEARN_MS) {
      this.seen = true;
      try { this.store?.setItem(ALTGR_CTRL, '1'); } catch { /* kept for this tab only */ }
      this.log('[keys] this browser sends AltGr as Left Ctrl and Right Alt: from now on a Left Ctrl right before Right Alt does not reach the game');
    }
    if (e.code === 'ControlLeft') {
      if (!down) { this.ctrlAt = -Infinity; this.dropped = false; }
      else if (e.repeat) { if (this.dropped) return; }
      else {
        this.ctrlAt = this.now();
        this.dropped = false;
        if (this.seen) {
          this.held = send; this.heldAt = this.ctrlAt;
          this.timer = setTimeout(() => this.flush(), WAIT_MS);
          return;
        }
      }
    }
    send();
  }

  /** a Left Ctrl held back goes to the game now */
  flush(): void {
    const f = this.held;
    this.cancel();
    f?.();
  }

  /** a Left Ctrl held back goes nowhere (the input layer is going) */
  cancel(): void {
    if (this.timer !== null) clearTimeout(this.timer);
    this.timer = null;
    this.held = null;
  }
}

// Game controllers through the Gamepad API, for the game's one virtual pad
// (runtime/gamepad.h, presented to the game as a DirectInput gamepad by
// runtime/dinput_pad.c).
//
// navigator.getGamepads() exists on the page's main thread only, so the page
// polls it every frame and publishes the pad into the HostMailbox under a
// seqlock; the guest reads it when the game polls its device.  Of the
// controllers with the standard mapping and the steering wheels (wheel.ts:
// the wheel, its pedals and buttons made the pad's, and the game offered a
// driving device; an RC radio drives as one), the one the player last
// pressed a button on drives the
// pad, so a controller next to a wheel takes over with a press and the wheel
// takes it back with one of its own.  Before any press, and when that one
// goes away, the first connected of them drives, but a wheel's dead twin
// (deadTwin: a Fanatec base's second collection) never does (one that connects later
// waits for a press), as gamepad.m does; without either the first
// controller is read through its known layout (hidpad.ts: 8BitDo's), or else
// as if it had the standard mapping, but for an axis resting at an end when
// it showed up (a pedal, a throttle, a trigger), which is no stick.  Chrome
// on Android gives every controller the standard mapping's places, called
// standard or not (androidLayout): those are read as they come, but for an
// Xbox One S with its 2016 firmware's id, which Chrome maps wrong there
// (hidpad.ts oneS2016Android).  Chrome
// exposes a controller only after a button press on the page, or a stick
// pushed past half way.  Valve's controllers (the Steam Controllers, a Steam
// Deck's controls) are no gamepads to the browser: while the game runs,
// steampad.ts reads those the player picked through WebHID and puts them
// beside the browser's own as standard-mapping ones (allPads).
//
// Rumble goes the other way: runtime/dinput_pad.c plays the game's
// force-feedback effects as two motor levels in the mailbox, updated every
// frame the game polls the pad; this file plays them on the controller's
// vibrationActuator ("dual-rumble") in short overlapping effects, and lets
// the motors stop once the levels stop coming (a paused or parked game, a
// hidden page) or fall to zero.
//
// The page has a share too (PadPage): Home, or both sticks pressed in, opens
// its menu, which F9 opens on a keyboard (the game binds neither), and while
// one of its dialogs is open the controller works the dialog instead of the
// game.
import {
  IM_OFF_PAD_NAME, IM_PAD_AXIS, IM_PAD_BUTTONS, IM_PAD_CONNECTED, IM_PAD_FAMILY, IM_PAD_GEN, IM_PAD_RUMBLE, IM_PAD_SEQ,
  IM_PAD_WHEEL, IM_RUMBLE_SEQ, IM_RUMBLE_STRONG, IM_RUMBLE_WEAK,
  PAD_A, PAD_AXIS_LT, PAD_AXIS_LX, PAD_AXIS_LY, PAD_AXIS_RT, PAD_AXIS_RX, PAD_AXIS_RY, PAD_B, PAD_BACK, PAD_DDOWN,
  PAD_DLEFT, PAD_DRIGHT, PAD_DUP, PAD_HOME, PAD_LB, PAD_LS, PAD_RB, PAD_RS, PAD_START, PAD_X, PAD_Y,
  PADF_GENERIC, PADF_NINTENDO, PADF_PLAYSTATION, PADF_XBOX,
} from './proto';
import {
  describeMap, findHat, guessMap, hatDirs, isPedals, loadMap, loadShifter, pedalSetOf, pedalsOf, readWheel, Shifter,
  shifterGear, usbIds, WHEEL_MAP_EVENT, wheelOf, withSetUp, type OtherAxes, type ShifterMode, type WheelInfo, type WheelMap,
} from './wheel';
import { HidPadReader, knownPad, OneS2016Reader, oneS2016Android } from './hidpad';
import { LocalPadWriter } from './local-pads';
import { allPads, useSteamPads } from './steampad';
export { allPads };

export interface PadSnapshot { connected: boolean; buttons: number; axes: number[]; family: number; name: string; index: number; wheel?: boolean }

// standard mapping: buttons[i] -> PAD_* (6 and 7 are the analog triggers)
const BUTTON_OF: (number | -1)[] = [PAD_A, PAD_B, PAD_X, PAD_Y, PAD_LB, PAD_RB, -1, -1, PAD_BACK, PAD_START,
  PAD_LS, PAD_RS, PAD_DUP, PAD_DDOWN, PAD_DLEFT, PAD_DRIGHT, PAD_HOME];

/** the controller family and a display name from Gamepad.id: Chrome writes
 *  "Name (STANDARD GAMEPAD Vendor: 054c Product: 0ce6)", Firefox "054c-0ce6-Name"
 *  (on Linux and macOS without the leading zeros: "54c-ce6-Name").
 *  A wheel's family is its buttons' (a G29's are PlayStation's, a G920's Xbox's), a known pad's its labels'; Valve
 *  labels A, B, X and Y as Xbox does (its controllers, Steam's virtual pad). */
export function familyOf(id: string): { family: number; name: string } {
  const v = usbIds(id)?.vendor;
  let name = id.replace(/\s*\((?:STANDARD GAMEPAD\s*)?(?:Vendor:[^)]*)?\)\s*$/i, '').replace(/^[0-9a-f]{1,4}-[0-9a-f]{1,4}-/i, '').trim();
  if (!name) name = 'Game Controller';
  const s = id.toLowerCase(), w = wheelOf(id)?.layout, e = knownPad(id)?.face;
  if (w === 'ps' || w === 'xbox') return { family: w === 'ps' ? PADF_PLAYSTATION : PADF_XBOX, name };
  if (e) return { family: e === 'xbox' ? PADF_XBOX : PADF_NINTENDO, name };
  const family = v === '045e' || v === '28de' || /xbox|xinput/.test(s) ? PADF_XBOX
    : v === '054c' || /dualsense|dualshock|playstation/.test(s) ? PADF_PLAYSTATION
    : v === '057e' || /pro controller|joy-con|nintendo/.test(s) ? PADF_NINTENDO : PADF_GENERIC;
  return { family, name };
}

/** a Gamepad in the standard mapping -> the virtual pad (sticks -1..1 with
 *  +y down, which is already the Gamepad API's direction; triggers 0..1).
 *  notStick: axes read as 0 (a controller without the standard mapping: those
 *  that rested at an end when it showed up) */
export function mapStandard(g: Gamepad, notStick?: ReadonlySet<number>): PadSnapshot {
  let buttons = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < BUTTON_OF.length && i < g.buttons.length; i++) {
    const b = BUTTON_OF[i], bt = g.buttons[i];
    if (b >= 0 && bt && (bt.pressed || bt.value > 0.5)) buttons |= 1 << b;
  }
  const ax = (i: number) => {
    const v = g.axes[i];
    return typeof v === 'number' && isFinite(v) && !notStick?.has(i) ? Math.max(-1, Math.min(1, v)) : 0;
  };
  const tr = (i: number) => { const b = g.buttons[i]; return b ? Math.max(0, Math.min(1, b.value || (b.pressed ? 1 : 0))) : 0; };
  const axes = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0];
  axes[PAD_AXIS_LX] = ax(0); axes[PAD_AXIS_LY] = ax(1); axes[PAD_AXIS_RX] = ax(2); axes[PAD_AXIS_RY] = ax(3);
  axes[PAD_AXIS_LT] = tr(6); axes[PAD_AXIS_RT] = tr(7);
  const { family, name } = familyOf(g.id);
  return { connected: true, buttons, axes, family, name, index: g.index };
}

/** a steering wheel -> the virtual pad (wheel.ts): the wheel on LX, the brake and gas pedals on LT and RT (others:
 *  pedals on their own USB); its shifter's gears through shift (the lever's state, and what the player picked for it) */
export function mapWheel(g: Gamepad, m: WheelMap, hat: number, shift?: { shifter: Shifter; mode: ShifterMode },
                         others?: OtherAxes): PadSnapshot {
  const pressed = g.buttons.map(b => !!b && (b.pressed || b.value > 0.5));
  const { buttons: own, axes } = readWheel(g.axes, pressed, m, hat, others);
  const buttons = own | (shift && m.gears ? shift.shifter.buttons(shifterGear(pressed, m.gears), shift.mode, performance.now()) : 0);
  const { family, name } = familyOf(g.id);
  return { connected: true, buttons, axes, family, name, index: g.index, wheel: true };
}

/** a known pad (8BitDo's, Xbox's on Bluetooth on a Mac) without the standard mapping -> the virtual pad (hidpad.ts) */
export function mapHid(g: Gamepad, r: HidPadReader): PadSnapshot {
  const { buttons, axes } = r.read(g.axes, g.buttons.map(b => !!b && (b.pressed || b.value > 0.5)));
  const { family, name } = familyOf(g.id);
  return { connected: true, buttons, axes, family, name, index: g.index };
}

/** Xbox's One S with its 2016 firmware (or a pad with its id) under Chrome on Android, whose standard mapping Chrome
 *  gets wrong -> the virtual pad (hidpad.ts oneS2016Android) */
export function mapOneS2016(g: Gamepad, r: OneS2016Reader): PadSnapshot {
  const { buttons, axes } = r.read(g.axes, g.buttons);
  const { family, name } = familyOf(g.id);
  return { connected: true, buttons, axes, family, name, index: g.index };
}

/**
 * Whether a controller without the standard mapping has its places all the same: Chrome on Android reads every
 * controller through Android's key codes and puts its buttons and sticks where the standard mapping has them (the
 * sticks on axes 0 to 3, the triggers buttons 6 and 7, the D-pad buttons 12 to 15), but calls one it knows no mapping
 * for not standard ("8BitDo Ultimate 2 Wireless (Vendor: 2dc8 Product: 6012)", mapping "").  Read through the 8BitDo
 * layout (hidpad.ts: its HID report's order) such a pad had only A and B in place and its D-pad opened the page's menu
 * (a player's report: nothing worked from one day to the next).  Chrome on a big tablet asks for desktop websites and
 * says Linux: there it shows by Chrome's id with Android's 16 buttons (17 with Home) on a touch screen.
 */
export function androidLayout(g: Gamepad): boolean {
  if (g.mapping === 'standard') return false;
  const ua = navigator.userAgent ?? '';
  if (/Android/.test(ua)) return true;
  return /X11; Linux/.test(ua) && (navigator.maxTouchPoints ?? 0) > 0 && /\(Vendor: [0-9a-f]{4} Product: [0-9a-f]{4}\)$/i.test(g.id) &&
    (g.buttons.length === 16 || g.buttons.length === 17) && g.axes.length < 10;
}

/** the controller driving the game's pad (null: no game, or no controller); PAD_DRIVER_EVENT on the window when
 *  another one does (the Controls sheet shows that one) */
let driver: { index: number; id: string } | null = null;
export const PAD_DRIVER_EVENT = 'nfsu2-pad-driver';
/** whether a controller may drive the pad while others are connected: the standard mapping (Chrome on Android's
 *  too), a steering wheel, or a pad of a known layout (hidpad.ts); with the controllers connected (pads), not a wheel's dead
 *  twin */
export const mayDrive = (g: Gamepad | null, pads?: readonly (Gamepad | null)[]) => !!g &&
  (g.mapping === 'standard' || !!wheelOf(g.id) || !!knownPad(g.id) || androidLayout(g)) && !(pads && deadTwin(g, pads));

/**
 * Whether a wheel is the dead twin of another: a controller of the same id is connected too, and every axis of this
 * one reads exactly 0, as no wheel's do once it reported (a hat switch let go reads past 1, a pedal let go at an end).
 * A Fanatec base has a second joystick collection, which Windows makes a controller of its own with the same name,
 * and which sends nothing: connected first, it drove before any press, and nothing steered; its axes, every one 0,
 * were the base's first look (axesWhenSeen), and the guess from them put gas and brake on one axis, the clutch's,
 * whose rest read as the brake held down (the car reversing at full throttle).  Such a twin never drives.
 */
export function deadTwin(g: Gamepad, pads: readonly (Gamepad | null)[]): boolean {
  return g.mapping !== 'standard' && !!wheelOf(g.id) && g.axes.length > 0 && g.axes.every(v => v === 0) &&
    pads.some(o => !!o?.connected && o.index !== g.index && o.id === g.id);
}
export function drivingPad(): Gamepad | null {
  if (!driver) return null;
  try { const g = allPads()[driver.index]; return g?.connected && g.id === driver.id ? g : null; }
  catch { return null; }
}

/** what the poller knows of the controller driving the pad: whether it has the standard mapping's places (std: its
 *  own, or Chrome on Android's), its axes when it showed up; if it is a wheel, the model, how it makes the pad, the
 *  axis of its D-pad, its shifter and what the player picked for that; if it is an 8BitDo pad without the standard
 *  mapping, its reader */
interface Seen {
  index: number; id: string; std: boolean; axes0: number[]; ends: Set<number>; wheel: WheelInfo | null; map: WheelMap | null;
  hat: number; shifter: Shifter; mode: ShifterMode; hid: HidPadReader | null;
  others: string;            // a wheel's: the other controllers its map was made with (pedalsBeside)
  oneS: OneS2016Reader | null;   // Xbox's One S with its 2016 firmware under Chrome on Android (hidpad.ts)
  rs: [number, number]; rsAt: number; rsSaid: boolean;   // the right stick's axes as last seen, since when (stillStick)
}

/** the controllers besides the wheels and those with the standard mapping, which may be a wheel's pedals on their
 *  own USB (known ones, or set up), as a key: the wheel's map is made again when it changes */
function pedalsBeside(pads: readonly (Gamepad | null)[]): string {
  return pads.filter(p => !!p?.connected && p.mapping !== 'standard' && !wheelOf(p.id)).map(p => p!.id).join('\n');
}

/**
 * Each controller's axes when it first drove the pad on this page, by Gamepad.id: a wheel's layout comes from them
 * (a pedal let go rests at an end).  A wheel drives again after a controller did once a button is pressed on it,
 * perhaps with a foot on the gas already, and its axes read anew then had the gas off its rest: no pedal of the
 * model's, so the guess took the clutch for the gas until a reload (a player's report).  So a wheel keeps its first
 * look, unless a later one is better (betterLook).
 */
const firstAxes = new Map<string, number[]>();
function axesWhenSeen(g: Gamepad, wheel: WheelInfo | null): number[] {
  const now = Array.from(g.axes, v => typeof v === 'number' && isFinite(v) ? v : 0);
  const first = firstAxes.get(g.id);
  if (first && first.length === now.length && !(wheel && betterLook(wheel, first, now, g.buttons.length))) return first;
  if (firstAxes.size < 16 || first) firstAxes.set(g.id, now);
  return now;
}
/** whether a wheel's look now makes a better layout than its first: the model's own where the first gave a guess, or
 *  any that read where the first read every axis 0 (no report yet, a dead twin's), but for one losing the model's own
 *  (a pedal held down then) */
function betterLook(wheel: WheelInfo, first: number[], now: number[], nbuttons: number): boolean {
  const placed = (a: number[]) => !!guessMap(wheel, a, nbuttons).placed, zero = (a: number[]) => a.every(v => v === 0);
  if (zero(first) && !zero(now)) return placed(now) || !placed(first);
  return !placed(first) && placed(now);
}

/** what the page itself does with the controller */
export interface PadPage {
  /** Home, or both sticks pressed in: the page's menu (open or close it) */
  menu(): void;
  /** whether a dialog of the page is open: it has the controller, the game gets it at rest */
  dialog(): boolean;
  /** a button went down while dialog() (a PAD_* number; the left stick's directions come as the D-pad's) */
  press(button: number): void;
  /** the right stick (x, y: -1..1, +y down) each time the controller is read while no dialog is open (quick chat's
   *  picker); true: the page uses it now, the game gets it at rest (else the game looks round the car with it:
   *  runtime/look.c) */
  stick?(x: number, y: number): boolean;
  /** the right stick pressed in alone (not the menu's shortcut) while no dialog is open and capture() does not have
   *  the controller (quick chat's picker opens or closes); true: the page took it, the game does not get it (else
   *  the game's: a car's hydraulics) */
  click?(): boolean;
  /** the stick whose click goes to click() (PAD_RS unless the player picked PAD_LS, or -1: none; app/sitekeys.ts) */
  chatButton?(): number;
  /** the whole controller each time it is read while no dialog is open (photo mode: runtime/photo.c), with the
   *  buttons pressed since the last read; true: the page has it now, the game gets it at rest */
  capture?(s: PadSnapshot, pressed: number): boolean;
}

/** the touch controls' share of the pad (web/src/app/touch.ts): PAD_* button bits and the left stick's x */
export interface TouchPad { buttons: number; lx: number }

/** a real controller's snapshot with the touch controls' added (their buttons too, the stick further out of the
 *  two); without a real one, the touch controls are the controller */
function withTouch(s: PadSnapshot, t: TouchPad): PadSnapshot {
  const axes = [...s.axes];
  if (Math.abs(t.lx) > Math.abs(axes[PAD_AXIS_LX])) axes[PAD_AXIS_LX] = t.lx;
  return s.connected ? { ...s, buttons: s.buttons | t.buttons, axes }
    : { connected: true, buttons: t.buttons, axes, family: PADF_GENERIC, name: 'Touch controls', index: -2 };
}

/** a stick pressed in alone waits this long (ms) for the other, the menu's shortcut, before the game gets it (the horn,
 *  a car's hydraulics); let go before, the game gets it this long */
const CHORD_MS = 120, TAP_MS = 80;
/** a right stick held exactly where it is this long, off centre, on a controller without the standard mapping reads
 *  as let go (PadPoller.stillStick) */
const STILL_MS = 2000;

/** the left stick as four directions, PAD_D* bits: on past 0.55, off below 0.40 (runtime/dinput_pad.c's hat) */
function stickDirs(x: number, y: number, prev: number): number {
  const on = (bit: number, v: number) => v > 0.55 || (v > 0.40 && (prev & 1 << bit) !== 0) ? 1 << bit : 0;
  return on(PAD_DUP, -y) | on(PAD_DDOWN, y) | on(PAD_DLEFT, -x) | on(PAD_DRIGHT, x);
}

export class PadPoller {
  private localPads: LocalPadWriter | null;
  private order: number[] = [];            // controller indices in connection order
  private last: PadSnapshot | null = null;
  private f32 = new Float32Array(1);
  private i32 = new Int32Array(this.f32.buffer);
  private pressedBefore = 0;
  // the sticks and triggers where they last counted as the player's use (a drifting stick does not)
  private usedAxes = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0];
  // rumble: the last mailbox update seen and when, what is playing
  private rumbleSeq = 0;
  private rumbleSeen = 0;
  private rumbleSent = 0;
  private rumbleNow: [number, number] = [0, 0];
  private rumblePad: Gamepad | null = null;
  // the page's share: buttons kept from the game until let go, the left stick's directions; a stick pressed in alone,
  // kept from the game while the other may follow (the menu): its bit and since when, and a tap's until when
  private held = 0;
  private stick = 0;
  private alone = 0;
  private aloneAt = 0;
  private tap = 0;
  private tapUntil = 0;
  // the touch controls' virtual controller (touch.ts), and the phone's vibration for the game's rumble without a
  // controller: when it last buzzed
  private touch: TouchPad | null = null;
  private buzzAt = 0;
  // the controller driving the pad as it showed up (a wheel's layout comes from it)
  private seen: Seen | null = null;
  // each controller's buttons as last polled (a radio's axes too, where they last were its use), and the one a button
  // was last pressed on (choose)
  private down = new Map<number, { id: string; on: boolean[]; at?: number[] }>();
  private chosen: { index: number; id: string } | null = null;
  private polled = false;
  /** performance.now() of a real controller's last button press (0: none yet) */
  lastPress = 0;
  // split screen's seats (local-pads.ts) read the standard mapping, but for a pad Chrome on Android maps wrong
  // (hidpad.ts oneS2016Android): each such one with a reader of its own
  private localOneS = new Map<string, OneS2016Reader>();
  private readLocal = (g: Gamepad): PadSnapshot => {
    if (!oneS2016Android(g)) return mapStandard(g);
    const key = `${g.index}|${g.id}`;
    let r = this.localOneS.get(key);
    if (!r) { if (this.localOneS.size >= 8) this.localOneS.clear(); this.localOneS.set(key, r = new OneS2016Reader()); }
    return mapOneS2016(g, r);
  };
  // views of the game's memory: dropped by dispose(), so nothing keeps an ended
  // process's (1 GB+) shared memory reachable or writes into its mailbox
  private h: Int32Array | null;
  private u8: Uint8Array | null;
  // Valve's controllers while the poller runs (steampad.ts)
  private steam: () => void;
  private onConnect = (e: GamepadEvent) => {
    this.log(`[pad] connected: ${e.gamepad.id} (index ${e.gamepad.index}, mapping "${e.gamepad.mapping}")`);
    this.poll();
  };
  private onDisconnect = (e: GamepadEvent) => {
    this.log(`[pad] disconnected: ${e.gamepad.id}`);
    this.poll();
  };
  // the player set up a wheel (or went back to the guess): read its layout again
  private onWheelMap = () => {
    if (this.seen) this.seen.map = null;
    this.poll();
  };

  /** onPress: a button went down; onUse: that, or a stick or trigger moved a quarter of its range; page: the page's
   *  menu and dialogs */
  constructor(h: Int32Array, u8: Uint8Array, private base: number,
              private onPress: () => void, private log: (s: string) => void, private onUse?: () => void,
              private page?: PadPage) {
    this.h = h; this.u8 = u8;
    this.localPads = new LocalPadWriter(u8.buffer, base);
    addEventListener('gamepadconnected', this.onConnect);
    addEventListener('gamepaddisconnected', this.onDisconnect);
    addEventListener(WHEEL_MAP_EVENT, this.onWheelMap);
    this.steam = useSteamPads(log);
  }

  /** stop for good: listeners removed, the mailbox views dropped */
  dispose() {
    removeEventListener('gamepadconnected', this.onConnect);
    removeEventListener('gamepaddisconnected', this.onDisconnect);
    removeEventListener(WHEEL_MAP_EVENT, this.onWheelMap);
    this.rumble(null);
    this.steam();
    this.h = null; this.u8 = null;
    this.localPads = null;
    if (driver) { driver = null; dispatchEvent(new Event(PAD_DRIVER_EVENT)); }
  }

  /** the controller driving the pad, or null */
  current(): string | null { return this.last?.connected ? this.last.name : null; }

  /** the touch controls' virtual controller, merged with a real one (null: none) */
  setTouch(t: TouchPad | null) { this.touch = t; this.poll(); }

  poll() {
    if (!this.h) return;
    const pads = allPads();
    const live = new Set<number>();
    for (const g of pads) if (g && g.connected) { live.add(g.index); if (!this.order.includes(g.index)) this.order.push(g.index); }
    this.order = this.order.filter(i => live.has(i));
    const kept = this.localPads?.reserved() ?? new Set<number>();
    const byIndex = (i: number) => kept.has(i) ? null : pads[i] ?? null;
    this.choose(pads, kept);
    const c = this.chosen, cg = c && byIndex(c.index);
    let pick = cg?.connected && cg.id === c!.id ? c!.index : undefined;
    if (pick === undefined) {
      this.chosen = null;
      pick = this.order.find(i => mayDrive(byIndex(i), pads)) ?? this.order.find(i => mayDrive(byIndex(i)));
    }
    // pedals on their own are no controller (released, a stick of theirs is pushed all the way)
    if (pick === undefined) pick = this.order.find(i => !kept.has(i) && !isPedals(byIndex(i)?.id ?? ''));
    const g = pick === undefined ? null : byIndex(pick);
    if (g?.index !== driver?.index || g?.id !== driver?.id) {
      if (g && driver) this.log(`[pad] ${g.id} drives now${this.chosen ? ' (a button pressed on it)' : ''}`);
      driver = g && { index: g.index, id: g.id };
      dispatchEvent(new Event(PAD_DRIVER_EVENT));
    }
    const s: PadSnapshot = g ? this.read(g, pads) : { connected: false, buttons: 0, axes: [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0], family: PADF_GENERIC, name: '', index: -1 };
    this.rumble(g);
    const pressed = s.buttons & ~this.pressedBefore;
    this.pressedBefore = s.buttons;
    if (pressed) { this.onPress(); this.lastPress = performance.now(); }
    if (pressed || s.axes.some((v, i) => Math.abs(v - this.usedAxes[i]) > 0.25)) { this.usedAxes = s.axes; this.onUse?.(); }
    const both = this.touch ? withTouch(s, this.touch) : s;
    if (this.touch && !g) this.buzz();
    const out = this.page ? this.forPage(both, pressed) : both;
    this.localPads?.poll(pads, this.readLocal, !!globalThis.document?.hidden || !!this.page?.dialog());
    if (this.same(out)) return;
    this.publish(out, !this.last || this.last.connected !== out.connected || this.last.index !== out.index || this.last.name !== out.name);
    this.last = out;
  }

  /** A button pressed on a controller that may drive the pad makes it the one that does (chosen).  One that shows up
   *  with a button held was pressed (Chrome shows a controller on a press), but not one there at the first poll (a
   *  wheel's shifter left in a gear).  A radio has few buttons or none: a stick or a switch of its moved half way
   *  from where it was while it last drove (or showed up) counts as a press. */
  private choose(pads: readonly (Gamepad | null)[], kept: Set<number>) {
    const down = new Map<number, { id: string; on: boolean[]; at?: number[] }>();
    if (this.chosen && kept.has(this.chosen.index)) this.chosen = null;
    for (const g of pads) {
      if (!g?.connected || kept.has(g.index)) continue;
      const on = g.buttons.map(b => !!b && (b.pressed || b.value > 0.5));
      const was = this.down.get(g.index);
      const before = was?.id === g.id ? was.on : this.polled ? [] : on;
      let at: number[] | undefined;
      if (wheelOf(g.id)?.layout === 'radio') {
        const now = Array.from(g.axes, v => typeof v === 'number' && isFinite(v) ? v : 0), prev = was?.id === g.id ? was.at : undefined;
        const moved = !!prev && now.some((v, i) => Math.abs(v - (prev[i] ?? v)) >= 0.5);
        if (moved) this.chosen = { index: g.index, id: g.id };
        at = !prev || moved || (driver?.index === g.index && driver.id === g.id) ? now : prev;
      }
      if (mayDrive(g, pads) && on.some((v, i) => v && !before[i])) this.chosen = { index: g.index, id: g.id };
      down.set(g.index, at ? { id: g.id, on, at } : { id: g.id, on });
    }
    this.down = down;
    this.polled = true;
  }

  /** the controller driving the pad as the pad: a wheel through its layout (the model's, with the player's set-up
   *  over it, or the guess from how it showed up) and its shifter, one in the standard mapping's places as it is, an
   *  8BitDo pad through its known layout, any other as if it had the standard mapping, but for the axes that rested at
   *  an end when it showed up, and with Chrome's hat switch as its D-pad.  The first two axes (the left stick, in
   *  every browser's placement) are always a stick: Chrome shows a controller once a stick is pushed past half way,
   *  so it may sit at an end then, and it steered nothing until a reload.  A wheel's gas and brake are those of
   *  known pedals on their own USB while they are connected (Fanatec's: pedalSetOf), unless the player set up others.
   *  pads: the controllers connected. */
  private read(g: Gamepad, pads: readonly (Gamepad | null)[]): PadSnapshot {
    let k = this.seen;
    if (!k || k.index !== g.index || k.id !== g.id) {
      const wheel = wheelOf(g.id), axes0 = axesWhenSeen(g, wheel), known = knownPad(g.id);
      const std = g.mapping === 'standard' || (!wheel && androidLayout(g));
      const ends = new Set<number>();
      if (!std) axes0.forEach((v, i) => { if (i > 1 && Math.abs(v) >= 0.9 && Math.abs(v) <= 1.05) ends.add(i); });
      const hid = !wheel && known && !std ? new HidPadReader(known.face, axes0, known.ltFirst, known.maker) : null;
      const oneS = !wheel && oneS2016Android(g) ? new OneS2016Reader() : null;
      k = this.seen = { index: g.index, id: g.id, std, axes0, ends, wheel, map: null, hat: std ? -1 : findHat(axes0),
        shifter: new Shifter(), mode: 'off', hid, others: '', oneS, rs: [0, 0], rsAt: performance.now(), rsSaid: false };
      if (oneS) this.log(`[pad] ${g.id}: read as ${oneS.describe()}`);
      if (g.mapping !== 'standard') {
        this.log(`[pad] ${g.id}: no standard mapping in this browser; ${g.axes.length} axes at ` +
          `[${axes0.map(v => v.toFixed(2)).join(' ')}], ${g.buttons.length} buttons`);
        if (hid) this.log(`[pad] read as ${hid.describe()}`);
        else if (std) this.log('[pad] read as it is: Android put it in the standard mapping\'s places');
        else if (!k.wheel) this.log(`[pad] read as if it had one${ends.size ? `, but for axes ${[...ends].join(', ')} (at an end: no stick)` : ''}` +
          `${k.hat >= 0 ? `, the D-pad on axis ${k.hat}` : ''}`);
      }
    }
    if (k.hid) return mapHid(g, k.hid);
    if (k.oneS) return mapOneS2016(g, k.oneS);
    if (k.hat < 0 && !k.std) {
      k.hat = findHat(g.axes);
      if (k.hat >= 0) this.log(`[pad] ${g.id}: the D-pad on axis ${k.hat}`);
    }
    if (k.wheel && g.mapping === 'standard') return { ...mapStandard(g), wheel: true };
    if (k.wheel) {
      const beside = k.wheel.layout === 'radio' ? '' : pedalsBeside(pads);
      if (k.map && k.others !== beside) k.map = null;
      if (!k.map) {
        let guess = guessMap(k.wheel, k.axes0, g.buttons.length);
        const kept = loadMap(g.id), ped = beside ? pads.find(p => !!p?.connected && !!pedalSetOf(p.id)) : undefined;
        if (ped) guess = { ...guess, ...pedalsOf(ped.id, pedalSetOf(ped.id)!, ped.axes.length) };
        k.map = kept ? withSetUp(guess, kept, id => pads.some(p => !!p?.connected && p.id === id)) : guess;
        k.others = beside;
        k.mode = loadShifter(g.id);
        this.log(`[pad] ${g.id}: ${k.wheel.layout === 'radio' ? 'an RC radio' : 'a steering wheel'}, ${describeMap(k.map, k.hat)}` +
          `${k.map.gears ? `; the shifter: ${k.mode}` : ''}`);
      }
      const others: OtherAxes = id => { for (const p of pads) if (p?.connected && p.id === id) return p.axes; return undefined; };
      return mapWheel(g, k.map, k.hat, k, others);
    }
    const s = mapStandard(g, k.std ? undefined : k.ends);
    if (!k.std && k.hat >= 0) s.buttons |= hatDirs(g.axes[k.hat]);
    if (g.mapping !== 'standard') this.stillStick(k, g, s);
    return s;
  }

  /** A controller without the standard mapping (read in its places: Chrome on Android's, or as if it had them) whose
   *  right stick has not moved at all for STILL_MS off centre reads as having it let go, until it moves.  Some phone
   *  controllers have a touch pad in its place, which keeps the place of the last touch once the finger is off (a
   *  player's GT NX under Chrome on Android: axes 2 and 3 stayed at -0.97 after a tap), and the game kept looking round
   *  the car with it (runtime/look.c springs back only when the stick does).  A thumb on a stick off centre moves it a
   *  little within that time; one that does hold it exactly gets the view back until the stick moves. */
  private stillStick(k: Seen, g: Gamepad, s: PadSnapshot) {
    const x = g.axes[2] ?? 0, y = g.axes[3] ?? 0, now = performance.now();
    if (x !== k.rs[0] || y !== k.rs[1]) { k.rs = [x, y]; k.rsAt = now; return; }
    if (now - k.rsAt < STILL_MS || (s.axes[PAD_AXIS_RX] === 0 && s.axes[PAD_AXIS_RY] === 0)) return;
    if (!k.rsSaid) {
      k.rsSaid = true;
      this.log(`[pad] ${g.id}: the right stick stayed at [${x.toFixed(2)} ${y.toFixed(2)}] for ${STILL_MS / 1000} s: ` +
        'read as let go until it moves (a touch pad in its place?)');
    }
    s.axes[PAD_AXIS_RX] = s.axes[PAD_AXIS_RY] = 0;
  }

  /** The page's share of the controller: Home, or the second stick pressed in while the other is, opens or closes its
   *  menu.  While a dialog of the page is open, the buttons and the left stick work it and the game gets the
   *  controller at rest.  A button held then (or the shortcut's) stays away from the game until it is let go, so the
   *  A that closed the menu does not press A in the game too.  A stick pressed in alone (the horn, horn.c; a car's
   *  hydraulics) reaches the game once CHORD_MS passed without the other, or for TAP_MS when let go before, so the
   *  shortcut does not sound the horn or bounce the car; the right one goes to the page's click() first (quick
   *  chat), and when the page takes it the game never gets it. */
  private forPage(s: PadSnapshot, pressed: number): PadSnapshot {
    const page = this.page!, sticks = 1 << PAD_LS | 1 << PAD_RS, home = 1 << PAD_HOME, now = performance.now();
    const menu = (pressed & home) !== 0 || ((pressed & sticks) !== 0 && (s.buttons & sticks) === sticks);
    if (menu) { page.menu(); this.held |= s.buttons & (sticks | home); }
    const captured = !page.dialog() && !menu && !!page.capture?.(s, pressed);
    const chat = page.chatButton?.() ?? PAD_RS;
    const clicked = (b: number) => chat >= 0 && b === 1 << chat && !captured && !page.dialog() && !!page.click?.();
    if (pressed & sticks && (s.buttons & sticks) !== sticks) { this.alone = s.buttons & sticks; this.aloneAt = now; }
    let wait = 0;
    if (menu) this.alone = 0;
    else if (this.alone && !(s.buttons & this.alone)) {
      if (!clicked(this.alone)) { this.tap = this.alone; this.tapUntil = now + TAP_MS; }
      this.alone = 0;
    } else if (this.alone && now - this.aloneAt < CHORD_MS) wait = this.alone;
    else if (this.alone) { if (clicked(this.alone)) this.held |= this.alone; this.alone = 0; }
    const tap = now < this.tapUntil ? this.tap : 0;
    const dirs = stickDirs(s.axes[PAD_AXIS_LX], s.axes[PAD_AXIS_LY], this.stick), turned = dirs & ~this.stick;
    this.stick = dirs;
    if (captured) {
      this.held = s.buttons;
      return { ...s, buttons: 0, axes: [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0] };
    }
    if (!page.dialog()) {
      this.held &= s.buttons;
      const buttons = (s.buttons & ~this.held & ~wait) | tap;
      const rs = s.connected && !!page.stick?.(s.axes[PAD_AXIS_RX], s.axes[PAD_AXIS_RY]);
      if (rs) { const axes = [...s.axes]; axes[PAD_AXIS_RX] = axes[PAD_AXIS_RY] = 0; return { ...s, buttons, axes }; }
      return buttons === s.buttons ? s : { ...s, buttons };
    }
    this.held = s.buttons;
    if (!menu) for (let b = 0; b < 16; b++) if ((pressed | turned) & 1 << b) page.press(b);
    return { ...s, buttons: 0, axes: [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0] };
  }

  private same(s: PadSnapshot) {
    const l = this.last;
    return !!l && l.connected === s.connected && l.buttons === s.buttons && l.index === s.index && !!l.wheel === !!s.wheel &&
      l.axes.every((v, i) => v === s.axes[i]);
  }

  // the seqlock: odd while writing; every word is an atomic store so the
  // guest never sees a half-written pad
  private publish(s: PadSnapshot, newPad: boolean) {
    const h = this.h, u8 = this.u8;
    if (!h || !u8) return;
    const seq = Atomics.load(h, IM_PAD_SEQ);
    Atomics.store(h, IM_PAD_SEQ, (seq + 1) | 0);
    Atomics.store(h, IM_PAD_CONNECTED, s.connected ? 1 : 0);
    Atomics.store(h, IM_PAD_FAMILY, s.family);
    Atomics.store(h, IM_PAD_BUTTONS, s.buttons);
    Atomics.store(h, IM_PAD_WHEEL, s.connected && s.wheel ? 1 : 0);
    for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) { this.f32[0] = s.axes[i]; Atomics.store(h, IM_PAD_AXIS + i, this.i32[0]); }
    if (newPad) {
      const name = s.name.replace(/[^\x20-\x7e]/g, '?').slice(0, 63);
      for (let i = 0; i < 64; i++) Atomics.store(u8, this.base + IM_OFF_PAD_NAME + i, i < name.length ? name.charCodeAt(i) : 0);
    }
    Atomics.store(h, IM_PAD_SEQ, (seq + 2) | 0);
    if (newPad) Atomics.add(h, IM_PAD_GEN, 1);
  }

  /** Without a controller, the touch controls' rumble: the phone's vibration (Android; on or off, no strength), a
   *  pulse as long as the game's strongest motor is strong, at most every 150 ms. */
  private buzz() {
    const h = this.h, now = performance.now();
    if (!h || typeof navigator.vibrate !== 'function' || now - this.buzzAt < 150) return;
    const seq = Atomics.load(h, IM_RUMBLE_SEQ);
    if (seq !== this.rumbleSeq) { this.rumbleSeq = seq; this.rumbleSeen = now; }
    if (now - this.rumbleSeen > 150 || document.visibilityState !== 'visible') return;
    const level = Math.max(Atomics.load(h, IM_RUMBLE_STRONG), Atomics.load(h, IM_RUMBLE_WEAK) * 0.6) / 65535;
    if (level < 0.25) return;
    this.buzzAt = now;
    navigator.vibrate(Math.round(30 + 90 * level));
  }

  /** the game's motor levels onto this controller (every frame, from poll) */
  private rumble(g: Gamepad | null) {
    const h = this.h;
    const va = g?.vibrationActuator;
    const can = !!va && typeof va.playEffect === 'function';
    // the touch controls rumble through the phone's vibration instead (buzz)
    const phone = !g && !!this.touch && typeof navigator.vibrate === 'function';
    if (h && Atomics.load(h, IM_PAD_RUMBLE) !== (can || phone ? 1 : 0)) Atomics.store(h, IM_PAD_RUMBLE, can || phone ? 1 : 0);
    const now = performance.now();
    let strong = 0, weak = 0;
    if (h && can) {
      const seq = Atomics.load(h, IM_RUMBLE_SEQ);
      if (seq !== this.rumbleSeq) { this.rumbleSeq = seq; this.rumbleSeen = now; }
      // levels the game still sends: it polls the pad every frame while it runs
      if (now - this.rumbleSeen < 150 && document.visibilityState === 'visible') {
        strong = Atomics.load(h, IM_RUMBLE_STRONG) / 65535; weak = Atomics.load(h, IM_RUMBLE_WEAK) / 65535;
      }
    }
    const [ps, pw] = this.rumbleNow, playing = ps > 0 || pw > 0;
    if (strong < 0.02 && weak < 0.02) {
      if (playing || (this.rumblePad && this.rumblePad !== g)) {
        const p = this.rumblePad?.vibrationActuator;
        if (p && typeof p.reset === 'function') void p.reset().catch(() => {});
        this.rumbleNow = [0, 0]; this.rumblePad = null;
      }
      return;
    }
    // overlapping 120 ms effects: renewed every 60 ms, every 30 ms while the
    // levels move (a hit fading), and at once for a new hit
    const since = now - this.rumbleSent;
    const hit = strong > ps + 0.2 || weak > pw + 0.2;
    const moved = Math.abs(strong - ps) >= 0.05 || Math.abs(weak - pw) >= 0.05;
    if (playing && this.rumblePad === g && !hit && (since < 30 || (since < 60 && !moved))) return;
    this.rumbleSent = now; this.rumbleNow = [strong, weak]; this.rumblePad = g;
    void va!.playEffect('dual-rumble', { duration: 120, startDelay: 0, strongMagnitude: strong, weakMagnitude: weak }).catch(() => {});
  }
}

import {
