  [D0G.MENU, SB.BACK], [D0G.ESCAPE, SB.START], [D0G.STEAM, SB.HOME], [D0G.STICK_CLICK, SB.LS], [D0G.RPAD_CLICK, SB.RS],
  [D0G.UP, SB.UP], [D0G.DOWN, SB.DOWN], [D0G.LEFT, SB.LEFT], [D0G.RIGHT, SB.RIGHT], [D0G.GRIP_L, SB.L4],
  [D0G.GRIP_R, SB.R4]] as const;
/** the pads are mounted turned: SDL turns their positions back by 15 degrees (the left one the other way), and moves a
 *  touched one's 1000 up and right */
const TURN = 0.261799;
function turned(x: number, y: number, angle: number, touched: boolean): [number, number] {
  const c = Math.cos(angle), s = Math.sin(angle), off = touched ? 1000 : 0;
  const clamp16 = (v: number) => Math.max(-32768, Math.min(32767, Math.trunc(v)));
  return [clamp16(c * x - s * y + off), clamp16(s * x + c * y + off)];
}
/** a clicked left pad's D-pad direction from where it was clicked (the controller gives it as buttons; this is for a
 *  report that does not), +y up: eight ways, none near the middle */
function padDirs(x: number, y: number): number {
  const r = Math.hypot(x, y);
  if (r < 8000) return 0;
  return (y > 0.38 * r ? 1 << SB.UP : 0) | (y < -0.38 * r ? 1 << SB.DOWN : 0) |
    (x < -0.38 * r ? 1 << SB.LEFT : 0) | (x > 0.38 * r ? 1 << SB.RIGHT : 0);
}

/**
 * A 2015 controller's reports, read as SDL's FormatStatePacketUntilGyro reads them.  The stick and the left pad share
 * their fields: a report carries the pad's position while a thumb is on it, else the stick's, and while both are in use
 * the reports take turns (LPAD_AND_STICK), so each keeps where it was last.  An older controller sends the pad's click
 * for the stick's when nobody touches the pad.  The triggers' analog is 7 bits doubled, full at 26000.
 */
export class D0GReader {
  private stick: [number, number] = [0, 0];
  private pad: [number, number] = [0, 0];
  private packet = -1;
  private last: SteamState | null = null;

  read(d: DataView): SteamReport {
    if (d.byteLength < 24 || d.getUint16(0, true) !== 1) return null;
    const type = d.getUint8(2);
    if (type === 3) return d.getUint8(3) >= 1 ? d.getUint8(4) === 1 ? 'off' : 'on' : null;   // a dongle's: the radio link
    if (type !== 1) return null;
    const packet = d.getUint32(4, true);
    if (packet === this.packet && this.last) return this.last;        // nothing new
    this.packet = packet;
    let m = d.getUint8(8) | d.getUint8(9) << 8 | d.getUint8(10) << 16;
    const x = d.getInt16(16, true), y = d.getInt16(18, true);
    let sx = 0, sy = 0, px = 0, py = 0;
    if (m & D0G.LPAD_TOUCH) {
      [px, py] = this.pad = [x, y];
      if (m & D0G.LPAD_AND_STICK) [sx, sy] = this.stick; else this.stick = [0, 0];
    } else {
      [sx, sy] = this.stick = [x, y];
      if (m & D0G.LPAD_AND_STICK) [px, py] = this.pad;
      else {
        this.pad = [0, 0];
        if (m & D0G.LPAD_CLICK) m = (m & ~D0G.LPAD_CLICK) | D0G.STICK_CLICK;
      }
    }
    if (m & D0G.LPAD_AND_STICK) m |= D0G.LPAD_TOUCH;
    let buttons = mapBits(m, D0G_BUTTONS);
    if ((m & D0G.LPAD_CLICK) && (m & D0G.LPAD_TOUCH) && !(m & (D0G.UP | D0G.DOWN | D0G.LEFT | D0G.RIGHT))) {
      const [tx, ty] = turned(px, py, -TURN, false);
      buttons |= padDirs(tx, ty);
    }
    const [rx, ry] = turned(d.getInt16(20, true), d.getInt16(22, true), TURN, (m & D0G.RPAD_TOUCH) !== 0);
    const trig = (n: number) => unit(((n << 7) | n) / 26000);
    const lt = m & D0G.LT ? 1 : trig(d.getUint8(11)), rt = m & D0G.RT ? 1 : trig(d.getUint8(12));
    buttons |= triggerBits(lt, rt, (m & D0G.LT) !== 0, (m & D0G.RT) !== 0);
    return this.last = { buttons, lx: axis(sx), ly: -axis(sy), rx: axis(rx), ry: -axis(ry), lt, rt };
  }
}

// ---- the Steam Deck ("Jupiter"): 64-byte reports, no report id, of type 9

const DECK_LOW = [[0x80, SB.A], [0x20, SB.B], [0x40, SB.X], [0x10, SB.Y], [0x8, SB.LB], [0x4, SB.RB], [0x1000, SB.BACK],
  [0x4000, SB.START], [0x2000, SB.HOME], [0x400000, SB.LS], [0x4000000, SB.RS], [0x100, SB.UP], [0x800, SB.DOWN],
  [0x400, SB.LEFT], [0x200, SB.RIGHT], [0x8000, SB.L5], [0x10000, SB.R5]] as const;
const DECK_HIGH = [[0x200, SB.L4], [0x400, SB.R4], [0x40000, SB.QAM]] as const;

/** a Steam Deck's report: buttons in two words, the triggers 0..32767, the sticks +y up */
export function readDeck(d: DataView): SteamReport {
  if (d.byteLength < 56 || d.getUint16(0, true) !== 1 || d.getUint8(2) !== 9) return null;
  const low = d.getUint32(8, true), high = d.getUint32(12, true);
  const lt = unit(d.getUint16(44, true) / 32767), rt = unit(d.getUint16(46, true) / 32767);
  const buttons = mapBits(low, DECK_LOW) | mapBits(high, DECK_HIGH) | triggerBits(lt, rt, (low & 2) !== 0, (low & 1) !== 0);
  return { buttons, lx: axis(d.getInt16(48, true)), ly: -axis(d.getInt16(50, true)),
    rx: axis(d.getInt16(52, true)), ry: -axis(d.getInt16(54, true)), lt, rt };
}

// ---- the Steam Controller of 2026 ("Triton"): reports with ids, 0x42/0x45/0x47 its state, 0x46/0x79 a dongle's link

// SDL reads the bit it calls MENU as Back and VIEW as Start
const TRITON_BUTTONS = [[0x1, SB.A], [0x2, SB.B], [0x4, SB.X], [0x8, SB.Y], [0x80000, SB.LB], [0x200, SB.RB],
  [0x4000, SB.BACK], [0x40, SB.START], [0x10000, SB.HOME], [0x8000, SB.LS], [0x20, SB.RS], [0x2000, SB.UP],
  [0x400, SB.DOWN], [0x1000, SB.LEFT], [0x800, SB.RIGHT], [0x20000, SB.L4], [0x80, SB.R4], [0x40000, SB.L5],
  [0x100, SB.R5], [0x10, SB.QAM]] as const;

/** a 2026 controller's report (data without its id): a sequence number, the buttons, the triggers 0..32767, the
 *  sticks +y up */
export function readTriton(reportId: number, d: DataView): SteamReport {
  if (reportId === 0x79 || reportId === 0x46) {
    const s = d.byteLength ? d.getUint8(0) : 0;
    return s === 1 ? 'off' : s === 2 ? 'on' : null;
  }
  if ((reportId !== 0x42 && reportId !== 0x45 && reportId !== 0x47) || d.byteLength < 17) return null;
  const m = d.getUint32(1, true);
  const lt = unit(d.getInt16(5, true) / 32767), rt = unit(d.getInt16(7, true) / 32767);
  const buttons = mapBits(m, TRITON_BUTTONS) | triggerBits(lt, rt, (m & 0x8000000) !== 0, (m & 0x800000) !== 0);
  return { buttons, lx: axis(d.getInt16(9, true)), ly: -axis(d.getInt16(11, true)),
    rx: axis(d.getInt16(13, true)), ry: -axis(d.getInt16(15, true)), lt, rt };
}

// ---- the commands: feature reports (64 bytes; the 2026 controller's report 1, 63) and its output report 0x80

const ID_CLEAR_DIGITAL_MAPPINGS = 0x81, ID_SET_DEFAULT_DIGITAL_MAPPINGS = 0x85, ID_SET_SETTINGS_VALUES = 0x87;
const ID_LOAD_DEFAULT_SETTINGS = 0x8e, ID_DONGLE_GET_WIRELESS_STATE = 0xb4, ID_TRIGGER_RUMBLE_CMD = 0xeb;
const SETTING_LEFT_TRACKPAD_MODE = 7, SETTING_RIGHT_TRACKPAD_MODE = 8, SETTING_LIZARD_MODE = 9;
const SETTING_SMOOTH_ABSOLUTE_MOUSE = 24, SETTING_WIRELESS_PACKET_VERSION = 49;
const SETTING_LEFT_TRACKPAD_CLICK_PRESSURE = 52, SETTING_RIGHT_TRACKPAD_CLICK_PRESSURE = 53;
const TRACKPAD_ABSOLUTE_MOUSE = 0, TRACKPAD_NONE = 7;

/** a message: its type, its payload's length, the payload */
const msg = (type: number, payload: number[] = []) => [type, payload.length, ...payload];
/** ID_SET_SETTINGS_VALUES with [setting, value] pairs (a value is 16 bits) */
const settings = (...s: [number, number][]) => msg(ID_SET_SETTINGS_VALUES, s.flatMap(([n, v]) => [n, v & 0xff, v >> 8 & 0xff]));

/** the feature reports that turn lizard mode off (SDL's ResetSteamController, DisableDeckLizardMode,
 *  DisableSteamTritonLizardMode), and for the 2015 controller those that bring it back (CloseSteamController) */
export const LIZARD = {
  d0gOff: [msg(ID_CLEAR_DIGITAL_MAPPINGS), msg(ID_LOAD_DEFAULT_SETTINGS), settings([SETTING_WIRELESS_PACKET_VERSION, 2],
    [SETTING_LEFT_TRACKPAD_MODE, TRACKPAD_NONE], [SETTING_RIGHT_TRACKPAD_MODE, TRACKPAD_NONE], [SETTING_SMOOTH_ABSOLUTE_MOUSE, 0])],
  d0gOn: [msg(ID_SET_DEFAULT_DIGITAL_MAPPINGS), msg(ID_LOAD_DEFAULT_SETTINGS),
    settings([SETTING_RIGHT_TRACKPAD_MODE, TRACKPAD_ABSOLUTE_MOUSE])],
  deckOff: [msg(ID_CLEAR_DIGITAL_MAPPINGS), settings([SETTING_SMOOTH_ABSOLUTE_MOUSE, 0],
    [SETTING_LEFT_TRACKPAD_MODE, TRACKPAD_NONE], [SETTING_RIGHT_TRACKPAD_MODE, TRACKPAD_NONE],
    [SETTING_LEFT_TRACKPAD_CLICK_PRESSURE, 0xffff], [SETTING_RIGHT_TRACKPAD_CLICK_PRESSURE, 0xffff])],
  // the Deck's watchdog brings lizard mode back unless this comes again (SDL: FeedDeckLizardWatchdog)
  deckKeep: [msg(ID_CLEAR_DIGITAL_MAPPINGS), settings([SETTING_RIGHT_TRACKPAD_MODE, TRACKPAD_NONE])],
  tritonOff: [settings([SETTING_LIZARD_MODE, 0])],
  tritonOn: [settings([SETTING_LIZARD_MODE, 1])],
};
/** how often the Deck and the 2026 controller are told again (ms): SDL's 3 s for the 2026 controller; the Deck's
 *  every 200 reads, about 3 s at 60 frames a second */
const KEEP_MS = { deck: 1000, triton: 2500 } as const;
/** the 2026 controller stops its motors on its own after about 50 ms: told again this often while they run */
const TRITON_RUMBLE_MS = 40;

let log: (s: string) => void = () => {};

/** a Gamepad.buttons entry */
interface Button { pressed: boolean; touched: boolean; value: number }

/** One controller: a HID interface of Valve's (a dongle has one per controller it links), and the Gamepad the page sees
 *  for it once it reported (connected). */
class SteamPad {
  readonly gp: Gamepad;
  readonly product: Product;
  /** a state report came, and a dongle did not say its controller went since */
  connected = false;
  /** the page keeps lizard mode off now */
  private lizardOff = false;
  private keep = 0;
  private reader = new D0GReader();
  private queue: Promise<unknown> = Promise.resolve();
  private firstReport = true;
  private buttons: Button[];
  private axes: number[];
  // rumble: the motors' levels (0..65535), until when, the timer that renews or stops them
  private motors: [number, number] = [0, 0];
  private motorsUntil = 0;
  private motorTimer = 0;

  constructor(readonly dev: HidDevice, index: number) {
    this.product = productOf(dev)!;
    this.buttons = Array.from({ length: NBUTTONS }, () => ({ pressed: false, touched: false, value: 0 }));
    this.axes = [0, 0, 0, 0];
    const self = this;
    const actuator = this.product.kind === 'd0g' ? null : {
      type: 'dual-rumble', effects: ['dual-rumble'],
      playEffect(_type: string, p: { duration?: number; strongMagnitude?: number; weakMagnitude?: number } = {}) {
        self.rumble(p.strongMagnitude ?? 0, p.weakMagnitude ?? 0, p.duration ?? 0);
        return Promise.resolve('complete');
      },
      reset() { self.rumble(0, 0, 0); return Promise.resolve('complete'); },
    };
    this.gp = { id: steamPadId(dev.productId), index, mapping: 'standard', connected: false, timestamp: 0,
      axes: this.axes, buttons: this.buttons, vibrationActuator: actuator, hapticActuators: [] } as unknown as Gamepad;
  }

  get name() { return `${this.product.name} (${hex4(VALVE)}:${hex4(this.dev.productId)})`; }

  /** a report from the interface */
  onReport = (e: Event) => {
    const { reportId, data } = e as HidReportEvent;
    if (this.firstReport) {
      this.firstReport = false;
      const bytes = Array.from(new Uint8Array(data.buffer, data.byteOffset, Math.min(data.byteLength, 32)), b => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0'));
      log(`[pad] ${this.name}: first report, id ${reportId}, ${data.byteLength} bytes: ${bytes.join(' ')}`);
    }
    const r = this.product.kind === 'd0g' ? reportId === 0 ? this.reader.read(data) : null
      : this.product.kind === 'deck' ? reportId === 0 ? readDeck(data) : null : readTriton(reportId, data);
    if (r === 'off') { this.gone('its controller went away'); return; }
    if (r === null || r === 'on') return;
    if (!this.connected) {
      this.connected = true;
      (this.gp as unknown as { connected: boolean }).connected = true;
      log(`[pad] ${this.name} is controller ${this.gp.index} (WebHID)`);
      announce('gamepadconnected', this.gp);
      this.lizard(active);
    }
    this.show(r);
  };

  private show(s: SteamState) {
    for (let i = 0; i < NBUTTONS; i++) {
      const b = this.buttons[i], on = (s.buttons >> i & 1) === 1;
      b.pressed = on; b.touched = on;
      b.value = i === SB.LT ? s.lt : i === SB.RT ? s.rt : on ? 1 : 0;
    }
    this.axes[0] = s.lx; this.axes[1] = s.ly; this.axes[2] = s.rx; this.axes[3] = s.ry;
    (this.gp as unknown as { timestamp: number }).timestamp = performance.now();
  }

  /** the controller is no more (a dongle's went, the interface went or closed); there: it is still there to be told
   *  to be a mouse again (the page closes it) */
  gone(why: string, there = false) {
    if (there) this.lizard(false);
    else { this.lizardOff = false; clearInterval(this.keep); this.keep = 0; }
    this.rumble(0, 0, 0);
    if (!this.connected) return;
    this.connected = false;
    (this.gp as unknown as { connected: boolean }).connected = false;
    this.show({ buttons: 0, lx: 0, ly: 0, rx: 0, ry: 0, lt: 0, rt: 0 });
    log(`[pad] ${this.name}: ${why}`);
    announce('gamepaddisconnected', this.gp);
  }

  /** feature reports one after another (a failed one tried again: SDL's dongle needs it), then for the Deck's settings
   *  a read (SDL drops the report a change of settings leaves) */
  private send(reports: number[][], what: string, readBack = false) {
    const id = this.product.kind === 'triton' ? 1 : 0, size = id ? 63 : 64;
    this.queue = this.queue.then(async () => {
      for (const r of reports) {
        const buf = new Uint8Array(size);
        buf.set(r);
        for (let tries = 0; ; tries++) {
          try { await this.dev.sendFeatureReport(id, buf); break; }
          catch (err) {
            if (tries >= 4 || !this.dev.opened) { log(`[pad] ${this.name}: ${what}: ${(err as Error)?.message ?? err}`); return; }
            await new Promise(res => setTimeout(res, 2));
          }
        }
      }
      if (readBack) await this.dev.receiveFeatureReport(0).catch(() => {});
    });
    return this.queue;
  }

  /** a dongle asked whether its controller is there (the 2015 one's answers with a link report): on its interfaces with
   *  Valve's reports (vendor-defined), not a keyboard's or a mouse's */
  ask() {
    if (this.product.kind === 'd0g' && this.product.dongle && this.dev.collections.some(c => c.usagePage >= 0xff00))
      void this.send([msg(ID_DONGLE_GET_WIRELESS_STATE)], 'the dongle\'s question');
  }

  /** lizard mode off (on: while the game has the page) or back */
  lizard(off: boolean) {
    off &&= this.connected && this.dev.opened;
    if (off === this.lizardOff) return;
    this.lizardOff = off;
    clearInterval(this.keep); this.keep = 0;
    const k = this.product.kind;
    if (off) {
      void this.send(k === 'd0g' ? LIZARD.d0gOff : k === 'deck' ? LIZARD.deckOff : LIZARD.tritonOff, 'lizard mode off', k === 'deck');
      if (k !== 'd0g') this.keep = setInterval(() => void this.send(k === 'deck' ? LIZARD.deckKeep : LIZARD.tritonOff,
        'lizard mode kept off', k === 'deck'), KEEP_MS[k]) as unknown as number;
    } else if (this.dev.opened && k !== 'deck') {
      void this.send(k === 'd0g' ? LIZARD.d0gOn : LIZARD.tritonOn, 'lizard mode back');
    }
  }

  /** the game's motors, strong (low frequency) and weak (high) 0..1, for ms (0: stop) */
  rumble(strong: number, weak: number, ms: number) {
    const k = this.product.kind;
    if (k === 'd0g') return;
    const to: [number, number] = ms > 0 && this.lizardOff ? [Math.round(unit(strong) * 65535), Math.round(unit(weak) * 65535)] : [0, 0];
    const was = this.motors, now = performance.now();
    this.motors = to;
    this.motorsUntil = to[0] || to[1] ? now + ms : 0;
    if (to[0] !== was[0] || to[1] !== was[1]) this.motorsOut();
    if ((to[0] || to[1]) && !this.motorTimer) {
      this.motorTimer = setInterval(() => {
        if (performance.now() >= this.motorsUntil) {
          this.motors = [0, 0];
          clearInterval(this.motorTimer); this.motorTimer = 0;
          this.motorsOut();
        } else if (k === 'triton') this.motorsOut();
      }, TRITON_RUMBLE_MS) as unknown as number;
    } else if (!to[0] && !to[1] && this.motorTimer) { clearInterval(this.motorTimer); this.motorTimer = 0; }
  }

  private motorsOut() {
    if (!this.dev.opened) return;
    const [l, r] = this.motors;
    if (this.product.kind === 'deck') {
      void this.send([[ID_TRIGGER_RUMBLE_CMD, 0, 0, 0, 0, l & 0xff, l >> 8, r & 0xff, r >> 8, 2, 0]], 'rumble');
    } else {
      // output report 0x80: type, intensity (16 bits), the left motor's speed (16) and gain, the right one's
      const out = new Uint8Array([0, 0, 0, l & 0xff, l >> 8, 0, r & 0xff, r >> 8, 0]);
      this.queue = this.queue.then(() => this.dev.sendReport(0x80, out)).catch(() => {});
    }
  }

  /** stop for good: lizard mode back, then the interface closed */
  close() {
    this.gone('closed', true);
    this.dev.removeEventListener('inputreport', this.onReport);
    this.queue = this.queue.then(() => this.dev.opened ? this.dev.close() : undefined).catch(() => {});
  }
}

/** a gamepad event for one of these, as the browser sends one for its own (the listeners read e.gamepad) */
function announce(type: 'gamepadconnected' | 'gamepaddisconnected', gp: Gamepad) {
  if (typeof dispatchEvent !== 'function') return;
  const e = new Event(type);
  Object.defineProperty(e, 'gamepad', { value: gp });
  dispatchEvent(e);
}

const pads = new Map<HidDevice, SteamPad>();
let users = 0;
/** the game runs and has the page, visible and focused: lizard mode off */
let active = false;
const FIRST_INDEX = 16;

function update() {
  const on = users > 0 && typeof document !== 'undefined' && document.visibilityState === 'visible' && document.hasFocus();
  if (on === active) return;
  active = on;
  for (const p of pads.values()) p.lizard(on);
}

/** open a controller the player picked (in this visit or before), once */
async function add(dev: HidDevice) {
  if (!productOf(dev) || pads.has(dev) || !users) return;
  const used = new Set([...pads.values()].map(p => p.gp.index));
  let index = FIRST_INDEX;
  while (used.has(index)) index++;
  const p = new SteamPad(dev, index);
  pads.set(dev, p);
  try { if (!dev.opened) await dev.open(); }
  catch (err) {
    log(`[pad] ${p.name}: cannot open it: ${(err as Error)?.message ?? err}`);
    pads.delete(dev);
    return;
  }
  if (pads.get(dev) !== p) return;
  log(`[pad] ${p.name}: opened, ${dev.collections.map(c => `${hex4(c.usagePage)}:${hex4(c.usage)}`).join(' ') || 'no collections'}`);
  dev.addEventListener('inputreport', p.onReport);
  p.ask();
}

function remove(dev: HidDevice) {
  const p = pads.get(dev);
  if (!p) return;
  pads.delete(dev);
  p.close();
}

const onHidConnect = (e: Event) => void add((e as HidConnectionEvent).device);
const onHidDisconnect = (e: Event) => {
  const p = pads.get((e as HidConnectionEvent).device);
  if (p) { p.gone('unplugged'); pads.delete(p.dev); }
};
/** the tab closing: the 2015 controller told to be a mouse again (the others do it themselves) */
const onPageHide = () => { for (const p of pads.values()) p.lizard(false); };

/**
 * While the game runs (the PadPoller's, until the function it returns is called): the controllers picked before
 * opened, those plugged in or picked later too, lizard mode off while the page is visible and focused.  logf: the
 * page's log.
 */
export function useSteamPads(logf: (s: string) => void): () => void {
  const h = hid();
  if (!h) return () => {};
  log = logf;
  if (users++ === 0) {
    h.addEventListener('connect', onHidConnect);
    h.addEventListener('disconnect', onHidDisconnect);
    document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', update);
    addEventListener('focus', update);
    addEventListener('blur', update);
    addEventListener('pagehide', onPageHide);
    h.getDevices().then(ds => { for (const d of ds) void add(d); }, err => log(`[pad] WebHID: ${(err as Error)?.message ?? err}`));
    update();
  }
  let done = false;
  return () => {
    if (done) return;
    done = true;
    if (--users > 0) return;
    h.removeEventListener('connect', onHidConnect);
    h.removeEventListener('disconnect', onHidDisconnect);
    document.removeEventListener('visibilitychange', update);
    removeEventListener('focus', update);
    removeEventListener('blur', update);
    removeEventListener('pagehide', onPageHide);
    active = false;
    for (const d of [...pads.keys()]) remove(d);
  };
}

/** The browser's controllers (navigator.getGamepads) with these beside them, each at its index (the places between
 *  are null): what every reader of controllers in the page reads. */
export function allPads(): (Gamepad | null)[] {
  let own: (Gamepad | null)[] = [];
  try { own = typeof navigator.getGamepads === 'function' ? Array.from(navigator.getGamepads()) : []; } catch { /* none */ }
  if (!pads.size) return own;
  for (const p of pads.values()) {
    if (!p.connected) continue;
    while (own.length < p.gp.index) own.push(null);
    own[p.gp.index] = p.gp;
  }
  return own;
}

/** whether this browser can read them (WebHID: Chrome, Edge and Opera on a computer) */
export const steamPadsPossible = () => !!hid();

const FILTERS = Object.keys(STEAM_PRODUCTS).map(p => ({ vendorId: VALVE, productId: +p }));

/** The browser's list of these controllers to pick from (only from a click: Chrome asks for one).  The one picked
 *  works at once while a game runs, else from the next Play, and on later visits without asking.  Resolves to the
 *  names of those picked (none: the list closed). */
export async function connectSteamPad(): Promise<string[]> {
  const h = hid();
  if (!h) return [];
  const got = await h.requestDevice({ filters: FILTERS });
  for (const d of got) void add(d);
  return [...new Set(got.map(d => productOf(d)?.name).filter((n): n is string => !!n))];
}

/** the names of these controllers picked in this browser before (they open on Play) */
export async function steamPadsPicked(): Promise<string[]> {
  const h = hid();
  if (!h) return [];
  try { return [...new Set((await h.getDevices()).map(d => productOf(d)?.name).filter((n): n is string => !!n))]; }
  catch { return []; }
}

// The autotest's "real input" commands (nsdown, nstap, nstype, nsmouse,
// nsfocus ...; runtime/autotest.c) arrive as requests in the mailbox's
// synthetic ring.  On the Mac they became NSEvents posted into AppKit's
// queue; here they become DOM events dispatched on the game element, so they
// go through the same handlers as a person's keys and mouse (index.ts),
// including the browser-specific rules (Meta, Caps Lock on macOS, focus).
// Synthetic events are untrusted: they never trigger browser defaults.
import { CODE_OF_DIK, keyFor, strokeFor } from './keymap';
import {
  ISYN_ALT, ISYN_CTRL, ISYN_META, ISYN_SHIFT, KSYN_CHAR_DOWN, KSYN_CHAR_UP, KSYN_DOWN, KSYN_FOCUS_IN, KSYN_FOCUS_OUT,
  KSYN_MOUSE_DOWN, KSYN_MOUSE_MOVE, KSYN_MOUSE_UP, KSYN_REPEAT, KSYN_SCROLL, KSYN_UP,
} from './proto';

export interface SynReq { type: number; dik: number; mods: number; ch: number; a: number; b: number }
export interface SynthHooks {
  element: HTMLElement;
  mac: boolean;
  layout(): Map<string, string> | null;
  focus(active: boolean): void;          // the page's own blur/focus handling, as for a real switch
  log(s: string): void;
}

const MOD_CODES: [number, string][] = [[ISYN_META, 'MetaLeft'], [ISYN_SHIFT, 'ShiftLeft'], [ISYN_CTRL, 'ControlLeft'], [ISYN_ALT, 'AltLeft']];

export class SynthDriver {
  private held = new Set<string>();      // modifier codes held by synthetic events
  private caps = false;
  private mx = 0.5; private my = 0.5; private buttons = 0;
  constructor(private o: SynthHooks) {}

  private mods() {
    const has = (a: string, b: string) => this.held.has(a) || this.held.has(b);
    return { shiftKey: has('ShiftLeft', 'ShiftRight'), ctrlKey: has('ControlLeft', 'ControlRight'),
      altKey: has('AltLeft', 'AltRight'), metaKey: has('MetaLeft', 'MetaRight') };
  }
  private key(type: 'keydown' | 'keyup', code: string, repeat = false) {
    const m = this.mods();
    const ev = new KeyboardEvent(type, {
      code, key: keyFor(code, m.shiftKey, this.caps, this.o.mac, this.o.layout()), repeat, ...m,
      modifierCapsLock: this.caps, bubbles: true, cancelable: true, composed: true,
    });
    this.o.element.dispatchEvent(ev);
  }
  /** a modifier or Caps Lock going down or up, with the modifier state the browser would report */
  private modifier(code: string, down: boolean) {
    if (code === 'CapsLock') {
      // macOS: one event per toggle, keydown when it turns on, keyup when it
      // turns off; elsewhere a normal press and release
      if (this.o.mac) { if (!down) return; this.caps = !this.caps; this.key(this.caps ? 'keydown' : 'keyup', code); }
      else { if (down) this.caps = !this.caps; this.key(down ? 'keydown' : 'keyup', code); }
      return;
    }
    if (down) { this.held.add(code); this.key('keydown', code); }
    else { this.held.delete(code); this.key('keyup', code); }
  }
  private isMod(code: string) { return code === 'CapsLock' || /^(Shift|Control|Alt|Meta)(Left|Right)$/.test(code); }
  private press(code: string, type: number) {
    if (this.isMod(code)) { if (type !== KSYN_REPEAT) this.modifier(code, type !== KSYN_UP); return; }
    if (type === KSYN_UP) this.key('keyup', code); else this.key('keydown', code, type === KSYN_REPEAT);
  }
  private pointer(type: string, extra: PointerEventInit = {}) {
    const rc = this.o.element.getBoundingClientRect();
    const init: PointerEventInit = { clientX: rc.left + this.mx * rc.width, clientY: rc.top + this.my * rc.height,
      pointerId: 1, pointerType: 'mouse', isPrimary: true, buttons: this.buttons, bubbles: true, cancelable: true,
      composed: true, ...this.mods(), ...extra };
    this.o.element.dispatchEvent(type === 'wheel' ? new WheelEvent(type, init as WheelEventInit) : new PointerEvent(type, init));
  }

  handle(q: SynReq) {
    switch (q.type) {
      case KSYN_DOWN: case KSYN_UP: case KSYN_REPEAT: {
        const code = CODE_OF_DIK[q.dik];
        if (!code) { this.o.log(`[key] synthetic key: no DOM code for DIK 0x${q.dik.toString(16)}`); return; }
        const mods = MOD_CODES.filter(([bit]) => q.mods & bit).map(([, c]) => c);
        // "cmd+shift+Q": modifiers down in order, the key, and on release the reverse
        if (q.type === KSYN_DOWN) for (const c of mods) this.modifier(c, true);
        this.press(code, q.type);
        if (q.type === KSYN_UP) for (const c of mods.reverse()) this.modifier(c, false);
        return;
      }
      case KSYN_CHAR_DOWN: case KSYN_CHAR_UP: {
        const ch = String.fromCodePoint(q.ch);
        const s = strokeFor(ch, this.o.layout());
        if (!s) {
          if (q.type === KSYN_CHAR_DOWN)
            this.o.log(`[key] nstype: no key types U+${q.ch.toString(16).toUpperCase().padStart(4, '0')} on this layout`);
          return;
        }
        if (q.type === KSYN_CHAR_DOWN) { if (s.shift) this.modifier('ShiftLeft', true); this.key('keydown', s.code); }
        else { this.key('keyup', s.code); if (s.shift) this.modifier('ShiftLeft', false); }
        return;
      }
      case KSYN_FOCUS_OUT: case KSYN_FOCUS_IN: this.o.focus(q.type === KSYN_FOCUS_IN); return;
      case KSYN_MOUSE_MOVE: this.mx = q.a; this.my = q.b; this.pointer('pointermove'); return;
      case KSYN_MOUSE_DOWN: case KSYN_MOUSE_UP: {
        // the script's 0 left, 1 right, 2 middle -> DOM button numbers and the buttons mask
        const b = q.a | 0, dom = b === 1 ? 2 : b === 2 ? 1 : 0, bit = b === 1 ? 2 : b === 2 ? 4 : 1;
        if (q.type === KSYN_MOUSE_DOWN) this.buttons |= bit; else this.buttons &= ~bit;
        this.pointer(q.type === KSYN_MOUSE_DOWN ? 'pointerdown' : 'pointerup', { button: dom });
        return;
      }
      case KSYN_SCROLL: this.pointer('wheel', { deltaY: -q.a, deltaMode: 1 } as WheelEventInit); return;
    }
  }
}

// Steering wheels (Logitech G29 and the like) through the Gamepad API, for the game's virtual pad (gamepad.ts):
// the wheel becomes the left stick's x, the gas and brake pedals the right and left triggers, the D-pad and buttons
// the pad's, and the game is offered a driving device for it (runtime/dinput_pad.c), whose steering follows the
// wheel's position as the PC game's own wheel support did.
//
// No browser maps a wheel: Chrome, Firefox and Safari give it mapping "", its axes and buttons as its HID report
// descriptor has them, and each browser places those axes in Gamepad.axes its own way (Placement).  So for the
// models whose descriptor is known (ModelAxes: Logitech's G29, G920 and G923, G25, G27, Driving Force GT; Fanatec's
// bases) the page takes the wheel and each pedal from it, placed as the browser does; for any other wheel, or where
// the wheel shows a number of axes its descriptor does not explain or its axes do not sit where it puts them (a
// driver's settings, G HUB's combined pedals), it guesses from where the axes sit when the wheel shows up.  A pedal
// rests at one end of its axis (+1 on Logitech's and Fanatec's, which report a released pedal as their most), so read
// as a stick it held the stick down: the bug this file fixed first.  The player can teach the page the right layout
// (WheelLearn, in the Controls sheet: turn the wheel, press each pedal), kept in this browser per model.  A shifter on
// the wheel (Logitech's Driving Force Shifter, the G25's and G27's, one on a Fanatec base) shows its gears as buttons;
// the game's gearbox only shifts up and down,
// so a move of the lever into a gear is one shift up or down, or the lever holds the handbrake (Shifter), as the
// player picks in the same sheet.
//
// An RC radio (a drone's transmitter running EdgeTX or OpenTX, in its USB joystick mode) drives as a wheel too: its
// channels are axes, CH1 to CH8 placed by usage (X, Y, Z, Rx, Ry, Rz, Slider, Dial: axes 0 to 7 in every browser but
// Linux's, where the eight come one after another all the same), in the order its mixer sends them, AETR unless the
// player changed it: aileron (the right stick across), elevator (the right stick up and down in mode 2, the left in
// mode 1), throttle (the stick without a spring, down when the radio is switched on), rudder, then the switches, each
// an axis at -1, 0 or +1.  Channels past the eighth are buttons.  So the right stick steers, the throttle stick is
// the gas and the elevator pulled back the brake (radioMap); none of its switches does anything until the player sets
// them up (WheelLearn: flip the switch for nitrous, the handbrake, a respawn), and with nothing the player can press,
// a stick or a switch moved half way takes the game's controller back from another one (gamepad.ts).

import { PAD_A, PAD_B, PAD_BACK, PAD_DDOWN, PAD_DLEFT, PAD_DRIGHT, PAD_DUP, PAD_HOME, PAD_LB, PAD_LS, PAD_RB, PAD_RS,
  PAD_START, PAD_X, PAD_Y } from './proto';
import { localStore, SHIFTER, WHEEL } from '../app/prefs';

/** a pedal: its axis, its value let go and pressed to the floor (gas and brake on one axis: the two halves); pad: the
 *  Gamepad.id of pedals on their own USB the axis is on, not the wheel's */
export interface Pedal { axis: number; rest: number; full: number; pad?: string }
/** how a wheel's axes and buttons make the pad */
export interface WheelMap {
  steer: number;                 // the wheel's axis
  centre: number;                // its value straight ahead
  lock: number;                  // how far from the centre is full lock to the right (negative: the axis runs the other way)
  gas: Pedal | null;
  brake: Pedal | null;
  handbrake?: Pedal;             // a handbrake lever on the wheel's base: pulled past HANDBRAKE_ON, the pad's X
  buttons: number[];             // buttons[i]: the PAD_* button i is (-1: none)
  gears?: number[];              // the shifter's buttons: 1st to 6th gear, then reverse (-1: none); absent: no shifter
  dpad?: [number, number];       // a hat switch read as two axes, x and y (Linux), where known
  placed?: Placement;            // from the model's descriptor, its axes placed so; absent: guessed
  learned?: boolean;             // set up by the player (WheelLearn), not guessed
  switches?: Switch[];           // a radio's switches the player set up
}
/** a radio's switch as one of the pad's buttons (pad: a PAD_* number): on while its axis sits near on (a channel
 *  at the switch's position), or while its button is pressed (a channel past the eighth) */
export interface Switch { pad: number; axis?: number; on?: number; button?: number }
/** how near its position (on) a switch's axis reads while it is there */
const SWITCH_NEAR = 0.3;

/** a HID axis by its usage on the Generic Desktop page ('hat': the hat switch, the D-pad) */
export type Usage = 'x' | 'y' | 'z' | 'rx' | 'ry' | 'rz' | 'slider' | 'dial' | 'hat';
/** a model's axes: those of its HID report descriptor, in the descriptor's order where that is known (listed), and
 *  which is the wheel, which each pedal and the handbrake's port */
export interface ModelAxes {
  axes: Usage[]; listed: boolean; steer: Usage; gas: Usage; brake: Usage; clutch?: Usage; handbrake?: Usage;
}

/**
 * Where a browser puts a wheel's axes in Gamepad.axes (Chromium device/gamepad, Firefox dom/gamepad, WebKit
 * platform/gamepad/mac):
 *   usage   Chrome on Windows and macOS, Firefox on Windows: at its usage less X's: X 0, Y 1, Z 2, Rx 3, Ry 4, Rz 5,
 *           Slider 6, Dial 7, the hat switch 9 (one axis: hatDirs); a usage seen again (another collection's) is left
 *           out, and an axis of another page put in a place no usage took
 *   kernel  Chrome and Firefox on Linux (joydev, evdev): the axes Linux made of them one after another in the order
 *           of its codes (ABS_X, Y, Z, RX, RY, RZ, THROTTLE the slider, RUDDER the dial), the hat switch two (ABS_HAT0X
 *           and HAT0Y)
 *   listed  Firefox on macOS: in the descriptor's order, X to Rz and the hat switch (one axis)
 *   tree    Safari: in the descriptor's order, X to Rz; no hat switch, so no D-pad
 * A known model's axes are placed the one way that gives as many axes as the wheel shows; failing that, by usage
 * where the wheel shows more (a driver's or another collection's after them: X to Rz sit where they do by usage on
 * Linux too).
 */
export type Placement = 'usage' | 'kernel' | 'listed' | 'tree';
const PLACEMENTS: Placement[] = ['usage', 'kernel', 'listed', 'tree'];
const USAGE_AT: Record<Usage, number> = { x: 0, y: 1, z: 2, rx: 3, ry: 4, rz: 5, slider: 6, dial: 7, hat: 9 };
const KERNEL_CODE: Record<Usage, number> = { x: 0, y: 1, z: 2, rx: 3, ry: 4, rz: 5, slider: 6, dial: 7, hat: 16 };

/** each of the model's axes' index when placed so (a hat switch read as two: its x, y after it), and how many axes
 *  the browser shows then; null for a placement in the descriptor's order where that order is not known */
export function placeAxes(m: ModelAxes, p: Placement): { at: Partial<Record<Usage, number>>; length: number } | null {
  const at: Partial<Record<Usage, number>> = {};
  let length = 0;
  if (p === 'usage') for (const u of m.axes) { at[u] = USAGE_AT[u]; length = Math.max(length, USAGE_AT[u] + 1); }
  else if (p === 'kernel') {
    for (const u of [...m.axes].sort((a, b) => KERNEL_CODE[a] - KERNEL_CODE[b])) { at[u] = length; length += u === 'hat' ? 2 : 1; }
  } else if (!m.listed) return null;
  else for (const u of m.axes) if (u !== 'slider' && u !== 'dial' && (u !== 'hat' || p === 'listed')) at[u] = length++;
  return { at, length };
}

  '0eb7:0001': { ...FTEC_OLD, buttons: FTEC_BUTTONS, gears: FTEC_GEARS },                       // ClubSport V2
  '0eb7:038e': { ...FTEC_OLD, buttons: FTEC_BUTTONS, gears: FTEC_GEARS },                       // ClubSport V1
  '0eb7:0197': { ...FTEC_OLD, gears: PS_GEARS }, '0eb7:0011': FTEC_OLD,                         // Porsche 911 wheels, CSR Elite
};
// whole vendors that make wheels and little else: Thrustmaster's wheel bases, Simagic, Simucube, Moza ... (Fanatec's
// pedals, shifters and handbrakes come on their own too: its bases are KNOWN, a new one by its name, "FANATEC Wheel")
const WHEEL_IDS = new Set(['044f:b65d', '044f:b65e', '044f:b664', '044f:b669', '044f:b66d', '044f:b66e', '044f:b66f',
  '044f:b677', '044f:b67f', '044f:b691', '044f:b692', '044f:b696', '045e:02a2', '0483:0522', '0483:a355', '0079:1864',
  '11ff:0511', '1209:ffb0', '3416:0301', '3416:0302']);
const WHEEL_VENDORS = new Set(['16d0', '2433', '346e']);
// a wheel maker's pedals, shifter, handbrake or button box on its own USB: no wheel, though its vendor is a wheel's
const NOT_WHEEL = /\b(pedals?|shifter|handbrake|hand brake|button ?box)\b/i;

/** pedals on their own USB: their axes by usage (in the descriptor's order), which is the gas and the brake, and
 *  where a pedal let go reads */
export interface PedalSet { axes: Usage[]; gas: Usage; brake: Usage; rest: number }
// Fanatec's on USB, not through a base: the ClubSport Pedals V3 (an SDL user's report, PadForge issue 81: X the gas,
// Y the brake, Z the clutch, Rx a handbrake's place, 0 let go), the CSL Elite, the CSL with the load cell and the
// ClubSport USB adapter so too (BeamNG's maps); the ClubSport Pedals V1 and V2 Rx, Ry and Rz, let go at their most
// (Assetto Corsa's preset, BeamNG's map)
const FTEC_USB_PEDALS: PedalSet = { axes: ['x', 'y', 'z', 'rx'], gas: 'x', brake: 'y', rest: -1 };
const PEDAL_SETS: Record<string, PedalSet> = {
  '0eb7:183b': FTEC_USB_PEDALS, '0eb7:6204': FTEC_USB_PEDALS, '0eb7:6205': FTEC_USB_PEDALS, '0eb7:6206': FTEC_USB_PEDALS,
  '0eb7:1a95': FTEC_USB_PEDALS, '0eb7:1839': { axes: ['rx', 'ry', 'rz'], gas: 'rx', brake: 'ry', rest: 1 },
};
/** the known pedals Gamepad.id is, or null */
export function pedalSetOf(id: string): PedalSet | null {
  const u = usbIds(id);
  return (u && PEDAL_SETS[`${u.vendor}:${u.product}`]) || null;
}
/** whether Gamepad.id is pedals on their own: known ones, or named so (no wheel) */
export function isPedals(id: string): boolean {
  return !!pedalSetOf(id) || (/\bpedals?\b/i.test(id) && !wheelOf(id));
}
/** known pedals' gas and brake as the wheel's (id: theirs; n: the axes the browser shows of them): an axis at its
 *  usage where the browser places them so (Chrome, Firefox on Windows: as many axes), else in the descriptor's order */
export function pedalsOf(id: string, set: PedalSet, n: number): { gas: Pedal; brake: Pedal } {
  const at = (u: Usage) => n > USAGE_AT[u] ? USAGE_AT[u] : set.axes.indexOf(u);
  const p = (u: Usage): Pedal => ({ axis: at(u), rest: set.rest, full: -set.rest, pad: id });
  return { gas: p(set.gas), brake: p(set.brake) };
}
// RC radios: EdgeTX's joystick (pid.codes 1209:4f54), or one that names its firmware or maker ("EdgeTX RadioMaster
// TX16S Joystick", OpenTX's "FrSky Taranis Joystick" on STMicro's demo ids, which other devices use too)
const RADIO_IDS = new Set(['1209:4f54']);
const RADIO_NAME = /\b(edgetx|opentx|frsky|radiomaster|taranis)\b/i;

/** the USB vendor and product from Gamepad.id: Chrome writes "Name (... Vendor: 046d Product: c24f)", Firefox
 *  "046d-c24f-Name" */
export function usbIds(id: string): { vendor: string; product: string } | null {
  const c = /Vendor:\s*([0-9a-f]{4})\s*Product:\s*([0-9a-f]{4})/i.exec(id) ?? /^([0-9a-f]{1,4})-([0-9a-f]{1,4})-/i.exec(id);
  return c ? { vendor: c[1].toLowerCase().padStart(4, '0'), product: c[2].toLowerCase().padStart(4, '0') } : null;
}

/** whether Gamepad.id is a steering wheel's, and which (asked every frame: kept per id) */
const seenIds = new Map<string, WheelInfo | null>();
export function wheelOf(id: string): WheelInfo | null {
  let w = seenIds.get(id);
  if (w !== undefined) return w;
  const u = usbIds(id), key = u ? `${u.vendor}:${u.product}` : '';
  const k = KNOWN[key], named = /\bwheel\b|driving force|steering/i.test(id);
  w = k ? { vendor: u!.vendor, product: u!.product, ...k }
    : RADIO_IDS.has(key) || RADIO_NAME.test(id) ? { vendor: u?.vendor ?? '', product: u?.product ?? '', layout: 'radio', degrees: 0 }
    : (u && (WHEEL_IDS.has(key) || (WHEEL_VENDORS.has(u.vendor) && !NOT_WHEEL.test(id)))) || named
    ? { vendor: u?.vendor ?? '', product: u?.product ?? '', layout: 'generic', degrees: 0 } : null;
  if (seenIds.size < 64) seenIds.set(id, w);
  return w;
}

/** whether an axis value is a hat switch read as one axis, let go (it reads outside -1..1 then) */
const hatRest = (v: number) => Math.abs(v) > 1.05;

/**
 * The layout of a wheel nobody set up: axes0 is where its axes sat when it showed up (the browser shows a controller
 * after a button press, so the pedals are let go then).  Full lock is DEFAULT_LOCK_DEGREES of its rotation, or all
 * of it where that is unknown.  A known model's wheel and pedals come from its descriptor, placed as the browser
 * does: the placement that gives as many axes as the wheel shows (else by usage, where it shows more), with its wheel
 * off the ends and its gas and brake at one, or every axis 0 (Chrome on macOS before the wheel's first report, a
 * Fanatec base's twin: the pedals rest at +1 then).  Any other
 * wheel's are guessed: the wheel is the first axis that is neither a hat switch let go nor at an end (X, axis 0,
 * where the browser has no hat switch before it); pedals are the axes resting at an end, the first the gas, the
 * brake Rz (axis 5 where axes are placed by usage) or else the last; without one at an end, combined pedals on the
 * axis after the wheel, gas up, brake down.  The buttons and the shifter's are the model's, and its handbrake's
 * port where it rests at an end (a Fanatec base's).
 */
export function guessMap(info: WheelInfo, axes0: readonly number[], nbuttons: number): WheelMap {
  if (info.layout === 'radio') return radioMap(axes0, nbuttons);
  const table = info.buttons ?? (info.layout === 'ps' ? PS_BUTTONS : info.layout === 'xbox' ? XBOX_BUTTONS : GENERIC_BUTTONS);
  const gears = shifterOf(info, nbuttons);
  const base = {
    centre: 0, lock: info.degrees > DEFAULT_LOCK_DEGREES ? DEFAULT_LOCK_DEGREES / info.degrees : 1,
    buttons: Array.from({ length: nbuttons }, (_, i) => table[i] ?? -1), ...(gears ? { gears } : {}),
  };
  const atEnd = (v: number | undefined) => typeof v === 'number' && !hatRest(v) && Math.abs(v) >= 0.9;
  const pedal = (i: number): Pedal => { const r = atEnd(axes0[i]) ? Math.sign(axes0[i]) : 1; return { axis: i, rest: r, full: -r }; };
  const m = info.axes, unread = axes0.every(v => v === 0);
  const tries: [Placement, boolean][] = m ? [...PLACEMENTS.map((p): [Placement, boolean] => [p, false]), ['usage', true]] : [];
  for (const [p, more] of tries) {
    const a = placeAxes(m!, p);
    if (!a || (more ? axes0.length <= a.length : a.length !== axes0.length)) continue;
    const steer = a.at[m!.steer]!, gas = a.at[m!.gas]!, brake = a.at[m!.brake]!, hat = a.at.hat;
    if (!unread && (hatRest(axes0[steer]) || atEnd(axes0[steer]) || !atEnd(axes0[gas]) || !atEnd(axes0[brake]))) continue;
    // the handbrake's port only where it was seen let go, at an end (as a pedal)
    const hb = m!.handbrake !== undefined ? a.at[m!.handbrake] : undefined;
    return { ...base, steer, gas: pedal(gas), brake: pedal(brake),
      ...(hb !== undefined && atEnd(axes0[hb]) ? { handbrake: pedal(hb) } : {}),
      ...(p === 'kernel' && hat !== undefined ? { dpad: [hat, hat + 1] as [number, number] } : {}), placed: p };
  }
  const steer = Math.max(0, axes0.findIndex(v => !hatRest(v) && !atEnd(v)));
  const ends: number[] = [];
  axes0.forEach((v, i) => { if (i !== steer && atEnd(v)) ends.push(i); });
  let gas: Pedal | null = null, brake: Pedal | null = null;
  if (ends.length >= 2) {
    const b = ends.includes(5) && ends[0] !== 5 ? 5 : ends[ends.length - 1];
    gas = pedal(ends[0]); brake = pedal(b);
  } else if (ends.length === 1) gas = pedal(ends[0]);
  else {
    const c = axes0.findIndex((v, i) => i > steer && !hatRest(v));
    if (c >= 0) { gas = { axis: c, rest: 0, full: -1 }; brake = { axis: c, rest: 0, full: 1 }; }
  }
  return { ...base, steer, gas, brake };
}

/**
 * A radio's layout nobody set up: its first four channels are the sticks, the throttle the one of them resting at an
 * end when the radio showed up (pulled down; CH3, axis 2, in the usual AETR order where none or more than one does),
 * the other three aileron, elevator and rudder in that order.  The aileron steers, all of it full lock; the throttle
 * from that end to the other is the gas; the elevator pulled back the brake: the way the throttle rests, as both are
 * a stick's up and down and a radio sends every stick's up the same way.  No buttons and no switches.
 */
export function radioMap(axes0: readonly number[], nbuttons: number): WheelMap {
  const sticks = [0, 1, 2, 3], ends = sticks.filter(i => Math.abs(axes0[i] ?? 0) >= 0.9 && Math.abs(axes0[i]) <= 1.05);
  const thr = ends.length === 1 ? ends[0] : 2, down = ends.length === 1 ? Math.sign(axes0[thr]) : -1;
  const [ail, ele] = sticks.filter(i => i !== thr);
  return { steer: ail, centre: 0, lock: 1, gas: { axis: thr, rest: down, full: -down }, brake: { axis: ele, rest: 0, full: down },
    buttons: Array.from({ length: nbuttons }, () => -1), switches: [] };
}

/** a hat switch read as one axis (Chrome, Firefox on Windows and macOS) as PAD_D* bits: positions 0 (up) to 7
 *  (up-left) at 2/7 apart from -1; anything else (let go, or 0 before the first report) is none */
export function hatDirs(v: number): number {
  if (!(v >= -1.01 && v <= 1.01)) return 0;
  const pos = Math.round((v + 1) * 3.5);
  if (Math.abs(v - (pos / 3.5 - 1)) > 0.05) return 0;
  const U = 1 << PAD_DUP, D = 1 << PAD_DDOWN, L = 1 << PAD_DLEFT, R = 1 << PAD_DRIGHT;
  return [U, U | R, R, D | R, D, D | L, L, U | L][pos];
}

/** a hat switch read as two axes (Linux: x -1 left to 1 right, y -1 up to 1 down) as PAD_D* bits */
export function dpadDirs(x: number, y: number): number {
  return (x < -0.5 ? 1 << PAD_DLEFT : x > 0.5 ? 1 << PAD_DRIGHT : 0) | (y < -0.5 ? 1 << PAD_DUP : y > 0.5 ? 1 << PAD_DDOWN : 0);
}

const clamp = (v: number, lo: number, hi: number) => v < lo ? lo : v > hi ? hi : v;
/** the axes of the controllers besides the wheel, by Gamepad.id (pedals on their own USB) */
export type OtherAxes = (id: string) => readonly number[] | undefined;
/**
 * A pedal's travel, 0 let go to 1 on the floor.  Pedals on their own (pad) are read from others; they send nothing
 * until a pedal first moves ("pump a pedal": hid-fanatecff), so the browser's 0 is a pedal let go, as 0 is no value
 * an axis of theirs gives once read (12 or 16 bits from one end to the other).
 */
export function pedalValue(p: Pedal | null | undefined, axes: readonly number[], others?: OtherAxes): number {
  if (!p) return 0;
  let v = (p.pad !== undefined ? others?.(p.pad) : axes)?.[p.axis];
  if (p.pad !== undefined && v === 0) v = p.rest;
  if (typeof v !== 'number' || !isFinite(v) || p.full === p.rest) return 0;
  return clamp((v - p.rest) / (p.full - p.rest), 0, 1);
}
/** how far a handbrake lever is pulled (of its travel) for the handbrake: the game's is a button */
export const HANDBRAKE_ON = 0.3;

/** a wheel's state as the pad's: buttons (1 << PAD_*), and axes LX (the wheel, -1 .. 1 at full lock), LY, RX, RY
 *  (0), LT (the brake), RT (the gas).  hat: the axis the browser put the hat switch on, as one (-1: none seen);
 *  others: pedals on their own USB */
export function readWheel(axes: readonly number[], pressed: readonly boolean[], m: WheelMap, hat: number,
                          others?: OtherAxes): { buttons: number; axes: number[] } {
  let buttons = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < pressed.length && i < m.buttons.length; i++) if (pressed[i] && m.buttons[i] >= 0) buttons |= 1 << m.buttons[i];
  if (hat >= 0 && hat !== m.steer) buttons |= hatDirs(axes[hat]);
  if (m.dpad) buttons |= dpadDirs(axes[m.dpad[0]], axes[m.dpad[1]]);
  if (m.switches) for (const s of m.switches) if (switchOn(s, axes, pressed)) buttons |= 1 << s.pad;
  if (pedalValue(m.handbrake, axes) > HANDBRAKE_ON) buttons |= 1 << PAD_X;
  const w = axes[m.steer];
  const lx = typeof w === 'number' && isFinite(w) && m.lock ? clamp((w - m.centre) / m.lock, -1, 1) : 0;
  return { buttons, axes: [lx, 0, 0, 0, pedalValue(m.brake, axes, others), pedalValue(m.gas, axes, others)] };
}

/** whether a radio's switch is at its position (or its button pressed) */
function switchOn(s: Switch, axes: readonly number[], pressed: readonly boolean[]): boolean {
  if (s.button !== undefined) return !!pressed[s.button];
  const v = axes[s.axis ?? -1];
  return typeof v === 'number' && isFinite(v) && Math.abs(v - (s.on ?? 0)) < SWITCH_NEAR;
}

/** the axis carrying a hat switch read as one: one that reads outside -1..1 (let go), or -1 */
export function findHat(axes: readonly number[]): number {
  return axes.findIndex(hatRest);
}

// ---- the shifter ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/** the model's shifter buttons (1st to 6th gear, reverse; -1 one the wheel does not show), or null: none known */
export function shifterOf(info: WheelInfo, nbuttons: number): number[] | null {
  const g = info.gears?.map(i => i < nbuttons ? i : -1);
  return g && g.some(i => i >= 0) ? g : null;
}

/** the shifter's position: 1 to 6 a gear, 7 reverse, 0 neutral */
export function shifterGear(pressed: readonly boolean[], gears: readonly number[]): number {
  for (let i = 0; i < gears.length; i++) if (gears[i] >= 0 && pressed[gears[i]]) return i + 1;
  return 0;
}

/** what the shifter does: push-up, a move into 1st, 3rd or 5th gear shifts up and into 2nd, 4th or 6th down, reverse
 *  holds the handbrake; pull-up, the same but up and down the other way round; handbrake, any gear holds it; off */
export type ShifterMode = 'push-up' | 'pull-up' | 'handbrake' | 'off';
export const SHIFTER_MODES: readonly ShifterMode[] = ['push-up', 'pull-up', 'handbrake', 'off'];
/** how long (ms) a move into a gear presses shift up or down: the game reads its controller once a frame, 30 times
 *  a second at the least, and a press it must see, and a let-go between two */
export const SHIFT_PRESS_MS = 100;

/**
 * The shifter as the pad's buttons, those the wheel's own shift with (runtime/dinput_pad.c g_prof_wheel, or what the
 * player bound to them in the game's Controls): the right paddle (RB) shifts up, the left (LB) down, Square (X) is
 * the handbrake.  The game's gearbox only shifts up and down, one gear a press, so a move of the lever into a gear
 * is a press of SHIFT_PRESS_MS, and the next shift a move back through neutral and in again: a lever left in a gear
 * holds no button, and the paddles shift as before.  A handbrake gear holds it while the lever is there, but not a
 * lever there when the wheel showed up (left in reverse, it would hold the car) until it has been in neutral.
 */
export class Shifter {
  private gear = -1;          // the lever's position as last read (-1: not yet)
  private armed = false;      // the lever has been in neutral since the wheel showed up
  private press = 0;
  private until = 0;

  /** the PAD_* bits for the lever in gear (shifterGear) at time now (ms) */
  buttons(gear: number, mode: ShifterMode, now: number): number {
    if (this.gear < 0) this.gear = gear;
    if (gear === 0) this.armed = true;
    if (gear !== this.gear) {
      this.gear = gear;
      if (gear >= 1 && gear <= 6 && (mode === 'push-up' || mode === 'pull-up')) {
        this.press = (gear % 2 === 1) === (mode === 'push-up') ? 1 << PAD_RB : 1 << PAD_LB;
        this.until = now + SHIFT_PRESS_MS;
      }
    }
    const brake = mode === 'handbrake' ? gear > 0 : mode !== 'off' && gear === 7;
    return (now < this.until ? this.press : 0) | (brake && this.armed ? 1 << PAD_X : 0);
  }
}

/** a short line for the log: what drives what */
export function describeMap(m: WheelMap, hat: number): string {
  const name = (id: string) => id.replace(/\s*\([^)]*\)\s*$/, '').replace(/^[0-9a-f]{1,4}-[0-9a-f]{1,4}-/i, '');
  const p = (x: Pedal | null | undefined) => x ? `axis ${x.axis}${x.pad !== undefined ? ` of ${name(x.pad)}` : ''} ` +
    `(${x.rest.toFixed(2)} to ${x.full.toFixed(2)})` : 'none';
  const gears = m.gears ? m.gears.map(i => i >= 0 ? i : '-').join(' ') : '';
  if (m.switches) {
    const s = m.switches.map(x => `${SWITCH_PADS[x.pad] ?? x.pad} ${x.button !== undefined ? `button ${x.button}` : `axis ${x.axis} at ${x.on?.toFixed(2)}`}`);
    return `steering axis ${m.steer} (centre ${m.centre.toFixed(2)}, full lock ${m.lock >= 0 ? '+' : ''}${m.lock.toFixed(2)}), ` +
      `gas ${p(m.gas)}, brake ${p(m.brake)}, switches ${s.length ? s.join(', ') : 'none'}, ${m.learned ? 'set up by the player' : 'guessed'}`;
  }
  return `wheel axis ${m.steer} (centre ${m.centre.toFixed(2)}, full lock ${m.lock >= 0 ? '+' : ''}${m.lock.toFixed(2)}), ` +
    `gas ${p(m.gas)}, brake ${p(m.brake)}, ${m.handbrake ? `handbrake ${p(m.handbrake)}, ` : ''}` +
    `D-pad ${m.dpad ? `axes ${m.dpad.join(' and ')}` : hat >= 0 ? `axis ${hat}` : 'none seen'}, ` +
    `shifter ${gears ? `buttons ${gears}` : 'none known'}, ` +
    (m.learned ? 'set up by the player' : m.placed ? `the model's own (axes placed by ${m.placed})` : 'guessed');
}

// ---- the player's set-up, kept in this browser per model ------------------------------------------------------
/** a model's part of the keys: its USB ids, or its name where the browser gives none */
const modelKey = (id: string) => { const u = usbIds(id); return u ? `${u.vendor}:${u.product}` : id.slice(0, 80); };
/** the key a wheel's set-up is kept under */
export function wheelKey(id: string): string {
  return WHEEL + modelKey(id);
}
/** the model's layout (guessMap) with the player's set-up of its wheel and pedals over it: the buttons and the
 *  shifter stay the model's, so a set-up kept from before a change to those gets it; pedals set up on their own USB
 *  only while those are connected (has: whether a controller of that id is), else the guess's (the wheel's own) */
export function withSetUp(guess: WheelMap, kept: WheelMap, has: (id: string) => boolean = () => true): WheelMap {
  const here = (p: Pedal | null) => p?.pad === undefined || has(p.pad);
  const pedals = here(kept.gas) && here(kept.brake) ? { gas: kept.gas, brake: kept.brake } : { gas: guess.gas, brake: guess.brake };
  return { ...guess, steer: kept.steer, centre: kept.centre, lock: kept.lock, ...pedals,
    dpad: kept.dpad ?? guess.dpad, ...(guess.switches ? { switches: kept.switches ?? [] } : {}), placed: undefined, learned: true };
}
/** the picks of this page (storage may be off) */
const shifterPicks = new Map<string, ShifterMode>();
/** what the player picked for the model's shifter (default push-up) */
export function loadShifter(id: string): ShifterMode {
  let v: string | null | undefined = shifterPicks.get(modelKey(id));
  v ??= localStore.get(SHIFTER + modelKey(id));
  return SHIFTER_MODES.find(m => m === v) ?? 'push-up';
}
/** keep the player's pick for the model's shifter; gamepad.ts reads it again on the event */
export function saveShifter(id: string, mode: ShifterMode) {
  shifterPicks.set(modelKey(id), mode);
  localStore.set(SHIFTER + modelKey(id), mode);        // (storage off: for this page only)
  dispatchEvent(new Event(WHEEL_MAP_EVENT));
}
export function loadMap(id: string): WheelMap | null {
  try {
    const m = localStore.getJSON(wheelKey(id)) as WheelMap | null;
    const ok = (p: Pedal | null) => p === null ||
      (Number.isInteger(p.axis) && isFinite(p.rest) && isFinite(p.full) && (p.pad === undefined || typeof p.pad === 'string'));
    const sw = (s: Switch) => !!s && SWITCH_PADS[s.pad] !== undefined &&
      (s.button !== undefined ? Number.isInteger(s.button) : Number.isInteger(s.axis) && typeof s.on === 'number' && isFinite(s.on));
    if (m && m.switches !== undefined && !(Array.isArray(m.switches) && m.switches.every(sw))) return null;
    return m && Number.isInteger(m.steer) && isFinite(m.centre) && isFinite(m.lock) && m.lock !== 0 && ok(m.gas) && ok(m.brake) &&
      Array.isArray(m.buttons) ? m : null;
  } catch { return null; }
}
/** keep the player's set-up (null: back to the guess); gamepad.ts reads it again on the event */
export function saveMap(id: string, m: WheelMap | null) {
  if (m) localStore.setJSON(wheelKey(id), m); else localStore.remove(wheelKey(id));      // (storage off: the guess stays)
  dispatchEvent(new Event(WHEEL_MAP_EVENT));
}
export const WHEEL_MAP_EVENT = 'nfsu2-wheel-map';

// ---- teaching the page the wheel's axes -------------------------------------------------------------------------
export type LearnStep = 'rest' | 'steer' | 'gas' | 'brake' | SwitchStep | 'done';
/** a radio's steps after the brake, each a switch for one of the pad's buttons (runtime/dinput_pad.c g_prof_wheel:
 *  A nitrous, X the handbrake, View a respawn) */
export type SwitchStep = 'nitrous' | 'handbrake' | 'respawn';
const SWITCH_STEPS: Record<SwitchStep, { pad: number; next: LearnStep }> = {
  nitrous: { pad: PAD_A, next: 'handbrake' }, handbrake: { pad: PAD_X, next: 'respawn' }, respawn: { pad: PAD_BACK, next: 'done' },
};
/** the switches' buttons by name, for the log */
const SWITCH_PADS: Record<number, SwitchStep> = { [PAD_A]: 'nitrous', [PAD_X]: 'handbrake', [PAD_BACK]: 'respawn' };
const isSwitchStep = (s: LearnStep): s is SwitchStep => s in SWITCH_STEPS;
/** how long (ms) a control has to be held still where it is for its step to take it */
const HOLD_MS = 700;

/**
 * The set-up's steps, fed the wheel's axes every frame (feed): let go of everything (rest: where every axis sits),
 * turn the wheel right to where full lock should be (steer: the axis that moved most, its centre and the lock, held
 * there HOLD_MS), press the gas pedal down (gas: the axis that moved most but the wheel's), the brake (brake: the
 * same, or the gas's axis the other way: combined pedals).  Each step takes a control once it has moved far enough
 * and held still; then map() is the wheel's set-up, with base's buttons.  The pedals may be on another controller
 * (pads: their Gamepad.ids, fed their axes after the wheel's: pedals on their own USB), the wheel not; such a pedal
 * that read the browser's 0 let go had sent nothing yet (pedalValue): its rest is the end away from the floor.  A
 * radio's (radio: its sticks for the wheel and the pedals) goes on with a switch for each of SwitchStep, which skip()
 * passes: a button pressed that was not at rest, or else the axis furthest from its rest but the sticks', at the
 * position it is flipped to (another position of a switch already taken can be another's).
 */
export class WheelLearn {
  step: LearnStep = 'rest';
  /** 0..1: how far the step is (the hold) */
  progress = 0;
  private rest: number[] = [];
  private last: number[] = [];
  private restPressed: boolean[] = [];
  private lastPressed: boolean[] = [];
  private still = 0;
  private steer = -1;
  private centre = 0;
  private lock = 0;
  private gas: Pedal | null = null;
  private brake: Pedal | null = null;
  private switches: Switch[] = [];
  private lens: number[] = [];                // how many axes the wheel and each of pads showed, as last fed

  constructor(private base: WheelMap, private radio = false, private pads: readonly string[] = []) {}

  /** the wheel's axes now, at time now (ms), a radio's buttons, and the axes of pads (in their order); true when the
   *  step changed */
  feed(own: readonly number[], now: number, pressed: readonly boolean[] = [], more: readonly (readonly number[])[] = []): boolean {
    if (!this.radio) pressed = [];
    if (this.radio) more = [];
    const axes = more.length ? [...own, ...more.flat()] : own, wheel = own.length;
    this.lens = [wheel, ...more.map(a => a.length)];
    const moved = this.last.length !== axes.length || axes.some((v, i) => Math.abs(v - this.last[i]) > 0.01) ||
      pressed.length !== this.lastPressed.length || pressed.some((v, i) => v !== this.lastPressed[i]);
    if (moved) this.still = now;
    this.last = axes.slice();
    this.lastPressed = pressed.slice();
    const held = Math.min(1, (now - this.still) / HOLD_MS);
    const before = this.step;
    if (this.step !== 'rest' && more.length) this.restAgain(axes);
    switch (this.step) {
      case 'rest':
        this.progress = held;
        if (held >= 1) { this.rest = axes.slice(); this.restPressed = pressed.slice(); this.step = 'steer'; }
        break;
      case 'steer': {
        const i = this.most(axes, [], 0.08, j => j < wheel);
        this.progress = i < 0 ? 0 : held;
        if (i >= 0 && held >= 1) { this.steer = i; this.centre = this.rest[i]; this.lock = axes[i] - this.rest[i]; this.step = 'gas'; }
        break;
      }
      case 'gas': {
        const i = this.most(axes, [this.steer], 0.3);
        this.progress = i < 0 ? 0 : held;
        if (i >= 0 && held >= 1) { this.gas = { axis: i, rest: this.rest[i], full: axes[i] }; this.step = 'brake'; }
        break;
      }
      case 'brake': {
        const g = this.gas!;
        // the gas's axis only the other way from its rest (combined pedals)
        const i = this.most(axes, [this.steer], 0.3, j => j !== g.axis || Math.sign(axes[j] - g.rest) === -Math.sign(g.full - g.rest));
        this.progress = i < 0 ? 0 : held;
        if (i >= 0 && held >= 1) { this.brake = { axis: i, rest: this.rest[i], full: axes[i] }; this.step = this.radio ? 'nitrous' : 'done'; }
        break;
      }
      default:
        if (isSwitchStep(this.step)) {
          const s = this.flipped(axes, pressed);
          this.progress = s ? held : 0;
          if (s && held >= 1) { this.switches.push({ pad: SWITCH_STEPS[this.step].pad, ...s }); this.step = SWITCH_STEPS[this.step].next; }
        }
    }
    if (this.step !== before) { this.progress = 0; this.still = now; }
    return this.step !== before;
  }

  /** a radio's switch step passed with no switch for it; true when it was one */
  skip(): boolean {
    if (!isSwitchStep(this.step)) return false;
    this.step = SWITCH_STEPS[this.step].next;
    this.progress = 0;
    this.last = [];                     // the next feed starts the next step's hold
    return true;
  }

  /** the switch flipped (or button pressed) for a switch step, or null */
  private flipped(axes: readonly number[], pressed: readonly boolean[]): Omit<Switch, 'pad'> | null {
    const button = pressed.findIndex((v, i) => v && !this.restPressed[i] && !this.switches.some(s => s.button === i));
    if (button >= 0) return { button };
    const sticks = [this.steer, this.gas?.axis ?? -1, this.brake?.axis ?? -1];
    const i = this.most(axes, sticks, 0.5, j => !this.switches.some(s => s.axis === j && Math.abs((s.on ?? 0) - axes[j]) < 2 * SWITCH_NEAR));
    return i >= 0 ? { axis: i, on: axes[i] } : null;
  }

  /** the axis furthest from its rest (at least min, a hat switch's never), not one of skip, or -1 */
  private most(axes: readonly number[], skip: number[], min: number, ok: (i: number) => boolean = () => true): number {
    let best = -1, far = min;
    axes.forEach((v, i) => {
      const r = this.rest[i];
      if (skip.includes(i) || hatRest(v) || hatRest(r ?? 0) || typeof r !== 'number' || !ok(i)) return;
      const d = Math.abs(v - r);
      if (d >= far) { far = d; best = i; }
    });
    return best;
  }

  /** the set-up, once done */
  map(): WheelMap | null {
    if (this.step !== 'done') return null;
    return { ...this.base, steer: this.steer, centre: this.centre, lock: this.lock, gas: this.where(this.gas),
      brake: this.where(this.brake), ...(this.radio ? { switches: this.switches } : {}), placed: undefined, learned: true };
  }

  /** a pedal taken from the axes fed as the wheel's or on one of pads: one on its own USB travels its whole axis, so
   *  pressed to an end it rests at the other (its first report may have come with the pedal on its way down) */
  private where(p: Pedal | null): Pedal | null {
    if (!p) return p;
    let i = p.axis - this.lens[0];
    if (i < 0) return p;
    for (let d = 0; d < this.pads.length; d++) {
      const n = this.lens[d + 1] ?? 0;
      if (i < n) {
        const rest = Math.abs(p.rest) < 0.9 && Math.abs(p.full) >= 0.9 ? -Math.sign(p.full) : p.rest;
        return { axis: i, rest, full: p.full, pad: this.pads[d] };
      }
      i -= n;
    }
    return null;
  }

  /** pedals on their own send nothing until one first moves, every axis of theirs the browser's 0 until then: where
   *  that was their rest, it is taken again from their first report (each axis let go but the one starting down) */
  private restAgain(axes: readonly number[]) {
    if (this.rest.length !== axes.length) return;
    for (let d = 1, at = this.lens[0]; d < this.lens.length; at += this.lens[d++]) {
      const n = this.lens[d], unread = (j: number) => this.rest[j] === 0;
      if (n && Array.from({ length: n }, (_, j) => at + j).every(unread) && axes.slice(at, at + n).some(v => v !== 0))
        for (let j = at; j < at + n; j++) this.rest[j] = axes[j];
    }
  }
}

// /lastfm.html: where Last.fm's "allow access" page sends the player back, with a token, in the popup the start page opened
// (app/lastfm.ts).  The token is traded for the session key (the server's /lastfm), which goes where the start page reads it; the
// start page sees the change (a storage event) and says what came of it.  The popup then closes.  Last.fm's pages cut the popup's
// link to the start page (window.opener is null by then), so this never loads the start page itself: a browser that keeps the
// window open gets one line saying it can be closed.
import { keepSession } from './app/lastfm';
import { LASTFM_RESULT, localStore } from './app/prefs';
import { lastLanguage, setLanguage, t } from './app/i18n';

async function connect(): Promise<string> {
  const token = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('token');
  if (!token) return 'token';
  try {
    const r = await fetch('/lastfm', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify({ op: 'session', token }) });
    const j = await r.json() as { name?: unknown; sk?: unknown; error?: unknown };
    if (r.ok && typeof j.name === 'string' && typeof j.sk === 'string') { keepSession({ name: j.name, sk: j.sk }); return 'ok'; }
    return typeof j.error === 'string' ? j.error : 'down';
  } catch { return 'down'; }
}

void connect().then(async result => {
  localStore.setJSON(LASTFM_RESULT, { result, at: Date.now() });
  window.close();
  await setLanguage(lastLanguage()).catch(() => false);
  const p = Object.assign(document.createElement('p'), { className: 'hint lastfm-closed',
    textContent: result === 'ok' ? t('Last.fm connected. You can close this window.') : t('Last.fm didn\'t connect. Close this window and try again.') });
  document.body.append(p);
});

// The virtual LAN on the page: one WebSocket to the server's switch
// (web/server-rs/crates/lan, /lan on this page's origin) and the net mailboxes the C
// runtime publishes (runtime/web/net_proto.h, one layout):
//   HostKind.Net  free roam (runtime/web/roam_web.c): frame kinds 1 and 2
//   HostKind.Lan  LAN play, the Winsock HLE's virtual LAN (runtime/web/net_lan.c):
//                 frame kinds 3 (UDP), 4 (TCP), 5 (ICMP)
//
//   C (TX rings) --> this file --> WebSocket --> switch --> other browsers
//   C (RX rings) <-- this file <-- WebSocket <-- switch       (routed by frame kind)
//
// The page runs this in a worker of its own (remote.ts starts worker.ts, which
// runs this file's Link), so that nothing on the page's main thread (each
// frame's GPU work, the menus, a tab in the background) makes a datagram wait
// either way; on the main thread (attachNet) when no worker can start, and in
// the test harnesses that load this file alone.  It never
// blocks: it sleeps on each TX ring's bell with Atomics.waitAsync (C rings it
// when it queued frames) and writes received frames straight into the right RX
// ring, then rings C's network thread with Atomics.notify.  The switch assigns
// a virtual IPv4 address; this writes it into every mailbox, keeps the
// connection (reconnects with back-off and asks for the same address again,
// with the token the switch gave with it: /lan?resume, then the address and
// the token in the first message, never in the URL),
// writes the switch's peer list as a bitmap into the mailboxes, tells the LAN
// side when a browser left (its TCP connections are reset), and pings the
// switch for its round-trip time.  The server's own online host (the game's
// Online mode, web/server-rs/crates/online) is on the peer list as server: true: in the
// bitmap, never among the players.  Nothing connects until the runtime
// registers a mailbox, which it does only when a network feature is used (free
// roam: roam = on; LAN play: the game's first WSAStartup, its LAN screens).
//
// A place on the switch is held only while something needs it: each mailbox
// says so in its want word (free roam while it runs; LAN play from the game's
// WSAStartup to its last WSACleanup, so the LAN and Online screens).  When no
// mailbox has wanted it for idleMs the page closes the socket ("idle": the
// switch frees the address at once) and tells C (NET_PAGE_IDLE); the next
// want connects again.  The switch also hears whether LAN play is open
// ({"t":"lan"}): LAN broadcasts go only to the browsers that have it open,
// and with "udp" (the bound UDP ports as bits, Endpoint.udpPorts) only to
// those of them with a socket on the broadcast's port.
// A player who is away (the app's check, web/src/app/away.ts) gives the place
// back the same way, wanted or not: setAway(true) closes the socket ("idle")
// and tells C NET_PAGE_IDLE (Online and LAN play lose their connections, free
// roam its friends), and nothing connects until setAway(false).
//
// What C queued at once goes to the switch as one message (a bundle, nfsu2-lan):
// free roam's snapshot to each friend, the same bytes, once with the friends'
// addresses (TxBundle); and the switch sends this page its datagrams as compact
// bundles (kind 33: the same frames, about a quarter fewer bytes, proto.ts
// unpackCompact; the hello's "bundle":1 and "compact":1).
//
// The operator may remove a player (web/server-rs/crates/lan, Kicks and bans):
// the switch sends {"t":"kick"} or {"t":"ban"} with the operator's message (a
// ban with its number, the banned player's name and when it was made), then
// closes with 4001 or 4003.  The page tells the player (onRemoved) and stays
// off the switch for the rest of this game, as after goOffline.  The hello
// names this browser's own id (NetOptions.id, and NetOptions.was), which a ban
// names besides the player's address, and the token of the keyphrase it plays
// with (NetOptions.claim), which says whose claimed names it may play under,
// and which a ban names too.  A race ban keeps the player on the switch
// ({"t":"races"}: onRaces; the switch drops its races); so does someone else's
// ban that names only this player's address ("addr": a VPN's server, a phone
// network, a home shared with the banned player).  A name the operator
// took away ({"t":"rename"}, then the close 4004: onRename) keeps the page off
// the switch until the player picks another (rename), under which it goes back.
//
// TCP frames are never dropped here: while the LAN RX ring is full they wait
// in order (the C side's streams have no retransmission; the WebSocket and the
// switch are reliable and ordered).  A TCP connect to this browser while it has
// no LAN endpoint is answered with a reset (refused), as a host without a
// listener would.
