// Shader ABI check: compiles every WGSL module
// of a shader dump in this browser's WebGPU, builds render pipelines with the
// ABI's explicit layouts, and runs the vertex-pulling compute test against a
// CPU decoder with com.c decl_fetch semantics, and runs every vertex shader
// that has test vectors (vs_<id>.vec) against the CPU interpreter.  Result: one line
// "SHADERCHECK {json}" and document.title = 'DONE'.
//
//   /test/shadercheck.html?opfs=<dir>/<sub>   the dump in OPFS (default shadercheck/shaders)
//   &cross                                    also every game VS (ids < 1000) x every game PS
import { ALPHA_ALWAYS, ALPHA_GREATEREQUAL, KWIN_SIZE, HLPAR_SIZE, createShaderAbi, isCubePs, type ShaderAbi } from '../gpu/shader-abi';

const q = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
const pre = document.createElement('pre'); document.body.append(pre);
const log = (s: string) => { pre.textContent += s + '\n'; console.log(s); };

interface ModuleResult { name: string; bytes: number; ms: number; errors: string[]; warnings: number }
interface Summary {
  adapter: string; modules: number; vs: number; ps: number; psCube: number; compileErrors: number; warnings: number;
  compileMsTotal: number; compileMsMax: number; pipelines: number; pipelineErrors: number; pipelineMsTotal: number;
  pipelineMsMax: number; pull: { cases: number; exact: number; maxUlp: number; flushed: number; bad: number } | null;
  diff: DiffResult | null; psdiff: DiffResult | null; failures: string[]; ok: boolean;
}

async function readDump(path: string): Promise<{ files: Map<string, string>; vecs: Map<string, ArrayBuffer> }> {
  let dir = await navigator.storage.getDirectory();
  for (const part of path.split('/').filter(Boolean)) dir = await dir.getDirectoryHandle(part);
  const files = new Map<string, string>(), vecs = new Map<string, ArrayBuffer>();
  for await (const [name, h] of dir.entries()) {
    if (h.kind !== 'file') continue;
    const file = await (h as FileSystemFileHandle).getFile();
    if (name.endsWith('.wgsl')) files.set(name, await file.text());
    else if (name.endsWith('.vec') || name.endsWith('.pvec')) vecs.set(name.replace(/\.p?vec$/, ''), await file.arrayBuffer());
  }
  return { files, vecs };
}

// ---- differential test: the WGSL vertex function vs the CPU interpreter ----
// vs_<id>.vec comes from web/tools/wgsl-xl --pairs (vs_run on the same bytes
// and constants).  The vertex entry point becomes a plain function called by
// a compute shader that stores the 29 VOut floats per vertex.
interface DiffResult { modules: number; vertices: number; components: number; bad: number; maxRel: number; worst: string;
  /** pixel shaders: alpha-test decisions that differ only because alpha is within the tolerance of aref */
  edgeFlips?: number }
async function vsDiff(device: GPUDevice, name: string, code: string, vec: ArrayBuffer, res: DiffResult, failures: string[]) {
  const u = new Uint32Array(vec, 0, 4);
  if (u[0] !== 0x31565356) { failures.push(`${name}.vec: bad magic`); return; }
  const nv = u[1], stride = u[2];
  const vbBytes = new Uint8Array(vec, 16, nv * stride);
  const consts = new Float32Array(vec, 16 + nv * stride, 1024);
  const want = new Float32Array(vec, 16 + nv * stride + 4096, nv * 29);
  const head = code.match(/@vertex fn (vs_\d+)\(@builtin\(vertex_index\) vid: u32, @builtin\(instance_index\) iid: u32\) -> VOut \{/);
  if (!head) { failures.push(`${name}: no vertex entry point`); return; }
  // the draw's K block at row KB of the window, as the renderer passes it in firstInstance
  const KB = 37;
  const cs = code.replace(head[0], 'fn vsfn(vid: u32, iid: u32) -> VOut {') + `
@group(0) @binding(3) var<storage, read_write> OUTV: array<f32>;
@compute @workgroup_size(64) fn cs(@builtin(global_invocation_id) g: vec3u) {
  if (g.x >= arrayLength(&OUTV) / 29u) { return; }
  let o = vsfn(g.x, ${KB}u);
  let b = g.x * 29u;
  for (var c = 0u; c < 4u; c++) {
    OUTV[b + c] = o.pos[c]; OUTV[b + 4u + c] = o.col0[c]; OUTV[b + 8u + c] = o.col1[c];
    OUTV[b + 12u + c] = o.uv0[c]; OUTV[b + 16u + c] = o.uv1[c]; OUTV[b + 20u + c] = o.uv2[c]; OUTV[b + 24u + c] = o.uv3[c];
  }
  OUTV[b + 28u] = o.fog;
}`;
  const module = device.createShaderModule({ code: cs, label: name + '.cs' });
  const ci = await module.getCompilationInfo();
  const errs = ci.messages.filter(m => m.type === 'error');
  if (errs.length) { failures.push(`${name} (compute twin): ${errs.map(m => m.message).join('; ')}`); return; }
  const pipe = await device.createComputePipelineAsync({ layout: 'auto', compute: { module } });
  const vbSize = Math.max(16, (vbBytes.length + 3) & ~3);
  const vb = device.createBuffer({ size: vbSize, usage: GPUBufferUsage.STORAGE | GPUBufferUsage.COPY_DST });
  const vbCopy = new Uint8Array(vbSize); vbCopy.set(vbBytes);
  device.queue.writeBuffer(vb, 0, vbCopy);
  // a 64 KB window (KWIN_SIZE) with the block at row KB; the rows around it hold other values,
  // so a shader that read outside its block would differ from the CPU
  const k = new ArrayBuffer(KWIN_SIZE);
  new Float32Array(k).fill(-7.25);
  new Uint32Array(k, KB * 16, 4).set([stride, 0x03020100, 0, 0]);    // tsel: stage k reads oTk
  new Float32Array(k, KB * 16 + 16, 1024).set(consts);
  const kb = device.createBuffer({ size: KWIN_SIZE, usage: GPUBufferUsage.UNIFORM | GPUBufferUsage.COPY_DST });
  device.queue.writeBuffer(kb, 0, k);
  const out = device.createBuffer({ size: nv * 29 * 4, usage: GPUBufferUsage.STORAGE | GPUBufferUsage.COPY_SRC });
  const rd = device.createBuffer({ size: nv * 29 * 4, usage: GPUBufferUsage.MAP_READ | GPUBufferUsage.COPY_DST });
  const bg = device.createBindGroup({ layout: pipe.getBindGroupLayout(0), entries: [
    { binding: 0, resource: { buffer: vb } }, { binding: 1, resource: { buffer: kb } }, { binding: 3, resource: { buffer: out } }] });
  const enc = device.createCommandEncoder();
  const pass = enc.beginComputePass(); pass.setPipeline(pipe); pass.setBindGroup(0, bg); pass.dispatchWorkgroups(Math.ceil(nv / 64)); pass.end();
  enc.copyBufferToBuffer(out, 0, rd, 0, nv * 29 * 4);
  device.queue.submit([enc.finish()]);
  await rd.mapAsync(GPUMapMode.READ);
  const got = new Float32Array(rd.getMappedRange().slice(0)); rd.unmap();
  vb.destroy(); kb.destroy(); out.destroy(); rd.destroy();
  const FIELD = ['pos', 'col0', 'col1', 'uv0', 'uv1', 'uv2', 'uv3'];
  let bad = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < nv * 29; i++) {
    const g = got[i], w = want[i];
    res.components++;
    if (g === w || (Number.isNaN(g) && Number.isNaN(w))) continue;
    const rel = Math.abs(g - w) / Math.max(1, Math.abs(w));
    if (rel > res.maxRel) { res.maxRel = rel; res.worst = `${name} v${Math.floor(i / 29)} ${i % 29 === 28 ? 'fog' : FIELD[Math.floor((i % 29) / 4)] + '.' + 'xyzw'[i % 29 % 4]}: gpu ${g} cpu ${w}`; }
    if (!(rel <= 1e-4)) {
      bad++;
      if (bad <= 3) failures.push(`${name} vertex ${Math.floor(i / 29)} out ${i % 29}: gpu ${g} cpu ${w}`);
    }
  }
  res.modules++; res.vertices += nv; res.bad += bad;
}

// ---- vertex pulling: CPU reference = com.c decl_fetch ----
// f32 arithmetic in JS: a double division of small integers rounded once to
// f32 equals the correctly rounded f32 division, as C does in decl_fetch.
function declFetch(b: Uint8Array, a: number, type: number): number[] {
  const dv = new DataView(b.buffer, b.byteOffset, b.byteLength);
  const f = (x: number) => dv.getFloat32(x, true), s = (x: number) => dv.getInt16(x, true), u = (x: number) => dv.getUint16(x, true);
  const F = Math.fround;
  switch (type) {
    case 0: return [f(a), 0, 0, 1];
    case 1: return [f(a), f(a + 4), 0, 1];
    case 2: return [f(a), f(a + 4), f(a + 8), 1];
    case 3: return [f(a), f(a + 4), f(a + 8), f(a + 12)];
    case 4: return [F(b[a + 2] / 255), F(b[a + 1] / 255), F(b[a] / 255), F(b[a + 3] / 255)];
    case 5: return [b[a], b[a + 1], b[a + 2], b[a + 3]];
    case 8: return [F(b[a] / 255), F(b[a + 1] / 255), F(b[a + 2] / 255), F(b[a + 3] / 255)];
    case 6: return [s(a), s(a + 2), 0, 1];
    case 7: return [s(a), s(a + 2), s(a + 4), s(a + 6)];
    case 9: return [F(s(a) / 32767), F(s(a + 2) / 32767), 0, 1];
    case 10: return [F(s(a) / 32767), F(s(a + 2) / 32767), F(s(a + 4) / 32767), F(s(a + 6) / 32767)];
    case 11: return [F(u(a) / 65535), F(u(a + 2) / 65535), 0, 1];
    case 12: return [F(u(a) / 65535), F(u(a + 2) / 65535), F(u(a + 4) / 65535), F(u(a + 6) / 65535)];
  }
  return [0, 0, 0, 1];
}
const f32bits = (x: number) => { const t = new Float32Array([x]); return new Uint32Array(t.buffer)[0]; };
function ulpDiff(x: number, y: number): number {
  const a = f32bits(x) | 0, b = f32bits(y) | 0;
  const oa = a < 0 ? 0x80000000 - a : a, ob = b < 0 ? 0x80000000 - b : b;   // ordered integers
  return Math.abs(oa - ob);
}
const isDenormal = (x: number) => x !== 0 && Math.abs(x) < 1.1754943508222875e-38;

async function pullTest(device: GPUDevice, code: string, failures: string[]) {
  const module = device.createShaderModule({ code, label: 'pulltest' });
  const info = await module.getCompilationInfo();
  const errs = info.messages.filter(m => m.type === 'error');
  if (errs.length) { failures.push('pulltest: ' + errs.map(m => m.message).join('; ')); return null; }
  const pipeline = await device.createComputePipelineAsync({ layout: 'auto', compute: { module } });
  // deterministic bytes (xorshift32), long enough for base + offset + 16
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(8192);
  let x = 0x12345678;
  for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i++) { x ^= x << 13; x ^= x >>> 17; x ^= x << 5; bytes[i] = x & 0xff; }
  // a few readable values among the random bits (exact small floats, short extremes)
  new DataView(bytes.buffer).setFloat32(16, 1.5, true); new DataView(bytes.buffer).setInt16(40, -32768, true);
  const vb = device.createBuffer({ size: bytes.length, usage: GPUBufferUsage.STORAGE | GPUBufferUsage.COPY_DST });
  device.queue.writeBuffer(vb, 0, bytes);
  const N = 13 * 8, outSize = N * 16;
  const out = device.createBuffer({ size: outSize, usage: GPUBufferUsage.STORAGE | GPUBufferUsage.COPY_SRC });
  const rd = device.createBuffer({ size: outSize, usage: GPUBufferUsage.MAP_READ | GPUBufferUsage.COPY_DST });
  const pt = device.createBuffer({ size: 16, usage: GPUBufferUsage.UNIFORM | GPUBufferUsage.COPY_DST });
  const bg = device.createBindGroup({ layout: pipeline.getBindGroupLayout(0), entries: [
    { binding: 0, resource: { buffer: vb } }, { binding: 1, resource: { buffer: out } }, { binding: 2, resource: { buffer: pt } }] });
  const res = { cases: 0, exact: 0, maxUlp: 0, flushed: 0, bad: 0 };
  for (const base of [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 4093, 6002, 7999 - 32]) {
    device.queue.writeBuffer(pt, 0, new Uint32Array([base, 0, 0, 0]));
    const enc = device.createCommandEncoder();
    const pass = enc.beginComputePass(); pass.setPipeline(pipeline); pass.setBindGroup(0, bg); pass.dispatchWorkgroups(1); pass.end();
    enc.copyBufferToBuffer(out, 0, rd, 0, outSize);
    device.queue.submit([enc.finish()]);
    await rd.mapAsync(GPUMapMode.READ);
    const got = new Float32Array(rd.getMappedRange().slice(0));
    rd.unmap();
    for (let t = 0; t <= 12; t++) for (let o = 0; o < 8; o++) {
      const want = declFetch(bytes, base + o, t);
      for (let c = 0; c < 4; c++) {
        const g = got[(t * 8 + o) * 4 + c], w = want[c];
        res.cases++;
        if (f32bits(g) === f32bits(w) || (Number.isNaN(g) && Number.isNaN(w))) { res.exact++; continue; }
        if (isDenormal(w) && g === 0) { res.flushed++; continue; }
        // bit-exact is required (the helpers round divisions like C does);
        // the ulp distance is only reported
        const d = ulpDiff(g, w);
        res.maxUlp = Math.max(res.maxUlp, d);
        res.bad++;
        if (res.bad <= 10) failures.push(`pull type ${t} base ${base} off ${o} comp ${c}: gpu ${g} cpu ${w} (${d} ulp)`);
      }
    }
  }
  return res;
}


// ---- differential test: the WGSL pixel function vs the reference interpreter ----
// ps_<id>.pvec comes from web/tools/wgsl-xl --pairs (ps_ref_run, the Mac's
// pixel shader semantics executed on the bytecode).  The fragment entry point
// becomes a plain function; textureSample becomes the same analytic "texture"
// the reference uses, and discard sets a flag, so it runs in a compute shader.
const FTEX = `
fn ftex2(k: u32, c: vec2f) -> vec4f {
  let f = f32(k);
  return vec4f(0.5 + 0.4 * sin(c.x * 3.1 + f * 0.37), 0.5 + 0.4 * cos(c.y * 2.3 + f * 0.5),
               0.5 + 0.4 * sin((c.x + c.y) * 1.7 + f), 0.5 + 0.4 * cos(c.x * c.y * 5.3 + 0.2 * f));
}
fn ftex3(k: u32, c: vec3f) -> vec4f { return ftex2(k, vec2f(c.x + c.z * 0.3, c.y - c.z * 0.2)); }
`;
async function psDiff(device: GPUDevice, name: string, code: string, vec: ArrayBuffer, res: DiffResult, failures: string[]) {
  const u = new Uint32Array(vec, 0, 4);
  if (u[0] !== 0x31565350) { failures.push(`${name}.pvec: bad magic`); return; }
  const np = u[1], cubemask = u[2];
  const par = new Uint8Array(vec, 16, 560);
  const inputs = new Float32Array(vec, 576, np * 25);
  const want = new Float32Array(vec, 576 + np * 100, np * 5);
  const head = code.match(/@fragment fn (ps_\d+)\(i: VOut\) -> @location\(0\) vec4f \{/);
  if (!head) { failures.push(`${name}: no fragment entry point`); return; }
  const body = code.replace(head[0], 'fn psfn(i: VOut) -> vec4f {').replaceAll('{ discard; }', '{ KILL = 1u; }')
    .replace(/textureSample\(tex(\d), smp\d, /g, (_m, k) => ((cubemask >> +k) & 1) ? `ftex3(${k}u, ` : `ftex2(${k}u, `);
  const cs = body + FTEX + `
var<private> KILL: u32;
@group(0) @binding(4) var<storage, read> PIN: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(5) var<storage, read_write> POUT: array<f32>;
@compute @workgroup_size(64) fn cs(@builtin(global_invocation_id) g: vec3u) {
  if (g.x >= arrayLength(&POUT) / 5u) { return; }
  let b = g.x * 25u;
  var i: VOut;
  i.pos = vec4f(0.0);
  i.col0 = vec4f(PIN[b], PIN[b + 1u], PIN[b + 2u], PIN[b + 3u]);
  i.col1 = vec4f(PIN[b + 4u], PIN[b + 5u], PIN[b + 6u], PIN[b + 7u]);
  i.uv0 = vec4f(PIN[b + 8u], PIN[b + 9u], PIN[b + 10u], PIN[b + 11u]);
  i.uv1 = vec4f(PIN[b + 12u], PIN[b + 13u], PIN[b + 14u], PIN[b + 15u]);
  i.uv2 = vec4f(PIN[b + 16u], PIN[b + 17u], PIN[b + 18u], PIN[b + 19u]);
  i.uv3 = vec4f(PIN[b + 20u], PIN[b + 21u], PIN[b + 22u], PIN[b + 23u]);
  i.fog = PIN[b + 24u];
  KILL = 0u;
  let c = psfn(i);
  let o = g.x * 5u;
  POUT[o] = c.x; POUT[o + 1u] = c.y; POUT[o + 2u] = c.z; POUT[o + 3u] = c.w; POUT[o + 4u] = f32(KILL);
}`;
  const module = device.createShaderModule({ code: cs, label: name + '.cs' });
  const ci = await module.getCompilationInfo();
  const errs = ci.messages.filter(m => m.type === 'error');
  if (errs.length) { failures.push(`${name} (compute twin): ${errs.map(m => m.message).join('; ')}`); return; }
  const pipe = await device.createComputePipelineAsync({ layout: 'auto', compute: { module } });
  const mk = (size: number, usage: number) => device.createBuffer({ size, usage });
  const pb = mk(560, GPUBufferUsage.UNIFORM | GPUBufferUsage.COPY_DST);
  device.queue.writeBuffer(pb, 0, par);
  const ib = mk(np * 100, GPUBufferUsage.STORAGE | GPUBufferUsage.COPY_DST);
  device.queue.writeBuffer(ib, 0, inputs);
  const ob = mk(np * 20, GPUBufferUsage.STORAGE | GPUBufferUsage.COPY_SRC);
  const rd = mk(np * 20, GPUBufferUsage.MAP_READ | GPUBufferUsage.COPY_DST);
  // the lit pixel shaders also read H, the other cars' headlights: none (n = 0), as the
  // reference interpreter has no such term (a web-only addition)
  const hb = /@group\(0\) @binding\(3\)/.test(code) ? mk(HLPAR_SIZE, GPUBufferUsage.UNIFORM) : null;
  const bg = device.createBindGroup({ layout: pipe.getBindGroupLayout(0), entries: [
    { binding: 2, resource: { buffer: pb } }, { binding: 4, resource: { buffer: ib } }, { binding: 5, resource: { buffer: ob } },
    ...(hb ? [{ binding: 3, resource: { buffer: hb } }] : [])] });
  const enc = device.createCommandEncoder();
  const pass = enc.beginComputePass(); pass.setPipeline(pipe); pass.setBindGroup(0, bg); pass.dispatchWorkgroups(Math.ceil(np / 64)); pass.end();
  enc.copyBufferToBuffer(ob, 0, rd, 0, np * 20);
  device.queue.submit([enc.finish()]);
  await rd.mapAsync(GPUMapMode.READ);
  const got = new Float32Array(rd.getMappedRange().slice(0)); rd.unmap();
  pb.destroy(); ib.destroy(); ob.destroy(); rd.destroy(); hb?.destroy();
  const aref = new Float32Array(vec, 16, 1)[0];
  const TOL = 1e-3;                         // relative, as for the colours below
  let bad = 0;
  for (let px = 0; px < np; px++) {
    const gk = got[px * 5 + 4], wk = want[px * 5 + 4];
    res.components++;
    if (gk !== wk) {
      // The alpha test (alpha >= aref) of a pixel whose alpha is within the
      // colour tolerance of aref may go either way on another GPU: accept the
      // flip when both alphas are that close and lie on opposite sides of
      // aref, i.e. the alpha test alone explains it; the colours must still match.
      const ga = got[px * 5 + 3], wa = want[px * 5 + 3], tol = TOL * Math.max(1, Math.abs(aref));
      const edge = Math.abs(ga - aref) <= tol && Math.abs(wa - aref) <= tol && (ga >= aref) === !gk && (wa >= aref) === !wk;
      if (!edge) { bad++; if (bad <= 3) failures.push(`${name} pixel ${px}: kill gpu ${gk} ref ${wk} (alpha gpu ${ga} ref ${wa}, aref ${aref})`); continue; }
      res.edgeFlips = (res.edgeFlips ?? 0) + 1;
    } else if (wk) continue;                // discarded on both sides: colour irrelevant
    for (let c = 0; c < 4; c++) {
      const g = got[px * 5 + c], w = want[px * 5 + c];
      res.components++;
      if (g === w || (Number.isNaN(g) && Number.isNaN(w))) continue;
      const rel = Math.abs(g - w) / Math.max(1, Math.abs(w));
      if (rel > res.maxRel) { res.maxRel = rel; res.worst = `${name} pixel ${px}.${'rgba'[c]}: gpu ${g} ref ${w}`; }
      if (!(rel <= 1e-3)) { bad++; if (bad <= 3) failures.push(`${name} pixel ${px}.${'rgba'[c]}: gpu ${g} ref ${w}`); }
    }
  }
  res.modules++; res.vertices += np; res.bad += bad;
}

async function main() {
  const path = q.get('opfs') ?? 'shadercheck/shaders';
  const { files, vecs } = await readDump(path);
  const failures: string[] = [];
  const adapter = await navigator.gpu.requestAdapter();
  if (!adapter) throw new Error('no WebGPU adapter');
  const device = await adapter.requestDevice();
  device.addEventListener('uncapturederror', e => failures.push('uncaptured: ' + (e as GPUUncapturedErrorEvent).error.message));
  const abi: ShaderAbi = createShaderAbi(device);
  const info = adapter.info;
  log(`adapter: ${info.vendor} ${info.architecture} ${info.description}; ${files.size} modules from OPFS ${path}`);

  // ---- 1. modules ----
  const mods = new Map<string, GPUShaderModule>();
  const results: ModuleResult[] = [];
  const names = [...files.keys()].filter(n => n !== 'pulltest.wgsl').sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b, 'en', { numeric: true }));
  for (const name of names) {
    const code = files.get(name)!;
    const t0 = performance.now();
    device.pushErrorScope('validation');
    const m = device.createShaderModule({ code, label: name });
    const ci = await m.getCompilationInfo();
    const scope = await device.popErrorScope();
    const ms = performance.now() - t0;
    const errors = ci.messages.filter(x => x.type === 'error').map(x => `${x.lineNum}:${x.linePos} ${x.message}`);
    if (scope) errors.push(scope.message);
    results.push({ name, bytes: code.length, ms, errors, warnings: ci.messages.filter(x => x.type === 'warning').length });
    if (errors.length) { failures.push(`${name}: ${errors.join(' | ')}`); log(`ERROR ${name}: ${errors.join(' | ')}`); }
    else mods.set(name.replace(/\.wgsl$/, ''), m);
  }
  const vsNames = [...mods.keys()].filter(n => n.startsWith('vs_'));
  const psNames = [...mods.keys()].filter(n => n.startsWith('ps_'));
  const idOf = (n: string) => parseInt(n.slice(3), 10);

  // ---- 2. pipelines with the explicit ABI layouts ----
  const pipeMs: number[] = [];
  let pipelineErrors = 0;
  async function pipeline(vs: string, ps: string, constants: Record<string, number>) {
    const t0 = performance.now();
    try {
      await device.createRenderPipelineAsync({
        label: `${vs}+${ps} ${JSON.stringify(constants)}`,
        layout: isCubePs(idOf(ps)) ? abi.layoutCube : abi.layout2d,
        vertex: { module: mods.get(vs)!, entryPoint: vs },
        fragment: { module: mods.get(ps)!, entryPoint: ps, constants, targets: [{ format: 'bgra8unorm' }] },
        primitive: { topology: 'triangle-list', frontFace: 'cw', cullMode: 'back' },
        depthStencil: { format: 'depth24plus-stencil8', depthWriteEnabled: true, depthCompare: 'less-equal' },
      });
    } catch (e) {
      pipelineErrors++;
      const msg = `pipeline ${vs}+${ps} ${JSON.stringify(constants)}: ${(e as Error).message}`;
      failures.push(msg); log('ERROR ' + msg);
    }
    pipeMs.push(performance.now() - t0);
  }
  const ff = mods.has('ps_0') ? 'ps_0' : null;
  for (const vs of vsNames) if (ff) await pipeline(vs, ff, { ALPHA_FUNC: ALPHA_ALWAYS });
  if (mods.has('vs_0'))
    for (const ps of psNames) {
      await pipeline('vs_0', ps, { ALPHA_FUNC: ALPHA_GREATEREQUAL });
      await pipeline('vs_0', ps, { ALPHA_FUNC: ALPHA_ALWAYS });
      await pipeline('vs_0', ps, { ALPHA_FUNC: ALPHA_GREATEREQUAL, PS20_TEXCOORD: 0 });
    }
  // &cross: the game's own VS modules (ids below 1000; the --pairs extras are left out) x every game PS
  if (q.has('cross'))
    for (const vs of vsNames) if (vs !== 'vs_0' && idOf(vs) < 1000) for (const ps of psNames) if (ps !== 'ps_0' && ps !== 'ps_256')
      await pipeline(vs, ps, { ALPHA_FUNC: ALPHA_GREATEREQUAL });

  // ---- 3. shaders against the CPU interpreters ----
  let diff: DiffResult | null = null, psdiff: DiffResult | null = null;
  if (vecs.size) {
    diff = { modules: 0, vertices: 0, components: 0, bad: 0, maxRel: 0, worst: '' };
    psdiff = { modules: 0, vertices: 0, components: 0, bad: 0, maxRel: 0, worst: '', edgeFlips: 0 };
    for (const [n, vec] of vecs) {
      if (!files.has(n + '.wgsl')) continue;
      if (n.startsWith('vs_')) await vsDiff(device, n, files.get(n + '.wgsl')!, vec, diff, failures);
      else await psDiff(device, n, files.get(n + '.wgsl')!, vec, psdiff, failures);
    }
    log(`vertex shader differential test: ${diff.modules} modules, ${diff.vertices} vertices, ${diff.bad} components over 1e-4 relative, max ${diff.maxRel.toExponential(2)} (${diff.worst})`);
    log(`pixel shader differential test: ${psdiff.modules} modules, ${psdiff.vertices} pixels, ${psdiff.bad} mismatches (kill flag or over 1e-3 relative), ${psdiff.edgeFlips} alpha-test flips within 1e-3 of aref accepted, max ${psdiff.maxRel.toExponential(2)} (${psdiff.worst})`);
  }

  // ---- 4. vertex pulling ----
  const pull = files.has('pulltest.wgsl') ? await pullTest(device, files.get('pulltest.wgsl')!, failures) : null;
  if (!files.has('pulltest.wgsl')) failures.push('pulltest.wgsl missing');
  if (pull && pull.bad) log(`ERROR vertex pulling: ${pull.bad} mismatches`);

  const cms = results.map(r => r.ms);
  const s: Summary = {
    adapter: `${info.vendor} ${info.architecture}`.trim(), modules: results.length,
    vs: results.filter(r => r.name.startsWith('vs_')).length,
    ps: results.filter(r => r.name.startsWith('ps_') && !isCubePs(idOf(r.name))).length,
    psCube: results.filter(r => r.name.startsWith('ps_') && isCubePs(idOf(r.name))).length,
    compileErrors: results.filter(r => r.errors.length).length, warnings: results.reduce((a, r) => a + r.warnings, 0),
    compileMsTotal: +cms.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0).toFixed(1), compileMsMax: +Math.max(0, ...cms).toFixed(1),
    pipelines: pipeMs.length, pipelineErrors, pipelineMsTotal: +pipeMs.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0).toFixed(1),
    pipelineMsMax: +Math.max(0, ...pipeMs).toFixed(1), pull, diff, psdiff, failures, ok: false,
  };
  s.ok = failures.length === 0 && s.compileErrors === 0 && pipelineErrors === 0 && !!pull && pull.bad === 0 && (!diff || diff.bad === 0) && (!psdiff || psdiff.bad === 0);
  for (const r of results) log(`module ${r.name} ${r.bytes} B ${r.ms.toFixed(1)} ms${r.errors.length ? ' ERROR' : ''}${r.warnings ? ` ${r.warnings} warnings` : ''}`);
  log('SHADERCHECK ' + JSON.stringify(s));
}

main().catch(e => log('SHADERCHECK ' + JSON.stringify({ ok: false, failures: ['exception: ' + (e as Error).message] })))
  .finally(() => { document.title = 'DONE'; });

#!/bin/bash
# Start NFS Underground 2 in the browser: one command on the Mac that hosts it.
#
#   web/start.sh [--data "<game folder>"] [--http-port 8080] [--open] [--no-build]
#   cd web && npm start -- [the same options]
#
# What it does, in order:
#   1. web/node_modules: installed (npm ci) if missing.
#   2. The game module (out/web/nfsu2.wasm): built with web/build.sh only when it
#      is missing or older than the runtime, the generated game code or the
#      build script.  A few seconds with the shared object cache.
#   3. The page (web/dist): built with node build.mjs only when older than its
#      sources.
#   4. The server (out/web/server-rs/nfsu2-server): built with
#      web/server-rs/build.sh only when it is missing or older than its sources
#      (it needs Rust: https://rustup.rs).
#   5. The server in the foreground, with the game folder: --data, else
#      $NFSU2_DATA, else the folder used last time, else
#      ~/projects/nsfu2/Need for Speed - Underground 2 if it exists.  Ctrl-C stops it.
# It prints the address for this Mac, http://localhost:<port>/; --open also opens
# it in Chrome.  The server listens on this Mac only: other PCs need HTTPS, from
# a certificate or a proxy or tunnel in front (web/deploy/).
# A build that fails stops here with its error (the last 40 lines; the whole log
# is in out/web/server/), instead of starting the server with a stale or missing
# module, page or server.
set -e -o pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"
STATE="$ROOT/out/web/server"
SERVER=out/web/server-rs/nfsu2-server
DATA="" HTTP_PORT=8080 OPEN=0 BUILD=1
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --data) DATA="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --http-port) HTTP_PORT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --open) OPEN=1; shift ;;
    --no-build) BUILD=0; shift ;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,23p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "start.sh: unknown option $1 (see --help)"; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
say() { printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }

# ---- the game folder ----------------------------------------------------------
if [ -z "$DATA" ]; then DATA="${NFSU2_DATA:-}"; fi
if [ -z "$DATA" ] && [ -f "$STATE/data-path" ]; then DATA="$(cat "$STATE/data-path")"; fi
if [ -z "$DATA" ] && [ -d "$HOME/projects/nsfu2/Need for Speed - Underground 2" ]; then DATA="$HOME/projects/nsfu2/Need for Speed - Underground 2"; fi
if [ -z "$DATA" ] || [ ! -f "$DATA/SPEED2.EXE" ]; then
  echo "Where is the game?  Start with the folder that holds SPEED2.EXE:"
  echo "  web/start.sh --data \"/path/to/Need for Speed - Underground 2\""
  [ -n "$DATA" ] && echo "(\"$DATA\" has no SPEED2.EXE)"
  exit 1
fi
mkdir -p "$STATE"; printf '%s' "$DATA" > "$STATE/data-path"

# ---- the port is free? -----------------------------------------------------------
if lsof -nP -iTCP:"$HTTP_PORT" -sTCP:LISTEN >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Port $HTTP_PORT is in use (by: $(lsof -nP -iTCP:"$HTTP_PORT" -sTCP:LISTEN | awk 'NR==2{print $1" pid "$2}')). Is the server already running?"
  echo "Open http://localhost:$HTTP_PORT/ if it is, or start on another port: web/start.sh --http-port 9080"
  exit 1
fi

if [ "$BUILD" = 1 ]; then
  # ---- 1. the page's tools ----
  if [ ! -d web/node_modules/esbuild ]; then
    say "Installing the page's tools (npm ci, once)"
    (cd web && npm ci --no-audit --no-fund)
  fi
  # ---- 2. the game module ----
  WASM=out/web/nfsu2.wasm
  stale=""
  if [ ! -f "$WASM" ]; then stale="missing"
  else
    newer="$(find -L runtime gen/all web/build.sh -newer "$WASM" -type f -print -quit 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [ -n "$newer" ] && stale="older than $newer"
  fi
  if [ -n "$stale" ]; then
    if ls -d deps/wasi-sdk-* >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f gen/all/fntab.c ]; then
      say "Building the game module ($stale)"
      if ! web/build.sh > "$STATE/build.log" 2>&1; then
        tail -40 "$STATE/build.log"
        echo "The game module did not build (the whole log: $STATE/build.log). The server was not started."
        exit 1
      fi
      tail -3 "$STATE/build.log"
    elif [ -f "$WASM" ]; then
      echo "The game module is $stale, but this checkout cannot build it (no wasi-sdk in deps/ or no gen/all): using the one there is."
    else
      echo "No game module (out/web/nfsu2.wasm) and no toolchain to build it: see docs/web/PLAYING.md, 'Building'."
      exit 1
    fi
  fi
  # ---- 3. the page ----
  if [ ! -f web/dist/main.js ] || [ -n "$(find web/src web/index.html web/build.mjs app/registry-defaults.txt CHANGELOG.md -newer web/dist/main.js -type f -print -quit 2>/dev/null || true)" ]; then
    say "Building the page"
    if ! (cd web && node build.mjs) > "$STATE/page-build.log" 2>&1; then
      tail -40 "$STATE/page-build.log"
      echo "The page did not build (the whole log: $STATE/page-build.log). The server was not started."
      exit 1
    fi
    tail -1 "$STATE/page-build.log"
  fi
  # ---- 4. the server ----
  if [ ! -x "$SERVER" ] || [ -n "$(find web/server-rs \( -name '*.rs' -o -name 'Cargo.*' -o -name '*.txt' \) -newer "$SERVER" -type f -print -quit 2>/dev/null || true)" ]; then
    say "Building the server"
    if ! web/server-rs/build.sh > "$STATE/server-build.log" 2>&1; then
      tail -40 "$STATE/server-build.log"
      echo "The server did not build (it needs Rust: https://rustup.rs; the whole log: $STATE/server-build.log). It was not started."
      exit 1
    fi
    tail -2 "$STATE/server-build.log"
  fi
fi
if [ ! -x "$SERVER" ]; then
  echo "No server ($SERVER): start without --no-build, or build it with web/server-rs/build.sh."
  exit 1
fi

# ---- 5. the server ----------------------------------------------------------------
say "Starting the server (Ctrl-C stops it)"
echo "  On this Mac:  http://localhost:$HTTP_PORT/"
if [ "$OPEN" = 1 ]; then
  ( for _ in $(seq 1 50); do curl -sf -o /dev/null "http://localhost:$HTTP_PORT/game.json" && break; sleep 0.2; done
    open -a "Google Chrome" "http://localhost:$HTTP_PORT/" 2>/dev/null || open "http://localhost:$HTTP_PORT/" ) &
fi
exec "$SERVER" --data "$DATA" --http-port "$HTTP_PORT"

// Windows' AltGr (web/src/input/altgr.ts, issue 58): its Left Ctrl kept from the game once the browser has shown that
// it sends one, every other Left Ctrl sent (at most WAIT_MS later), and nothing changed off Windows.
//   node --test web/test/altgr.test.mjs
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';

  entryPoints: [path.join(ROOT, 'web/src/input/altgr.ts')], bundle: true, format: 'esm', write: false })).outputFiles[0].text).toString('base64'));

const ALTGR = { code: 'AltRight', key: 'AltGraph', repeat: false };
const ALT = { code: 'AltRight', key: 'Alt', repeat: false };
const W = { code: 'KeyW', key: 'w', repeat: false };

function rig({ on = true, stored = null } = {}) {
  let t = 1000;
  const sent = [], logs = [], data = new Map(stored ? [['nfsu2.altgr-ctrl', stored]] : []);
  const store = { getItem: k => data.get(k) ?? null, setItem: (k, v) => data.set(k, v) };
  const f = new A.AltGrCtrl(on, s => logs.push(s), () => t, store);
  const key = (e, down, dt = 0) => { t += dt; f.key(e, down, () => sent.push(`${down ? '+' : '-'}${e.code}`)); };
  return { f, key, sent, logs, data };
}

test('off Windows nothing is held or dropped', () => {
  const r = rig({ on: false, stored: '1' });
  r.key(CTRL, true); r.key(ALTGR, true, 0.2); r.key(CTRL, false); r.key(ALTGR, false);
  assert.deepEqual(r.sent, ['+ControlLeft', '+AltRight', '-ControlLeft', '-AltRight']);
});

test('the first AltGr goes through as it did, and teaches the browser', () => {
  const r = rig();

  assert.equal(r.data.get('nfsu2.altgr-ctrl'), '1');
  assert.match(r.logs.join('\n'), /sends AltGr as Left Ctrl and Right Alt/);
  r.key(CTRL, false); r.key(ALTGR, false);
  r.key(CTRL, true, 500); r.key(ALTGR, true, 0.3);
  assert.deepEqual(r.sent.slice(4), ['+AltRight'], 'the next one: its Left Ctrl dropped');
  assert.match(r.logs.join('\n'), /its Left Ctrl \(0\.3 ms before Right Alt\) does not reach the game/);
});

  r.key(CTRL, true, 100); r.key(ALTGR, true, 60);
  assert.equal(r.data.get('nfsu2.altgr-ctrl'), undefined);

// subsystems: the order of attach and exit is controlled, so the late-attach
// rule (app review finding 6) is tested deterministically.
//   node --test web/test/app-session.test.mjs
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import path from 'node:path';

const FAKES = `
export const events = [];
export const ctl = {};
// the process: exits when the test says so; registrations never arrive
export async function startProcess() {
  let exit; const exited = new Promise(r => (exit = r));
  ctl.exit = exit;
  return { memory: new WebAssembly.Memory({ initial: 1, maximum: 2, shared: true }), exited,
    registered: () => new Promise(() => {}), terminate() { events.push('terminate'); exit(-1); } };

const later = (name, extra = {}) => (...args) => new Promise((res, rej) => {
  ctl[name] = { attach: () => res({ detach: () => events.push(name + ' detached'), stats: () => ({}), ...extra }), fail: (e) => rej(e) };
});
export const attachRenderer = later('renderer', { imageRect: () => ({ x: 0, y: 0, w: 1, h: 1 }) });
export const attachAudio = later('audio', { state: () => 'running' });
export const attachInput = later('input');
export const attachNet = later('net', { vip: () => null, peers: () => [] });

async function session(extra = {}) {
  events.length = 0;
  const logs = [], fatal = [];
  let closed = 0;
  const audio = { close: async () => { closed++; } };
  const s = await GameSession.start({ module: null, info: { pages: 0 }, saveDir: 's', env: {}, canvas: { width: 1, height: 1, clientWidth: 1, clientHeight: 1 },

test('a subsystem attached before the end is detached at the end', async () => {
  const { s } = await session();
  for (const n of ['renderer', 'audio', 'input', 'net']) ctl[n].attach();
  await tick();
  ctl.exit(0); await s.exited; await tick();
  assert.deepEqual(events.sort(), ['audio detached', 'input detached', 'net detached', 'renderer detached']);
});

test('a subsystem that attaches after the game ended is detached at once (renderer, audio, input, net)', async () => {

{"id": "AT001871", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/web/test/astc.test.mjs", "originalBytes": 8657, "originalSha256": "3c89c6b3d948ffe00e093f3190a0ee15602d091d092ec989fed3f09521939ba2", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 8657, "utf8TotalBytes": 8657}

// DXT1 rewritten as ASTC 4x4 (web/src/gpu/astc.ts), without a GPU:
//   node --test web/test/astc.test.mjs
// A decoder of the few ASTC blocks astc.ts writes (from the Khronos spec: block modes 0x042, 0x051, 0x451, endpoint
// modes 8 and 12) reads them back, and every texel is compared with the CPU's unpacking (dxt.ts) within what the
// rewriting allows.  The GPU check (web/tools/astc-check.mjs, Chrome and WebKit) gave the same figures on an Apple
// GPU: four colours at most 2 of 255 off, three colours 1, two-plane blocks 1 and their alpha exact.
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import * as esbuild from 'esbuild';

const ROOT = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '../..');
const entry = `export { unpackDxt } from './web/src/gpu/dxt.ts'; export { dxt1ToAstc, dxt1HasPunch } from './web/src/gpu/astc.ts';`;
const js = (await esbuild.build({ stdin: { contents: entry, resolveDir: ROOT, loader: 'ts' }, bundle: true, format: 'esm', write: false, platform: 'neutral' })).outputFiles[0].text;
const { unpackDxt, dxt1ToAstc, dxt1HasPunch } = await import('data:text/javascript;base64,' + Buffer.from(js).toString('base64'));
const DXT1 = 0x31545844;

/** one ASTC block (16 bytes) as 16 RGBA texels, or a string saying what it is not */
function decode(b) {
  const bit = i => (b[i >> 3] >> (i & 7)) & 1;
  const bits = (pos, n) => { let v = 0; for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) v |= bit(pos + i) << i; return v; };
  const mode = bits(0, 11), dual = (mode & 0x400) !== 0, base = mode & 0x3FF;
  if (base !== 0x042 && base !== 0x051) return `block mode ${mode.toString(16)}`;
  if (bits(11, 2) !== 0) return 'more than one partition';
  const trits = base === 0x051, nw = dual ? 32 : 16, wbits = trits ? Math.ceil(nw * 8 / 5) : nw * 2;
  // the weights: bit i of their sequence at bit 127 - i
  const wbit = i => bit(127 - i), wread = (pos, n) => { let v = 0; for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) v |= wbit(pos + i) << i; return v; };
  const w = [];
  if (!trits) for (let i = 0; i < nw; i++) w.push([0, 21, 43, 64][wread(2 * i, 2)]);
  else {
    for (let g = 0, pos = 0; g < nw; g += 5) {
      const n = Math.min(5, nw - g), len = [0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8][n], T = wread(pos, len); pos += len;
      const t = (x, i, k = 1) => (x >> i) & ((1 << k) - 1);
      let C, t3, t4;
      if (t(T, 2, 3) === 7) { C = t(T, 5, 3) << 2 | t(T, 0, 2); t4 = 2; t3 = 2; }
      else { C = t(T, 0, 5); if (t(T, 5, 2) === 3) { t4 = 2; t3 = t(T, 7); } else { t4 = t(T, 7); t3 = t(T, 5, 2); } }
      let t0, t1, t2;
      if (t(C, 0, 2) === 3) { t2 = 2; t1 = t(C, 4); t0 = t(C, 3) << 1 | (t(C, 2) & ~t(C, 3) & 1); }
      else if (t(C, 2, 2) === 3) { t2 = 2; t1 = 2; t0 = t(C, 0, 2); }
      else { t2 = t(C, 4); t1 = t(C, 2, 2); t0 = t(C, 1) << 1 | (t(C, 0) & ~t(C, 1) & 1); }
      w.push(...[t0, t1, t2, t3, t4].slice(0, n).map(x => [0, 32, 64][x]));
    }
  }
  const cem = bits(13, 4);
  let e0, e1;
  if (cem === 8 && !dual) {
    const v = Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, i) => bits(17 + 8 * i, 8));
    if (v[1] + v[3] + v[5] < v[0] + v[2] + v[4]) return 'blue contraction';
    e0 = [v[0], v[2], v[4], 255]; e1 = [v[1], v[3], v[5], 255];
  } else if (cem === 12 && dual) {
    const v = Array.from({ length: 8 }, (_, i) => { const q = bits(17 + 7 * i, 7); return q << 1 | q >> 6; });
    if (v[1] + v[3] + v[5] < v[0] + v[2] + v[4]) return 'blue contraction';
    e0 = [v[0], v[2], v[4], v[6]]; e1 = [v[1], v[3], v[5], v[7]];
  } else return `endpoint mode ${cem}${dual ? ' with two planes' : ''}`;
  const ccs = dual ? bits(128 - wbits - 2, 2) : -1;
  const out = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < 16; i++) {
    const px = [0, 1, 2, 3].map(c => {
      const wt = dual ? w[2 * i + (c === ccs ? 1 : 0)] : w[i];
      const C = Math.floor((e0[c] * 257 * (64 - wt) + e1[c] * 257 * wt + 32) / 64);
      return Math.round(C / 65535 * 255);
    });
    out.push(px);
  }
  return out;
}

const block = (c0, c1, idx) => new Uint8Array([c0 & 255, c0 >> 8, c1 & 255, c1 >> 8, idx & 255, (idx >> 8) & 255, (idx >> 16) & 255, idx >>> 24]);
/** the largest colour difference between the rewritten block and the unpacked one, and whether the alphas match */
function compare(src) {
  const a = dxt1ToAstc(src, 0, 8, 1, 1), got = decode(a);
  if (typeof got === 'string') return { error: got };
  const u = unpackDxt(DXT1, src, 0, 8, 4, 4);
  let max = 0, alpha = true;
  for (let i = 0; i < 16; i++) {
    const want = [u[4 * i + 2], u[4 * i + 1], u[4 * i], u[4 * i + 3]];
    if (got[i][3] !== want[3]) alpha = false;
    if (want[3]) max = Math.max(max, ...[0, 1, 2].map(c => Math.abs(got[i][c] - want[c])));
  }
  return { max, alpha };
}

test('four colours: the endpoints exact, the thirds within 2', () => {
  // c0 = F800 (red), c1 = 001F (blue); first row codes 0 1 2 3
  const src = block(0xF800, 0x001F, 0xE4);
  const a = decode(dxt1ToAstc(src, 0, 8, 1, 1));
  assert.deepEqual(a[0], [255, 0, 0, 255]);
  assert.deepEqual(a[1], [0, 0, 255, 255]);
  assert.deepEqual(a.slice(2, 4), [[171, 0, 84, 255], [84, 0, 171, 255]]);   // BC1: 170/85
  assert.deepEqual(compare(src), { max: 1, alpha: true });
});

test('the endpoints swapped when the second is darker (no blue contraction)', () => {
  // c0 = FFFF (white) > c1 = 0000 (black): the decoder would contract a white second endpoint's blue
  assert.deepEqual(compare(block(0xFFFF, 0x0000, 0x1B)), { max: 1, alpha: true });
});

test('three colours without a hole: the midpoint exact', () => {
  const src = block(0x001F, 0xF800, 0x24);           // c0 < c1, codes 0 1 2 0 ...
  const a = decode(dxt1ToAstc(src, 0, 8, 1, 1));
  assert.deepEqual(a.slice(0, 3), [[0, 0, 255, 255], [255, 0, 0, 255], [128, 0, 128, 255]]);   // BC1: 127/127, rounded
  assert.equal(compare(src).alpha, true);
});

test('a transparent texel: two planes, alpha exact', () => {
  const src = block(0x001F, 0xF800, 0xE4);           // c0 < c1 and code 3 in the first row
  assert.equal(dxt1HasPunch(src, 0, 8, 1, 1), true);
  const punch = { blocks: 0 };
  const a = decode(dxt1ToAstc(src, 0, 8, 1, 1, undefined, punch));
  assert.equal(punch.blocks, 1);
  assert.equal(a[3][3], 0);
  assert.deepEqual(compare(src), { max: 1, alpha: true });
});

test('dxt1HasPunch: only code 3 in a three-colour block', () => {
  assert.equal(dxt1HasPunch(block(0xF800, 0x001F, 0xFFFFFFFF), 0, 8, 1, 1), false);   // four colours: code 3 is a colour
  assert.equal(dxt1HasPunch(block(0x001F, 0xF800, 0xAAAAAAAA), 0, 8, 1, 1), false);   // three colours, codes 2 only
  assert.equal(dxt1HasPunch(block(0x1234, 0x1234, 0xC0000000), 0, 8, 1, 1), true);    // one colour, code 3 at the last texel
  // a level of 2x2 blocks, pitch 24: the hole in the last block
  const lv = new Uint8Array(48);
  lv.set(block(0xF800, 0x001F, 0), 0); lv.set(block(0xF800, 0x001F, 0), 8);
  lv.set(block(0xF800, 0x001F, 0), 24); lv.set(block(0x001F, 0xF800, 3), 32);
  assert.equal(dxt1HasPunch(lv, 0, 24, 2, 2), true);
  assert.equal(dxt1HasPunch(lv, 0, 24, 2, 1), false);
});

test('random blocks of every kind, within the limits', () => {
  let seed = 7;
  const rnd = () => (seed = (Math.imul(seed, 1103515245) + 12345) >>> 0) >>> 8;
  const worst = { four: 0, three: 0, holes: 0 };
  for (let i = 0; i < 20000; i++) {
    let c0 = rnd() & 0xFFFF, c1 = i % 5 === 4 ? c0 : rnd() & 0xFFFF;
    if (i % 7 === 0) c0 = [0, 0xFFFF, 0xF800, 0x07E0, 0x001F][rnd() % 5];
    const idx = (rnd() << 8 ^ rnd()) >>> 0, src = block(c0, c1, idx);
    const r = compare(src);
    assert.ok(!r.error, `block ${i}: ${r.error}`);
    assert.ok(r.alpha, `block ${i}: alpha`);
    const k = c0 > c1 ? 'four' : dxt1HasPunch(src, 0, 8, 1, 1) ? 'holes' : 'three';
    worst[k] = Math.max(worst[k], r.max);
  }
  assert.ok(worst.four <= 2 && worst.three <= 1 && worst.holes <= 1, JSON.stringify(worst));
});

test('the layout: blocks in rows of a wider pitch, an offset, into a buffer kept', () => {
  // 3x2 blocks at offset 5, pitch 30 (6 bytes past the blocks in each row)
  const src = new Uint8Array(5 + 60);
  for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) src.set(block(0xF800 - i, 0x001F + i, 0x1B * i), 5 + Math.floor(i / 3) * 30 + (i % 3) * 8);
  const buf = new Uint8Array(200), out = dxt1ToAstc(src, 5, 30, 3, 2, buf);
  assert.equal(out.buffer, buf.buffer);
  assert.equal(out.length, 96);
  for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) {
    const one = dxt1ToAstc(block(0xF800 - i, 0x001F + i, 0x1B * i), 0, 8, 1, 1);
    assert.deepEqual(Array.from(out.subarray(i * 16, i * 16 + 16)), Array.from(one));
  }
  assert.notEqual(dxt1ToAstc(src, 5, 30, 3, 2, new Uint8Array(16)).buffer.byteLength, 16);
});

// The server's fixes for the security and privacy audit, one test per finding,
// against the real server (out/web/server-rs/nfsu2-server, web/tools/server-cmd.mjs):
//   node --test --test-concurrency=1 web/test/audit.test.mjs
// - F1:  ?vip= is ignored; a dropped player's address goes back only to its token (/lan?resume); a client that
//        opens /lan over and over gets 429; the console names no client address
// - F3:  one client behind a proxy gets at most 64 requests at once (429 above), one IPv6 /48 at most 128 however
//        many /56s it uses, the last quarter of the budget is only for clients that hold nothing, others are
//        not locked out, and a download the client stopped reading (or reads a trickle of) is let go
// - F4:  with --tls-cert, no certificate for a handshake without the server's name (SNI) or with another;
//        a Host that is not its name gets 421
// - F7, PRIV-4: a DNS-rebinding page (any other Host) gets 421 everywhere, the /lan upgrade included
// - PRIV-1: the game folder is served and listed only as far as it is the game (the real folder's installer
//        log, SAVE and mod scripts never)
// - DEP-1: the server starts and serves in every mode, reading no network interfaces (systemd without AF_NETLINK)
// - DEP-4: a client's refused upgrades cost the console two lines a minute, not one each
// - DEP-8: the state folder the server makes is private (0700), the files in it 0600
// Ports: NFSU2_TEST_AUDIT_PORT1 (8529), NFSU2_TEST_AUDIT_PORT2 (8629): not deploy.test.mjs's, so the two can

  : !fs.existsSync(path.join(REPO, 'out/web/nfsu2.wasm')) ? 'no out/web/nfsu2.wasm (web/build.sh)' : false;

async function startServer(args, { env = {}, state = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(TMP, 'state-')), expectExit = false } = {}) {
  const c = spawn(...serverCommand(['--data', DATA, '--state', state, ...args]), { stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'], env: { ...process.env, ...env } });
  let out = '';
  c.stdout.on('data', d => { out += d; }); c.stderr.on('data', d => { out += d; });
  const exited = new Promise(r => c.on('exit', code => r(code)));
  const ready = await new Promise(res => {
    const t = setTimeout(() => res(false), 20000);
    const check = () => { if (out.includes('  access    :')) { clearTimeout(t); setTimeout(() => res(true), 300); } };
    c.stdout.on('data', check);
    exited.then(() => { clearTimeout(t); res(false); });
  });
  if (expectExit === false && !ready) { c.kill(); throw new Error(`server did not start:\n${out}`); }
  return { c, state, ready, out: () => out, exited, stop: async () => { c.kill('SIGTERM'); await exited; } };
}
function request(port, { method = 'GET', p = '/', host = `localhost:${port}`, headers = {}, useTls = false, servername, timeout = 10000 } = {}) {
  // (a 101 answer leaves the connection open: the head is enough)
  return new Promise((res, rej) => {
    const sock = useTls ? tls.connect({ host: '127.0.0.1', port, servername, rejectUnauthorized: false }) : net.connect(port, '127.0.0.1');
    const chunks = [];
    const t = setTimeout(() => { sock.destroy(); res({ status: 0, timedOut: true }); }, timeout);
    sock.on(useTls ? 'secureConnect' : 'connect', () => sock.write(`${method} ${p} HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: ${host}\r\nConnection: close\r\n` +
      Object.entries(headers).map(([k, v]) => `${k}: ${v}\r\n`).join('') + '\r\n'));
    sock.on('data', d => { chunks.push(d); if (/^HTTP\/1\.1 101 /.test(String(chunks[0])) && Buffer.concat(chunks).includes('\r\n\r\n')) sock.destroy(); });
    sock.on('error', e => { clearTimeout(t); chunks.length ? done() : res({ status: 0, error: e.code ?? e.message }); });
    sock.on('close', () => { clearTimeout(t); done(); });
    const done = () => {
      const b = Buffer.concat(chunks), end = b.indexOf('\r\n\r\n');
      res({ status: +String(b.subarray(0, 12)).split(' ')[1] || 0, head: String(b.subarray(0, end)), body: b.subarray(end + 4) });
    };
  });
}
// a /lan client behind the proxy, as the client at address xff
function lanClient(port, xff, { q = '', hello = null, name = 'player' } = {}) {
  const ws = new WebSocket(`ws://127.0.0.1:${port}/lan${q}`, { headers: { Host: HOST, 'X-Forwarded-For': xff } });
  const c = { ws, ctl: [], frames: [], status: 0 };
  c.opened = new Promise(res => {
    ws.on('open', () => { if (hello) ws.send(JSON.stringify(hello)); res(true); });
    ws.on('unexpected-response', (q, r) => { c.status = r.statusCode; res(false); });
    ws.on('error', () => res(false));
  });
  c.welcome = new Promise(res => {
    ws.on('message', (d, bin) => {
      if (bin) { c.frames.push(Buffer.from(d)); return; }
      const m = JSON.parse(String(d)); c.ctl.push(m);
      if (m.t === 'welcome') { if (!hello) ws.send(JSON.stringify({ t: 'hello', name })); res(m); }
    });
    ws.on('close', () => res(null));
  });
  return c;
}

test('F1: ?vip= is ignored, a dropped player\'s address goes back only to its token; /lan opened too fast gets 429; no client address on the console', { skip: SKIP, timeout: 90_000 }, async () => {
  const s = await startServer(['--behind-proxy', '--http-port', String(P2)], { env: { NFSU2_HOST: HOST } });
  try {
    const alice = lanClient(P2, '198.51.100.1', { name: 'Alice' }), bob = lanClient(P2, '198.51.100.2', { name: 'Bob' });
    await alice.welcome; const wb = await bob.welcome;
    assert.match(wb.token ?? '', /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{22}$/, 'the welcome carries a token');
    bob.ws.terminate();
    await sleep(200);
    // Mallory asks for Bob's address every way it can: ?vip=, a resume with a made-up token, a plain join
    const tries = [lanClient(P2, '203.0.113.9', { q: `?vip=${wb.vipStr}` }),
      lanClient(P2, '203.0.113.9', { q: '?resume', hello: { t: 'hello', name: 'Bob', vip: wb.vipStr, token: 'B'.repeat(22) } }),
      lanClient(P2, '203.0.113.9')];
    const got = (await Promise.all(tries.map(t => t.welcome))).map(w => w?.vipStr);
    console.log(`Bob had ${wb.vipStr}; Mallory's tries got ${got.join(', ')}`);
    assert.ok(got.every(v => v && v !== wb.vipStr), 'never Bob\'s address');
    const bob2 = lanClient(P2, '198.51.100.22', { q: '?resume', hello: { t: 'hello', name: 'Bob', vip: wb.vipStr, token: wb.token } });
    assert.equal((await bob2.welcome)?.vipStr, wb.vipStr, 'Bob, with his token, from another address');
    for (const c of [alice, bob2, ...tries]) c.ws.terminate();
    // a client that opens and closes /lan as fast as it can: a burst, then 429 (the review of F1: churning)
    const codes = {};
    for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++) {
      const c = lanClient(P2, '203.0.113.50');
      const ok = await c.opened;
      codes[ok ? 101 : c.status] = (codes[ok ? 101 : c.status] ?? 0) + 1;
      c.ws.terminate();
    }
    const other = lanClient(P2, '203.0.113.51');
    const otherOk = await other.opened; other.ws.terminate();
    console.log(`40 /lan openings in a row from one client: ${JSON.stringify(codes)}; another client meanwhile: ${otherOk ? 101 : other.status}`);
    assert.ok(codes[429] >= 15 && codes[101] >= 15, 'a burst, then 429');
    assert.ok(otherOk, 'another client is not affected');
    await sleep(300);
    const lanLines = s.out().split('\n').filter(l => l.startsWith('[lan]'));
    assert.ok(lanLines.some(l => / is back /.test(l)) && lanLines.some(l => /too fast/.test(l)), lanLines.join('\n'));
    assert.deepEqual(lanLines.filter(l => /198\.51\.100|203\.0\.113/.test(l)), [], 'no client address on the console');
  } finally { await s.stop(); }
});

// the upstream side of a proxy: one connection per request, each for the client at xff(i), never read
const BIG = '/data/MOVIES/DragTut.vp6';
// (answers: 200 held, 429 refused, closed: the connection closed with no answer (a refusal that raced the
// close, past the port's maxConnections, or past the 128 a Mac queues for the server to accept), other: no answer
// in 20 s)
async function hold(port, n, xff, socks, p = BIG) {
  const answers = { 200: 0, 429: 0, closed: 0, other: 0 };
  await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => new Promise(res => {
    const so = net.connect(port, '127.0.0.1');
    socks.push(so);
    let done = false;
    const end = k => { if (done) return; done = true; clearTimeout(t); answers[k in answers ? k : 'other']++; res(); };
    const t = setTimeout(() => end('other'), 20000);
    so.on('error', () => {});
    so.once('connect', () => so.write(`GET ${p} HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: ${HOST}\r\nX-Forwarded-For: ${xff(i)}\r\n\r\n`));
    so.once('data', d => { so.pause(); end(+String(d).split(' ')[1]); });
    so.once('close', () => end('closed'));
  })));
  return answers;
}
// Requests in progress that hold nothing in the kernel: saves (PUT /vault) whose body never comes, each for the client
// at xff(i).  An unread download fills its socket buffers on both ends, about 1 MB on a Mac's loopback: the ~800 that
// F3 held at once took 0.9-1.0 GB of the kernel's network memory (netstat -m: some 60,000 requests for memory denied
// in each run), the server lost some of the held ones, so the fill fell short of 768, and other tests' connections
// failed meanwhile.  Saves hold the shares now, downloads only the few past the vault's own limit (60 writes from a
// client in a burst, 120 from a site).  "100 Continue" goes out just before the request reaches the budget (nfsu2_http
// conn.rs), a refusal right after it; a save with no answer past it holds its share until the server's request
// timeout (30 s).  (answers: held, 429 refused, other: anything else, or nothing in 20 s; first: the first other's
// status line)
// They connect 64 at a time, each wave once the last one was answered: a Mac queues at most 128 connections the server
// has not accepted yet (kern.ipc.somaxconn) and resets the rest, so 768 at once lost every one past 128 the moment
// the server's accept loop fell a little behind (on a busy machine the fill once got 677 of 768, the others closed
// without a byte; with the server stopped for 300 ms, 128).
async function holdSaves(port, n, xff, socks) {
  const save = i => new Promise(res => {
    const so = net.connect(port, '127.0.0.1');
    socks.push(so);
    let text = '';
    const t = setTimeout(() => res(() => text), 20000);
    so.on('error', () => {});
    so.once('connect', () => so.write(`PUT /vault HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: ${HOST}\r\nX-Forwarded-For: ${xff(i)}\r\n` +
      `Authorization: Bearer ${'A'.repeat(43)}\r\nIf-Match: "${'0'.repeat(15)}1"\r\nContent-Length: 1024\r\nExpect: 100-continue\r\n\r\n`));
    so.on('data', d => { text += d; clearTimeout(t); res(() => text); });
    so.once('close', () => { clearTimeout(t); res(() => text); });
  });
  const got = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i += 64) got.push(...await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: Math.min(64, n - i) }, (_, j) => save(i + j))));
  await sleep(500);
  const answers = { held: 0, 429: 0, other: 0 };
  for (const text of got.map(f => f())) {
    const after = text.replace(/^HTTP\/1\.1 100 Continue\r\n\r\n/, '');
    const k = text === after ? 'other' : after === '' ? 'held' : after.startsWith('HTTP/1.1 429 ') ? 429 : 'other';
    answers[k]++;
    if (k === 'other') answers.first ??= text.split('\r\n')[0] || '(nothing)';
  }
  return answers;
}
const xffOther = (port, ip) => request(port, { p: '/players', host: HOST, headers: { 'X-Forwarded-For': ip } });
test('F3: one client behind a proxy holds at most 64 requests at once, one IPv6 /48 at most 128; the last quarter is for newcomers', { skip: SKIP, timeout: 180_000 }, async () => {
  const s = await startServer(['--behind-proxy', '--http-port', String(P2)], { env: { NFSU2_HOST: HOST } });
  await sleep(1500);                                   // the module's compression at start
  let socks = [];
  const free = () => { for (const so of socks) so.destroy(); socks = []; return sleep(500); };
  try {
    const a0 = await holdSaves(P2, 60, () => '203.0.113.66', socks);
    const a = await hold(P2, 140, () => '203.0.113.66', socks);
    const other = await xffOther(P2, '198.51.100.7');
    console.log(`one client: 60 saves ${JSON.stringify(a0)}, then 140 downloads ${JSON.stringify(a)}; another client meanwhile: ${other.status}`);
    assert.equal(a0.other, 0, `every save held or refused (${a0.first})`);
    assert.ok(a0.held + a[200] <= 64, `at most 64 at once for one client (${a0.held} + ${a[200]})`);
    assert.ok(a0[429] + a[429] + a.closed >= 130, `the rest refused (${a0[429]} + ${a[429]} + ${a.closed})`);
    assert.equal(other.status, 200, 'another client is not locked out');
    await free();
    // the review of F3: one /48 spread over 17 /56s, 64 each (the /56 budgets alone gave it 16 x 64 = 1024)
    const xff6 = i => `2001:db8:77:${(i % 17).toString(16)}00::${(i >> 4) + 1}`;
    const v0 = await holdSaves(P2, 120, xff6, socks);
    const v6 = await hold(P2, 17 * 64 - 120, i => xff6(i + 120), socks);
    const other6 = await xffOther(P2, '2001:db8:99::1');
    console.log(`17 x 64 from one /48: 120 saves ${JSON.stringify(v0)}, then downloads ${JSON.stringify(v6)}; another /48 meanwhile: ${other6.status}`);
    assert.equal(v0.other, 0, `every save held or refused (${v0.first})`);
    assert.ok(v0.held + v6[200] <= 128, `at most 128 at once for one /48 (${v0.held} + ${v6[200]})`);
    assert.equal(other6.status, 200);
    await free();
    // the last quarter of the 1024: a client that already holds one, under its own budget, may not take it
    // (24 clients fill it with 32 saves each: under the vault's own limit of 60 writes per client in a burst)
    const early = await hold(P2, 1, () => '198.51.100.9', socks);
    const saves = await holdSaves(P2, 24 * 32, i => `192.0.2.${(i % 24) + 1}`, socks);
    const held = early[200] + saves.held;
    const late = await hold(P2, 10, () => '2001:db8:b0::1', socks);
    const holder = await hold(P2, 1, () => '198.51.100.9', socks);
    const newcomer = await xffOther(P2, '198.51.100.10');
    console.log(`held ${held} of 1024 (saves: ${JSON.stringify(saves)}); then a new /48 got ${JSON.stringify(late)}, a client that held one got ${JSON.stringify(holder)}, a newcomer ${newcomer.status}`);
    assert.ok(held >= 768, `filled up to the last quarter (${held})`);
    assert.equal(saves.other, 0, `every save held or refused (${saves.first})`);
    assert.equal(late[200], 1, 'a client that holds nothing gets one of the last quarter, then no more');
    assert.equal(holder[200], 0, 'one that holds some gets none of it');
    assert.equal(newcomer.status, 200, 'a newcomer is never locked out');
  } finally { await free(); await s.stop(); }
});

// The game's Save option set to Autosave once per profile before Play
// (web/src/app/profile.ts, settings.ini "autosave"):
//   node --test web/test/autosave.test.mjs
// - the profile checksum is CRC-32/BZIP2 of all but the last 4 bytes XOR those
//   4 bytes read big-endian, checked against zlib's CRC-32 on bit-reversed
//   bytes (an implementation of its own) and the CRC catalogue's check value
// - a profile is changed only when every check holds (size, header, the three
//   checksums, version, the name inside, Save bytes 0 or 1); the change is the
//   two Save bytes and the two checksums it moves, nothing else
// - each profile is set once: Autosave or Off stay, a Prompt chosen in the game
//   after the change stays, a file the checks refuse is left and looked at again
// - renaming a profile (profile.ts renameProfile) moves its folder, file and
//   cover shoots, changes the name inside and the two checksums it moves, and
//   nothing else; a refused rename, or one that fails halfway, leaves the saves as they were
// - deleting a profile (profile.ts deleteProfile, the Saves tab's bin) takes its folder and its cover shoots in any
//   case, and nothing of another profile: not one whose name starts with it, nor its covers
// - a first profile's name field starts with Your name's letters and digits (profile.ts newProfileName), never NAME,
//   Player or a slur; a profile of a name of up to 15 with spaces is renamed like any other
// The profiles here are synthetic (the layout of profile.ts's header comment).
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import path from 'node:path';
import zlib from 'node:zlib';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import * as esbuild from 'esbuild';

const ROOT = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '../..');
const entry = `export * as P from './web/src/app/profile.ts'; export * as S from './web/src/app/settings.ts';`;
const js = (await esbuild.build({ stdin: { contents: entry, resolveDir: ROOT, loader: 'ts' }, bundle: true, format: 'esm', write: false, platform: 'neutral' })).outputFiles[0].text;
const { P, S } = await import('data:text/javascript;base64,' + Buffer.from(js).toString('base64'));

const DIR = 'NFS Underground 2';
const rev8 = b => { let r = 0; for (let k = 0; k < 8; k++) r |= ((b >> k) & 1) << (7 - k); return r; };
const rev32 = x => { let r = 0; for (let k = 0; k < 32; k++) r = (r << 1) | ((x >>> k) & 1); return r >>> 0; };
/** CRC-32/BZIP2 (MSB first, init and xorout all ones) from zlib's reflected CRC-32 */
const bzip2 = d => rev32(zlib.crc32(Buffer.from([...d].map(rev8))));
const sum = d => d.length < 4 ? 0 : (bzip2(d.subarray(0, d.length - 4)) ^ Buffer.from(d.subarray(d.length - 4)).readUInt32BE(0)) >>> 0;

/** A profile file as the game writes one: Save bytes (autosave, prompt), the name inside, everything else filler. */
function profile(name, autosave = 0, prompt = 1, { inside = name, version = 0x10D } = {}) {
  const f = Buffer.alloc(54966);
  for (let i = 36; i < f.length; i++) f[i] = (i * 7 + 3) & 0xff;      // career, cars, options: not zero
  f.write('20CM', 0, 'latin1');
  f.writeUInt32LE(54966, 4); f.writeUInt32LE(8, 8); f.writeUInt32LE(54930, 12);
  f.writeUInt32LE(version, 28); f.writeUInt32LE(54930, 32);
  f.fill(0, 36 + 53761, 36 + 53761 + 32); f.write(inside, 36 + 53761, 'latin1');
  f[36 + 50987] = autosave; f[36 + 50988] = prompt;
  return seal(f);
}
function seal(f) {
  f.writeUInt32LE(sum(f.subarray(28, 36)), 16); f.writeUInt32LE(sum(f.subarray(36)), 20); f.writeUInt32LE(sum(f.subarray(0, 24)), 24);
  return new Uint8Array(f.buffer, f.byteOffset, f.length);
}
const mode = (f, name) => P.readSaveMode(f, name);

test('checksum: CRC-32/BZIP2 but the last 4 bytes, XOR them (the catalogue check value, zlib)', () => {
  assert.equal(P.checksum(Buffer.from('123456789\0\0\0\0')), 0xFC891918);
  assert.equal(P.checksum(Buffer.from('abc')), 0);
  for (let n = 4; n < 600; n += 7) {
    const d = Buffer.alloc(n); for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) d[i] = (i * 131 + n * 7) & 0xff;
    assert.equal(P.checksum(d), sum(d), `${n} bytes`);
  }
  const a = Buffer.alloc(8); a.writeUInt32LE(0x10D, 0); a.writeUInt32LE(54930, 4);
  assert.equal(P.checksum(a), 0xF287C0BB, 'block A of every profile');
});

test('the Save option of a profile the checks accept', () => {
  assert.deepEqual(mode(profile('TOBI', 0, 1), 'TOBI'), { mode: 'prompt' });
  assert.deepEqual(mode(profile('TOBI', 1, 1), 'TOBI'), { mode: 'autosave' });
  assert.deepEqual(mode(profile('TOBI', 1, 0), 'TOBI'), { mode: 'autosave' });
  assert.deepEqual(mode(profile('TOBI', 0, 0), 'TOBI'), { mode: 'off' });
  assert.deepEqual(mode(profile('Tobi', 0, 1), 'TOBI'), { mode: 'prompt' }, 'the name in any case');

test('a file the checks refuse is never changed', () => {
  const bad = (f, name = 'TOBI') => { const r = mode(f, name); assert.ok('bad' in r, JSON.stringify(r)); return r.bad; };
  const good = profile('TOBI');
  assert.match(bad(good.subarray(0, 54965)), /54965 bytes/);
  const magic = Buffer.from(good); magic[0] = 0x33; assert.match(bad(seal(magic)), /20CM/);
  const edited = Buffer.from(good); edited[100] ^= 1; assert.match(bad(edited), /checksums/);    // a save editor's money change
  const head = Buffer.from(good); head[24] ^= 1; assert.match(bad(head), /checksums/);
  assert.match(bad(profile('TOBI', 0, 1, { version: 0x10C })), /version/);
  assert.match(bad(good, 'OTHER'), /name inside/);
  assert.match(bad(profile('TOBI', 2, 1)), /Save bytes/);
  assert.match(bad(profile('TOBI', 0, 255)), /Save bytes/);
});

test('withAutosave changes the two Save bytes and the checksums they move, nothing else', () => {
  const f = profile('TOBI', 0, 1), g = P.withAutosave(f);
  assert.deepEqual(mode(g, 'TOBI'), { mode: 'autosave' });
  const changed = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < f.length; i++) if (f[i] !== g[i]) changed.push(i);
  assert.ok(changed.every(i => (i >= 20 && i < 28) || i === 36 + 50987), `changed bytes ${changed}`);
  assert.equal(g[36 + 50987], 1); assert.equal(g[36 + 50988], 1);
  const b = Buffer.from(g);
  assert.equal(b.readUInt32LE(20), sum(b.subarray(36))); assert.equal(b.readUInt32LE(24), sum(b.subarray(0, 24)));
  assert.equal(b.readUInt32LE(16), sum(b.subarray(28, 36)));
  assert.equal(f[36 + 50987], 0, 'the original is not touched');
});

/** the save folder in memory, as savefs.ts filesOf gives it */
function folder(files) {
  const m = new Map(Object.entries(files));
  const writes = [];
  return {
    m, writes,
    listFiles: async () => [...m.keys()].sort().map(p => ({ path: p })),
    readBytes: async p => { if (!m.has(p)) throw new Error(`no ${p}`); const v = m.get(p); return typeof v === 'string' ? new TextEncoder().encode(v) : v; },
    readText: async p => { const v = m.get(p); return v === undefined ? null : typeof v === 'string' ? v : new TextDecoder().decode(v); },
    writeFile: async (p, d) => { writes.push(p); m.set(p, d); },
    remove: async p => { writes.push(`-${p}`); for (const k of [...m.keys()]) if (k === p || k.startsWith(p + '/')) m.delete(k); },
  };
}
const at = n => `${DIR}/${n}/${n}`;

test('each profile is set once, and a choice made in the game afterwards stays', async () => {
  const corrupt = Buffer.from(profile('BROKEN')); corrupt[500] ^= 0xff;
  const fs = folder({
    [at('TOBI')]: profile('TOBI', 0, 1), [at('OFFP')]: profile('OFFP', 0, 0), [at('AUTO')]: profile('AUTO', 1, 1),
    [at('BROKEN')]: corrupt, 'registry.txt': 'NotFirstTime=1\n', [`${DIR}/TOBI/notes.txt`]: 'x', [`${DIR}/EMPTY/other`]: 'y',
  });
  const r1 = await P.turnOnAutosave(fs, DIR);
  assert.deepEqual(r1.turnedOn, ['TOBI']);
  assert.deepEqual(mode(fs.m.get(at('TOBI')), 'TOBI'), { mode: 'autosave' });
  assert.deepEqual(mode(fs.m.get(at('OFFP')), 'OFFP'), { mode: 'off' }, 'Off is a choice: left');
  assert.equal(fs.m.get(at('BROKEN')), corrupt, 'a refused file is not written');
  assert.ok(r1.notes.some(n => /^BROKEN left as it is: .*checksums/.test(n)), r1.notes.join('\n'));
  assert.deepEqual(fs.writes.sort(), [P.AUTOSAVE_SEEN, at('TOBI')].sort());
  const seen = () => fs.m.get(P.AUTOSAVE_SEEN).split('\n').filter(l => l && !l.startsWith('#'));
  assert.deepEqual(seen(), ['AUTO', 'OFFP', 'TOBI'], 'BROKEN is looked at again next time');

  // the player picks Prompt in the game: the game writes the profile with prompt, and it stays so
  fs.m.set(at('TOBI'), profile('TOBI', 0, 1));
  fs.writes.length = 0;
  const r2 = await P.turnOnAutosave(fs, DIR);
  assert.deepEqual(r2.turnedOn, []);
  assert.deepEqual(fs.writes, [], 'nothing changed, nothing written');
  assert.deepEqual(mode(fs.m.get(at('TOBI')), 'TOBI'), { mode: 'prompt' });

  // BROKEN saved again by the game (its checksums hold now), OFFP deleted, a new TOBI after a delete
  fs.m.set(at('BROKEN'), profile('BROKEN', 0, 1));
  fs.m.delete(at('OFFP'));
  const r3 = await P.turnOnAutosave(fs, DIR);
  assert.deepEqual(r3.turnedOn, ['BROKEN']);
  assert.deepEqual(seen(), ['AUTO', 'BROKEN', 'TOBI']);
  fs.m.delete(at('TOBI'));
  await P.turnOnAutosave(fs, DIR);
  fs.m.set(at('TOBI'), profile('TOBI', 0, 1));
  assert.deepEqual((await P.turnOnAutosave(fs, DIR)).turnedOn, ['TOBI'], 'a new profile of a deleted one\'s name');
});

test('a rename moves the profile, its cover shoots and its autosave line, and changes the name inside', async () => {
  const dvd = cover(), mag = cover();
  const fs = folder({
    [at('TOBI')]: profile('TOBI', 0, 0), [`${DIR}/TOBI/notes.txt`]: 'x', [`${DIR}/TOBI DVD 1/TOBI DVD 1`]: dvd,
    [`${DIR}/TOBI Magazine 12/TOBI Magazine 12`]: mag, [at('AUTO')]: profile('AUTO', 1, 1), [`${DIR}/AUTO DVD 1/AUTO DVD 1`]: cover(),
    [P.AUTOSAVE_SEEN]: '# head\nAUTO\nTOBI\nTOBIAS\n', 'registry.txt': 'r',
  });
  const before = new Map(fs.m);
  assert.deepEqual(await P.renameProfile(fs, DIR, 'TOBI', 'Bob7'), { files: 4 });
  const f = before.get(at('TOBI')), g = fs.m.get(at('Bob7'));
  assert.deepEqual(mode(g, 'Bob7'), { mode: 'off' }, 'the checks hold under the new name, the Save option as it was');
  assert.equal(name(g), 'Bob7');
  const changed = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < f.length; i++) if (f[i] !== g[i]) changed.push(i);
  assert.ok(changed.every(i => (i >= 20 && i < 28) || (i >= 36 + 53761 && i < 36 + 53761 + 32)), `changed bytes ${changed}`);
  assert.equal(new TextDecoder().decode(fs.m.get(`${DIR}/Bob7/notes.txt`)), 'x');
  assert.equal(fs.m.get(`${DIR}/Bob7 DVD 1/Bob7 DVD 1`), dvd);
  assert.equal(fs.m.get(`${DIR}/Bob7 Magazine 12/Bob7 Magazine 12`), mag);
  assert.equal(fs.m.get(P.AUTOSAVE_SEEN), '# head\nAUTO\nBob7\nTOBIAS\n');
  assert.ok(![...fs.m.keys()].some(k => k.startsWith(`${DIR}/TOBI`)), [...fs.m.keys()].join('\n'));
  for (const k of [at('AUTO'), `${DIR}/AUTO DVD 1/AUTO DVD 1`, 'registry.txt']) assert.equal(fs.m.get(k), before.get(k), `${k} untouched`);
  assert.equal(fs.writes.findIndex(w => w.startsWith('-')), fs.writes.length - 3, 'the old folders go last');
});

test('a delete takes the profile and its cover shoots, any case, and nothing else', async () => {
  const fs = folder({
    [at('TOBI')]: profile('TOBI'), [`${DIR}/TOBI/notes.txt`]: 'x', [`${DIR}/TOBI DVD 1/TOBI DVD 1`]: cover(),
    [`${DIR}/tobi Magazine 12/tobi Magazine 12`]: cover(),

    [at('Big Bad Wolf')]: profile('Big Bad Wolf'), [`${DIR}/Big Bad Wolf DVD 2/Big Bad Wolf DVD 2`]: cover(),

test('a profile the game named with stale heap bytes gets a name again', async () => {
  // a failed cover shoot's save before runtime/overrides.c sub_004e8b70: 32 bytes of heap addresses, no NUL; the game's
  // folder takes 31 of them, read as UTF-8 by the I/O worker (U+FFFD for the bytes that are not)
  const stale = Buffer.from('a09c1d25f846232520d8252528d82525c4501e2530d82525cc501e25a89c1d25', 'hex');
  const dir = new TextDecoder().decode(stale.subarray(0, 31));
  assert.ok(dir.includes(String.fromCharCode(0xfffd)) && !dir.endsWith('%'));
  const f = profile('X', 1, 1, { inside: stale.toString('latin1') });
  assert.deepEqual(mode(f, dir), { mode: 'autosave' });
  assert.match(mode(f, new TextDecoder().decode(stale)).bad ?? '', /name inside/, 'all 32 bytes: not the game\'s folder');
  const fs = folder({ [at(dir)]: f, [at('OTHER')]: profile('OTHER') });
  assert.deepEqual(await P.renameProfile(fs, DIR, dir, 'NAME2'), { files: 1 });
  assert.deepEqual([...fs.m.keys()].sort(), [at('NAME2'), at('OTHER')]);
  const g = fs.m.get(at('NAME2'));
  assert.equal(name(g), 'NAME2');
  assert.ok(g.subarray(36 + 53766, 36 + 53761 + 32).every(b => b === 0), 'NUL-padded');
  assert.deepEqual(mode(g, 'NAME2'), { mode: 'autosave' });
});

  // the box starts with D6 8B 89 (LANGPACKS/chinese's NAME), the field keeps what is typed after it; the I/O worker
  // makes the folder of the path's UTF-8 (U+058B, U+FFFD)

  assert.deepEqual(mode(fs.m.get(at('KEI2')), 'KEI2'), { mode: 'prompt' });

test('a refused rename writes nothing', async () => {
  const corrupt = Buffer.from(profile('BROKEN')); corrupt[500] ^= 0xff;
  const files = { [at('TOBI')]: profile('TOBI'), [at('AUTO')]: profile('AUTO'), [at('BROKEN')]: corrupt, [`${DIR}/NEW DVD 2/NEW DVD 2`]: cover() };
  const refused = async (from, to, re) => {
    const fs = folder(files);
    const r = await P.renameProfile(fs, DIR, from, to);
    assert.match(r.refused ?? '', re, `${from} -> ${to}: ${JSON.stringify(r)}`);
    assert.deepEqual(fs.writes, []);
  };
  for (const bad of ['', 'ABCDEFGH', 'A B', 'A-B', 'Thé', 'A/B', '..', 'Big Bad Wolf', 'Bob DVD 1']) await refused('TOBI', bad, /1 to 7 letters and digits/);
  await refused('TOBI', 'auto', /There is a profile AUTO already/);
  await refused('TOBI', 'new', /cover shoot NEW DVD 2/);
  await refused('BROKEN', 'FIXED', /BROKEN cannot be renamed here: its checksums/);
  await refused('NOBODY', 'X', /no profile NOBODY/);
  assert.deepEqual(await P.renameProfile(folder(files), DIR, 'TOBI', 'TOBI'), { files: 0 });
});

test('a rename that fails halfway leaves the profile as it was', async () => {
  for (const [from, to] of [['TOBI', 'BOB'], ['Big Bad Wolf', 'TOBI'], ['Big Bad Wolf', 'BIGBAD']])
    for (const failAt of [1, 2, 3]) {
      const fs = folder({ [at(from)]: profile(from), [`${DIR}/${from} DVD 1/${from} DVD 1`]: cover(), [`${DIR}/${from}/GARAGE.DAT`]: 'g' });
      const before = new Map(fs.m);
      const write = fs.writeFile;
      let n = 0;
      fs.writeFile = async (p, d) => { if (++n === failAt) throw new Error('disk full'); return write(p, d); };
      await assert.rejects(P.renameProfile(fs, DIR, from, to), /disk full/, `${from} -> ${to}, write ${failAt}`);
      assert.deepEqual([...fs.m.keys()].sort(), [...before.keys()].sort(), `${from} -> ${to}, write ${failAt}`);
      for (const [k, v] of before) assert.equal(fs.m.get(k), v);
    }
});

// The app's away check (web/src/app/away.ts) on a fake clock: no input for a while gets a warning and then the
// place on the server goes back; a tab in the background gives it back without one; input brings it back.
//   node --test web/test/away.test.mjs
import { test, mock } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import * as esbuild from 'esbuild';
import { sourceKeys } from '../tools/i18n-keys.mjs';

const ROOT = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '../..');
const js = (await esbuild.build({ entryPoints: [path.join(ROOT, 'web/src/app/away.ts')], bundle: true, format: 'esm', write: false })).outputFiles[0].text;
const { AwayCheck } = await import('data:text/javascript;base64,' + Buffer.from(js).toString('base64'));
// the two texts as away.ts writes them (the English is the key the page translates), so new wording needs no change
// here: the warning counts down in {n}, the other is for when the place went back
const TEXTS = sourceKeys(fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, 'web/src/app/away.ts'), 'utf8')).keys.map(k => k.key);
const WARN = TEXTS.find(k => k.includes('{n}')), AWAY = TEXTS.find(k => !k.includes('{n}'));
assert.ok(TEXTS.length === 2 && WARN && AWAY, `away.ts's texts: ${JSON.stringify(TEXTS)}`);
const warn = n => WARN.replace('{n}', String(n));
const isWarn = s => !!s && s.startsWith(WARN.slice(0, WARN.indexOf('{n}')));

const L = { inputMs: 20 * 60_000, hiddenMs: 10 * 60_000, warnMs: 60_000 };
const MIN = 60_000;

// the page: a clock, a document that may be hidden, the game's input and network as the app sees them
function setup({ holding = true, input = true } = {}) {
  mock.timers.enable({ apis: ['setInterval'] });
  let t = 1000;
  Object.defineProperty(globalThis, 'performance', { value: { now: () => t }, configurable: true });
  const vis = new Set();
  globalThis.document = { hidden: false, addEventListener: (k, f) => vis.add(f), removeEventListener: (k, f) => vis.delete(f) };
  const g = { last: t, holding, calls: [], shown: [], logs: [] };
  const s = {
    input: { lastInput: () => (input ? g.last : null) },
    net: { holding: () => g.holding, away: on => { g.calls.push(on); g.holding = !on && g.holding; } },
  };
  const check = new AwayCheck(s, L, text => g.shown.push(text), l => g.logs.push(l));
  const tick = ms => { for (let k = 0; k < ms; k += 1000) { t += 1000; mock.timers.tick(1000); } };
  const use = () => { g.last = t; };
  const hide = on => { globalThis.document.hidden = on; for (const f of vis) f(); };
  return { g, check, tick, use, hide, now: () => t };
}
const done = (x) => { x.check.stop(); mock.timers.reset(); };

test('no input for 20 min: a warning that counts down 60 s, then the place goes back; input brings it back', () => {
  const x = setup();
  try {
    x.tick(20 * MIN - 1000);
    assert.deepEqual(x.g.shown, [], 'nothing before 20 min');
    x.tick(1000);
    assert.equal(x.g.shown.at(-1), warn(60));
    x.tick(30_000);
    assert.equal(x.g.shown.at(-1), warn(30));
    assert.deepEqual(x.g.calls, []);
    x.tick(30_000);
    assert.deepEqual(x.g.calls, [true], 'the place went back');
    assert.equal(x.g.shown.at(-1), AWAY);
    x.tick(10 * MIN);
    assert.deepEqual(x.g.calls, [true], 'once');
    x.use(); x.tick(1000);
    assert.deepEqual(x.g.calls, [true, false], 'back');
    assert.equal(x.g.shown.at(-1), null, 'the message is gone');
    assert.ok(x.g.logs.some(l => /no input for 21 min/.test(l)));
  } finally { done(x); }
});

test('input during the warning: it goes and the place stays', () => {
  const x = setup();
  try {
    x.tick(20 * MIN + 10_000);
    assert.ok(isWarn(x.g.shown.at(-1)), 'the warning');
    x.use(); x.tick(1000);
    assert.equal(x.g.shown.at(-1), null);
    x.tick(5 * MIN);
    assert.deepEqual(x.g.calls, []);
    x.tick(15 * MIN);                        // 20 min after that input: the warning again
    assert.ok(isWarn(x.g.shown.at(-1)), 'the warning');
  } finally { done(x); }
});

test('a tab in the background for 10 min: the place goes back at once, no warning first', () => {
  const x = setup();
  try {
    x.tick(5 * MIN); x.use();
    x.hide(true);
    x.tick(10 * MIN - 1000);
    assert.deepEqual(x.g.calls, []);
    x.tick(1000);
    assert.deepEqual(x.g.calls, [true]);
    assert.ok(!x.g.shown.some(isWarn), 'no warning');
    assert.equal(x.g.shown.at(-1), AWAY, 'the message for when they come back');
    x.hide(false); x.tick(5000);
    assert.deepEqual(x.g.calls, [true], 'seeing the tab again is not input');
    x.use(); x.tick(1000);
    assert.deepEqual(x.g.calls, [true, false]);

/** the page with main.js as `main` ('blocked', 'empty' or 'started'), in `language` when one is given */
async function open(main, language) {
  const p = await browser.newPage();
  await p.clock.install();
  if (language) await p.addInitScript(l => localStorage.setItem('nfsu2-page-language', l), language);
  await p.route(`${SITE}/**`, r => {
    const at = new URL(r.request().url()).pathname;

    return r.fulfill({ status: 404, body: '' });
  });
  await p.goto(`${SITE}/`);
  return p;

{"id": "AT001876", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/web/test/cf-sim.mjs", "originalBytes": 6361, "originalSha256": "d261f616007cf0e7cd79ad0d8aa95f3004dedc149e61aaabcfc965cb0b4b0f65", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 6361, "utf8TotalBytes": 6361}
